<header>The Second Book of the Great [Surgery]</header>

<margin>A</margin>

# Instruction on the Foundation of Open Sores,
## as they are newly described here, and shown to be different
### than what has been presented since antiquity.

**I**t is audacious enough to introduce a novelty and reject the old ways. But if justice is on our side, why should it not happen? For a custom is not an art; rather, an art is that which proves itself through its works. Now, an objection might be raised against this, such as: if no injury has ever been healed without me, or recognized without me, did everything stand still until my time? Is the medicine only within me and no one else? To this, my answer should also be heard. Regarding the origin, it is true: no one has ever described the foundation, origin, and source of <term>open sores <note>original: "Offenen Schäden"; generally referring to ulcers, chronic wounds, or syphilitic lesions that refuse to close.</note></term>. And that this is so—as they have written it—is publicly evident.

Furthermore, on the other hand, sores have indeed been healed, but ten times more have been ruined willfully and shamefully against the power of art, due to the deficiencies of the same. I write so that such things do not happen and will not happen. Now, I see perhaps one in ten being healed, while the other nine are ruined, and those ten are left hanging; who then deserves the praise?

<margin>B</margin>
Furthermore, they speak of an origin. But if it were as they claim, then their own origin would be contrary to their recipes, and the recipes and their described origin do not agree. For when all their recipes are read, there is only <term>Mercury <note>original: "Mercurius"; a heavy metal used extensively (and often transitionally) for treating skin diseases and syphilis.</note></term>, gold, or litharge, alum, vitriol, minium, verdigris, turpentine, resin, gum, and the like. Now look, and examine yourself closely: where does Mercury have the power to affect <term>yellow bile <note>original: "Cholera"; one of the four humors in ancient medicine.</note></term>, <term>phlegm <note>original: "Phlegma."</note></term>, <term>black bile <note>original: "Melancholia."</note></term>, or blood, that it might serve you so well there? Likewise for verdigris, alum, minium, and others. Now see how that rhymes: if you purge the yellow bile, whom have you helped thereby? Or what rhubarb has ever healed a sore? What elder bark, what <term>clyster <note>original: "Cristier sack"; an enema used to purge the bowels.</note></term> bag, what syrup? How can you then say that such origins create the open sores, when you can help no one with those same canons and rules, nor know how to help? You purge based on a "foundation" and yet do not know it; you administer an enema and do not hit the mark; you take away that which exits the backside and leave lying that which goes to the hole and creates the hole.

Tell me now, where is the origin of the open sores, and prove it according to the facts. If you say, "It is in the liver," why then does it not make the hole in the liver? Or in the spleen, why under the knee, or on the buttock? And why nowhere else so precisely as exactly where it chooses to be? How does it become so mild right there—your yellow bile, your phlegm, your blood, and your black bile? If it is a "flow from the head," why does it not act in the head? Since it is exactly there, where does it get its sharpness to become a hole? Because your books "bellow" it so, therefore it must be so? And because you teach it at the <term>High Schools <note>original: "Hohen Schulen"; referring to the universities of the time.</note></term>, therefore it must be correct? Oh, woe! It should not be so. Where do you have testimony that it is so, such that it must be believed and the foundation placed upon the books? If it is so, and there is no other foundation, why then do you not help the sick with it? Why do you ruin them? And further: Why do you not speak your own recipes from your own foundation? All the recipes you have against open sores, you have borrowed from old wives, some begged for, some learned from peasants—from people who know nothing of your "canons."

<margin>C</margin>
It would be good and fair, if you indeed knew and tasted the foundation so well, that you would provide your own recipes, and not help yourselves with those that go against your canons. Therefore, if your foundation were righteous, it would also be fair to create recipes from them, which you neither like to do nor can do. For see what I tell you here: You shout much about your books and libraries, which are well-polished. Now see: All your art is "wood," is wooden; and if the "wood" were not there, where would the Doctor be? So also, if Mercury were not there, who would be a Doctor now? A Doctor would be as rare as a blue donkey.

If your art consists only of these two pieces, even if you were to stand among the best—to say nothing of the lesser arts—why then do you need so many books? What good are they all to you? But <term>Doctor Brandt <note>A reference to Sebastian Brant (1457–1521), author of the famous satirical work *The Ship of Fools* (*Das Narrenschiff*).</note></term> has often reminded me of your library, for he thinks of it faithfully as he sails to <term>Narragonia <note>The fictional "Land of Fools" from Brant's *Ship of Fools*.</note></term>. It is indeed mocking and laughable that in so many books, the art is nothing more than "wood" and Mercury, and nothing else; that these two must ruin so many "rags" <note>likely referring to the patients or their bandages</note>, when a small <term>pamphlet <note>original: "Scartecklin"; a small, cheap book or folder.</note></term> could conclude it all.

# The Second Book of the Great
## Surgery / of the Founded and Proven Physician of both / Medicines DOCTOR PARACELSUS: Speaks of all the / Origin, Derivation, Signs, and Nature of the Open Sores of the entire / Body. Written to the Most Powerful, etc.

### The First Treatise indicates / how the first physicians handled Open Sores, / both the righteous and the unrighteous / physicians, and that with the arts and medicines.

### CHAPTER I.

<margin>B</margin>

### How after long trials of surgery in open / sores / no help was found, [and] how it further / proceeded.

**W**hen surgery was first discovered, and after that the <term>Open Sores <note>original: "Offnen Schäden"; chronic ulcers or wounds that fail to heal.</note></term> arose, the medicine for wounds was also used for these open sores. Sometimes this succeeded well, sometimes poorly—particularly the <term>wound-potions <note>herbal drinks intended to heal from within</note></term>, wound-salves, and wound-oils. But the use of plasters was found to be more beneficial; from this, it arose that plasters took precedence in medical treatment. Now, the origin of these Open Sores remained unknown—from whence they came, or what they were. For in medicine, the "foundation" was always lacking, so that it never followed the right course like other arts of mechanical practice. In those crafts, one always grasped the right trail, as is proven in all trades and arts. 

But in medicine, no man ever had such diligent and earnest pursuit as in the other arts; instead, men were negligent and unwilling in it. They felt a distaste for the sick and kept themselves among the healthy, pursuing harps, pipes, and singing, and thus forgot the love for their neighbor. They did not consider that a man is duty-bound to be helpful not to himself alone, but also to his neighbor as to himself. And thus, a healthy man is forced—according to the content of the Commandment—to work for the sick, and to seek ways and paths so that the sick might be helped. But he who gave and created nature and the Commandment is the teacher; He says: "Seek, and you shall find." <note>A reference to Matthew 7:7.</note> He points us to Himself, so that we should learn from Him, for He is gentle and of a humble heart. Therefore, the healthy man should not despair; 

<margin>C</margin> 

if he applies earnest diligence in love for his neighbor, no art will be withheld from him; nothing in nature will be so secret that it shall not be revealed to him. But medicine has always been the least esteemed among all the arts, except for what was driven by great necessity; otherwise, people always left the one who had fallen lying in the ditch. 

Now, however, the conscience of love appeared in some, who out of mercy for the sick labored to obtain health. They took an example from the dogs who licked the open sores of the sick. Based on this, they considered finding health to be the greatest good. They abandoned <term>Music <note>original: "Musica"; here representing leisure or academic distraction.</note></term> and the "dealings of the eyes" <note>likely referring to visual arts or superficial observation</note>. They labored so much in medicine that they found there must be something sharper and stronger through which the sores might be healed. They found through experience that there is not just one kind of Open Sore, but many; for every kind, there is a specific, corresponding medicine. 

Because of the resistance of the sores, they countered the rot and stench with salt-water; for some, they dried out the moisture with <term>iron dross <note>original: "Schmidzinder"; the scales or sparks from a blacksmith's forge, used for their drying and astringent properties.</note></term>, and many such little arts. Later, they also came upon <term>Celandine <note>original: "Schölkraut"</note></term>, oak leaves, <term>Skull-moss <note>original: "Todtenmieß"; a lichen found on skulls, once prized in pharmacopeias.</note></term>, and many more. Afterwards, they used resin, <term>Gloriet <note>a type of high-grade resin or turpentine</note></term>, and the like. But nowhere was anything perfect found, no matter how many things were tried. 

Afterwards, the <term>Sophists <note>Paracelsus's derogatory term for traditional academic physicians who relied on logic rather than experience.</note></term> arose, and their clever fantasies intruded. They pushed the common man away from seeking medicine and brought forth their tricky chatter, presenting a fictional origin and derivation for medicine. Yet their hearts were set on the "foundation" of driving great pride, promoting their own profit, and satisfying their pomp. God withdrew His teaching from them and let them build upon the sand, whereon they still stand. Upon this sand, their building will be overturned by the next wind—that is to say, their medicine has no powerful effect or strength. 

But regardless of their chatter, the sick did not despise the seeking of the common man, and they always sought help from the simple folk. Through these simple people, God allowed great art to come to light, which was always laughed at by the <term>Pharisaic doctors <note>doctors who, like the biblical Pharisees, were seen as obsessed with rules and status over true healing.</note></term>. And just as they have done, they also tried to destroy these arts, so that their "roast on the spit" <note>original: "Zutitkrey am Spieß"; a metaphor for their livelihood or "gravy train."</note> would not burn.

<summary>Paracelsus argues that true medical knowledge comes from God through love of neighbor and observation of nature, rather than through the "sophistry" and pride of academic physicians. He lists early empirical attempts at curing sores using minerals and herbs, contrasting these with the ineffective "chatter" of the medical establishment.</summary>

<margin>A</margin>

# CHAPTER II.

->*How the patients with Open Sores, because of their great pain, turned to the practitioners, who gave them guidance for the further discovery of medicines.*<-

Thus has Nature itself, through its great pain, presented its grievance to those who deal with such matters; and this occurred in such a way that it was believed "evil must be overcome with evil," and "wrath overcome with wrath" <note>This refers to the ancient medical philosophy of *Allopathy* (treating with opposites) or sometimes a crude version of *Homeopathy* (like cures like), which Paracelsus often critiqued or refined.</note>. From this it followed that since such pain existed within the sores, men undertook to drive it out with even greater pain. Thus, substances were selected and sought out that caused pain, such as salt, <term>vitriol <note>original: "Kupfferwasser"; historically referred to copper or iron sulfates used as astringents or corrosives.</note></term>, lye, and other similar things; also from herbs, such as <term>celandine <note>original: "Schölkraut"</note></term>, radish, and others of their kind. Such things, however, were unable to produce anything fruitful, except in common, simple sores, where they provided some mitigation and delay. 

Afterward, it was undertaken to strike these sores away through cutting; but to remove the "root" by cutting proved impossible. Instead, it was found to be a gross folly and lack of understanding, which should by no means be permitted in medicine. Following that same fantasy, the practice of <term>cautery <note>original: "Brennens"; the practice of burning tissue with hot metal or chemicals.</note></term> arose, and thus many types were attempted using glowing metals—gold, silver, iron—and also with molten lead and tin poured into the wounds, which even occurred in my own time. But in none of these were works of art discovered, only great folly—though occasionally, after long martyrdom, Nature improved itself. It also frequently happened that hot <term>mercury <note>original: "Mercurius"</note></term> was poured in as far as the sores reached, in which the most help was perceived. However, such terrible trembling of the limbs and so many great toothaches <note>A classic symptom of mercury poisoning, which causes gum disease and tooth loss.</note> grew out of this that the "art" could no longer be tolerated.

<margin>B</margin>

Thus, men were inclined to use that which caused greater pain than the open sores had in themselves, hoping that through the greater pain, the lesser would be driven out and healed. And so medicine was led astray for a long time with such undertakings, without considering whether it must be so or not. For if one wishes to speak fundamentally in medicine, then mark this point which I set before you: the healing of diseases is not established on the foundation of "driving out evil with evil" or "pain with pain," but rather consider that wrath should be overcome with goodness and mildness. 

For there are two foundations to be understood in medicine: "evil with worse" and "evil with good." It is no less true that wrath overcomes wrath, and strength overcomes strength. But how it fares for the "wrath" that is driven out is not pleasant. For if the greater wrath is to drive out the smaller, it usually results in a bloody skin. Likewise, if strength is to be mastered by a greater strength, it usually results in a "fist to the mouth." Thus, if an open sore, which is evil, is to be driven out with evil, there is a fear that it will take something with it in the process. In such skirmishes, when the "more evil" wants to drive out the "lesser evil," the patient must meanwhile risk his head. Therefore, my advice and undertaking is to exterminate the evil with goodness, and to teach accordingly so that this same art may be discovered—of which I may well boast in my healing, as follows in the first treatises hereafter.

---

<margin>C</margin>

# CHAPTER III.

->*How the Alchemists entered into medicine, and how Alchemy reveals whether to heal sores with wrath or with goodness.*<-

Now that the <term>Alchemists <note>Paracelsus was a pioneer in "Iatrochemistry," the use of chemistry to create medicines, bridging the gap between metallurgy/alchemy and physicians.</note></term> saw that the physicians were focused on "sharpness" (harshness) and through it undertook to find the healing of open sores, they took those same substances and prepared them according to the teachings of the Alchemical school, sharpening them to the highest degree. For instance, they made common salt liquid, and also <term>calcined <note>reduced to powder through heat</note></term> it in a <term>reverberatory furnace <note>original: "Reverber"; a furnace that reflects heat onto the substance.</note></term>, specifically using rock salt. Furthermore, they calcined vitriol and had it tested; this indeed proved successful in several sores, especially where it gripped the source. 

But because open sores are of many kinds and have many natures, and were only addressed <term>specifically <note>original: "Particulariter"</note></term> rather than seeking a <term>universal <note>original: "Vniversal"</note></term> cure, they came upon <term>sublimated mercury <note>original: "Mercurium sublimatum"; mercury chloride, a highly toxic and corrosive compound.</note></term>. Through this, a greater degree of healing was found, but because of the pain, no one could endure it. Afterward, they came upon <term>arsenic</term>, and upon <term>realgar <note>arsenic sulfide</note></term>, and other such <term>corrosives</term>, many of which were discovered one after another by the artists in Alchemy; each was tested individually, and in each, a specific "person" (case) was found—one in one manner, the other in another.

From this, it further arose—since each substance healed specific open sores—that the <term>Physicians <note>original: "Physici"; university-trained doctors.</note></term> emerged and made a distinction between the open sores, describing each according to its particular nature and adding the proven experiments to them. But because the origin of their healing in the disease was not as they themselves imagined it, their writings are to be considered useless. Especially since they have neither written nor taught from the foundation shown by <term>Astronomy</term> or the <term>Genealogy of Man</term>—that is, the Heavens indicate a different foundation that a physician should reflect upon. Which in...

<margin>A</margin>
...stands under the influence of the heavens, which works on and on; the older it becomes, the more it changes its works, like a human who grows from youth into old age—the longer it lasts, the more seriously it carries out its business. So it is also with genealogy; one person poisons the next through birth. Therefore, the last person suffers much more severely than the first. Such were the errors presented by the <term>useless codices <note>original: "vntüchtige Codices"; refers to the inherited medical textbooks of Galen and Avicenna that Paracelsus frequently criticized.</note></term>. Additionally, other errors have been brought forth that need not be mentioned here. But this much is to be known: that medicine has always been conducted with severity, always inclined to drive out evil with evil, never considering that no wrath is so great that it cannot be overcome with an equal measure of mildness. Nothing else was believed except that open injuries were a poison and should be driven out with poison; thus, they used poison against poison, not considering that two natures may exist in one body, just as wrath and goodness do. Although <term>Mercury <note>original: "Mercurius"; in Paracelsian thought, one of the three primary substances (Tria Prima) representing the transformative and healing principle, but also capable of being a corrosive poison.</note></term> is that which heals, it does so in two ways: in corrosiveness and in sweetness. They, however, did not recognize the sweetness but only sought after the sharpness, which is not becoming of a born physician. For look at the scorpion: it poisons, yet it heals itself again—but not through that same poison. Rather, it has another quality within it, separate from the poison, which heals. A man may give a harsh word and afterward a kind one. This is pointed out solely so that the physician should not stick to the proverb of "driving out evil with evil," but rather overcome the bitter through the sweet. For where the evil is, there also is the good. Through the good he should act, not through the evil, which is separated out through <term>alchemy <note>original: "Scheidung"; literally "separation," the process of refining a substance to remove its dross or toxicity.</note></term>.

### CHAPTER IV.
### How an order was made of corrosive medicines, and how surgery was mixed together with them, and what benefit or harm resulted from this.

<margin>B</margin>
After the <term>corrosives <note>original: "Corrosiff"; caustic substances used to burn away dead or infected flesh.</note></term> were sufficiently recognized and found in their work—what their nature and property were, and how they cast off an <term>eschar <note>original: "Escaram"; a dry crust or scab produced by a burn or corrosive application.</note></term> (that is, killed off a rim of flesh) and thus made a clear, clean hole and took away the old filth—they further applied surgery to it. Whatever was made of plaster and resin was found to be the most useful healing; from this experience, many kinds of plasters and ointments were subsequently invented. Now, however, because medicine was not yet set on the right track, and this was not the correct way—for the healing of injuries should not be in such a form—many adversities occurred, from which much misfortune arose. Thus, the sick were led around for many years and days, attacked with various <term>cauterizations <note>original: "Etzung"</note></term>, and tried in many ways. But because the true ground of healing was not so created by God, it was a wide sea in which no one could sail. For the reason was that even though a large eschar was cast off, the origin was not struck. To find and drive out the origin, all <term>physicians <note>original: "Physici"</note></term> shot wide of the mark. This gave cause for many writers to arise afterward, each believing he would hit the target. But because they took the arrows from the same quiver where the first ones searched, each followed the other in missing the mark, and thus never healed an open injury, unless nature itself healed over a long time—as it often happens that time itself heals a sickness. When this occurred, they <term>were made fools of <note>original: "einen Frewdaffen in den Elenbogen gehabt"; an idiom meaning they were deceived or held a worthless prize while thinking they were successful.</note></term>.

<margin>C</margin>
Furthermore, you should know that surgery is good here, as are the "sweet" corrosives. Only remember that you must grasp the origin; otherwise, you can never reach an end. For if you do not grasp the origin, all your plans will fail. Then, no kind of medicine is useful to you, and you can reach no conclusion. What you close up in one place, nature breaks open again in another. Or you yourself cauterize or cut it open again, or you must fear something worse. Therefore, do not think to make a burn-wound out of an open sore and then heal it like a burn, or to make a wound and then heal it like a wound. These plans all go against the wall; they shame you and the patient. Instead, you should know that neither cauterization nor surgery is the right way to heal open injuries. Therefore, do not strive to act according to what the physicians and <term>surgeons <note>original: "Chirurgici"</note></term> have written. For all their writings are detours and cannot be reconciled with the nature of open injuries. And although among them some students are found who have discovered a new find to heal open injuries through abstinence and <term>Guaiacum wood <note>original: "Holz Guaicum"; a medicinal wood from the Americas used as a popular but often ineffective treatment for syphilis in the 16th century.</note></term>, even this is not the right way. It is only that if nature has suffered long enough and wants to heal itself, and the time has come, then this find is indeed a good help. But where the time is not right, it is in vain and useless. I point this out to you so that you should know not to act in open injuries as has come down from olden times—all of which must happen through time, which "brings the roses," and for which many years and days must be expected. Instead, you should seek after the medicine that "cuts grain under the snow"—that is, acts against time. For medicine should overcome time, which was also left unrecorded by the ancients.
<margin>Medicine should overcome time</margin>

### CHAPTER V.
### How through the ancient artists, and the pursuit of health, certain secret arts were discovered, through which many origins of diseases were found.

The ancient artists were so eager that it would not be right if their industrious diligence were not described. For even though that which they sought was not fully brought forth, they were...

He connects the "transmutation" of metals to the "rejuvenation" of the human body, specifically regarding the treatment of persistent open sores and systemic diseases like quartan fever.</meta>

<page-num>66</page-num>
<header>The Second Book of the Great [Surgery]</header>

...yet the <term>Magnalia <note>original: "Magnalia"; refers to the "great works" or hidden wonders of God and nature that reveal the secrets of healing.</note></term> of medicine were thereby opened and discovered. They understood how to transform the lesser metals into the better: And although it is not against nature, it nevertheless meets much resistance. That iron becomes copper is evident; that copper becomes lead is also true, etc.

<margin>A</margin>
<margin>Artificial Transmutation [symbol]</margin>
Since they saw such wonderful transformation, they moved from that same <term>transmutation <note>The alchemical process of changing one substance into another; here, Paracelsus applies the logic of turning lead to gold to the "rejuvenating" of a sick body into a healthy one.</note></term> into medicine, in such a way that it happened that they worked and prepared certain <term>tinctures <note>concentrated medicinal solutions.</note></term> which, through poor storage, were eaten by chickens. The feathers of these chickens fell out—as I have seen—and grew back again. Through this, it was believed that humans could also be made young again in this way, so that whatever excess moisture was in the person would fall away. In this expulsion, the origin [of disease], which also arises through open sores, would be removed and a new, healthy nature planted—as is mentioned again in the treatise on healing. To judge such things is not against nature, but rather the desire of nature; for it is well known that such <term>regenerations <note>original: "Regenerierung"; the total renewal of the body's tissues.</note></term> have often occurred, proving that nature has shown its capability.

<margin> [symbol] </margin>
Now, it is no less true that in the healing of open sores, the ancients did not fully reach the end through such experience. The reason for this is the <term>Sophists <note>A derogatory term Paracelsus used for university-trained doctors who relied on rhetoric and old texts rather than practical experience.</note></term>, who have patched themselves into medicine, and the fictional <term>four Humors <note>original: "vier Humores"; the traditional Greek medical theory that health is governed by four fluids: blood, phlegm, yellow bile, and black bile.</note></term>, along with their useless chatter. Because of them, the arts have been laughed at and mocked, and thus medicine has fallen into "chatter-work." According to the contents of that same chatter, it has been governed until now; that [false] healing has prevailed, and the foundation of medicine—as mentioned above—has been extinguished.

<margin>B</margin>
But you should know this much: that this was the right foundation and intention, since the <term>Arcana <note>original: "Arcana"; powerful, secret "essences" or remedies that Paracelsus believed could strike at the heart of a disease.</note></term> are before our eyes, in which such powers and virtues are wonderfully found, so that they may again be rightly understood. What is greater in all of medicine than such a cleansing of the whole body, through which all the superfluity of the human is taken at the root and overturned? For what is the <term>purging <note>Standard medieval practice of using laxatives to balance the humors.</note></term> [of today] but that which does not take away what it should take, but rather takes away what it should not? And what does it take away, other than that which grows back immediately afterward? I speak so that the <term>seed <note>original: "Samen"; the "germ" or internal origin of a disease.</note></term> may be made healthy; then everything is well completed. And although it was written by the ancients what each thing purges, no true foundation was ever found to prove that what was claimed was actually driven out. The evidence testifies that the diseases always remained. As an example: if you purge <term>Melancholy <note>original: "Melancholiam"; black bile.</note></term> or <term>burnt Cholera <note>original: "Choleram adustam"; yellow bile that has been "scorched" by heat, thought to cause severe illness.</note></term> in a case of <term>Quartan fever <note>original: "Quartan"; a fever that recurs every four days, often associated with malaria.</note></term>, you cannot take away the Quartan through this. But when the old blood is made new, reborn, and made young—which must happen in the spleen—then the Quartan is healed. No one recovers unless the blood enters a youthful state. This is also to be understood with <term>Dropsy <note>original: "Wassersucht"; swelling caused by excess fluid (edema).</note></term>: if it is made young in its nature, then that youth drives out of itself whatever is not of the young, newborn blood. For in the same way, it has often happened that through such *Arcana*, teeth have fallen out which were rotten, worm-eaten, and burdened with all pain—for which no medicine was helpful or useful when used according to the foundations written by the ancients. But through the wonders of nature, they were rejuvenated in their roots, and the old ones fell out, and new ones grew in their place. Thus we should also know that in Quartan fever, the spleen must be renewed in this way. So also must every "seed" in which the origin of a disease lies. This should happen above all things in the healing of open sores, and without this foundation, no healing can be perfectly given.

## CHAPTER VI.
### How the origin of open sores is found in strange ways, and how it has been proven that the origin often moves or shifts.

<margin>C</margin>
Experience has shown something wonderful here, as mentioned in the previous chapters: that evil has been driven out by evil. Note such an experience: that in the great, agonizing pains of open sores, such great, painful medicines were used in response, such as the <term>Water of Hell <note>original: "Aqua gehenna"; a highly corrosive mineral acid.</note></term> and <term>Mercurial Water <note>original: "Aqua Mercurialis"; a solution of mercury.</note></term>, and others like them. Through their great pains, these drew the "seed" and the origin of the open sores into the open wounds of the injury. For such powers are in these <term>corrosives <note>substances that eat away tissue.</note></term> that they work along the same path through which the origin operates, and thus they come to the beginning of the disease, killing it "root and branch" <note>original: "Butzen vnd Stiel"; literally "core and stem."</note>. And such a thing is possible: for such corrosives are so subtle in spirit and so strongly natured toward the disease that they follow the disease backward from the wound of the injury to each origin, dissolving and resolving it, and sinking themselves into the wound of the injury. But as has been mentioned in several chapters, whoever wants to follow these rules must establish this: it requires a strong patient, and the doctor must be a very skilled and experienced one who has great experience in these things, and also knows how to prevent all injuries that might occur. I, for my part, will not give instruction in such matters. For so much care and anxiety are encountered that I will neither advise nor grant it to anyone. Furthermore, there is a wonderful effect in nature which resembles <term>magnets <note>original: "Magneten"; referring to the "attractive" force of certain medicines to pull toxins out of the body.</note></term>, which experience has provided; in the same way, when these medicines are taken internally, they have drawn the origins of the open sores to themselves and healed them internally where they lay. Subsequently, the wounds of the injuries were also healed with light skill. However, so that the <term>Pharisaic doctors <note>original: "Phariseischen Arzten"; Paracelsus's term for hypocritical medical authorities who care more for status and old laws than for healing.</note></term> would not lose their "chatter," this art also perished.

It has even come to this: if a proven physician has a proven **experiment** <note>In this context, a "tested remedy" or "clinical trial."</note> that is not made by the apothecary, it is despised and mocked. Thus the art of medicine has fallen into contempt; whoever wishes to use it correctly—and does use it—must be rejected and mocked by the others.

### CHAPTER VII.

#### How, during the time when various arts were being discovered, changes in diseases occurred, which necessitated the seeking of other arts.

<margin>B</margin>
Since so many types of diseases have grown over time, of a new and strange nature—including the mixing and uniting of several diseases with one another—it has happened that such strange occurrences have created confusion and hindrances for medicine. Therefore, these diseases have required the seeking of new arts. For in the same way that a human bothers himself daily with new fashions and grows weary of the old, loving instead strange new things, so too does such a nature and quality exist in the forces that cause disease. And just as craftsmen daily prepare themselves for new fashions, and learn and experience the new styles that fall into use daily to make them: so also should a physician be prepared and inclined to meet these same new fashions continually. For the new fashion arrives and creates a different nature of diseases; therefore, the old recipes cannot stand against these new, arriving diseases. Because of this, no one can defend himself using only the old writings and experiments. It would only be the case if an old disease showed itself, just as an old coat might occasionally be found.

Thus, when the new diseases arrived with different natures and properties, the true artists thought further, explored the **Light of Nature** <note>A core Paracelsian concept: the innate wisdom or "instruction manual" found within the natural world, accessible through observation and alchemy.</note> more deeply, and reached the foundation. Although the **Sophists** <note>Paracelsus’s term for traditional academic doctors who relied on books rather than experience and alchemy.</note> of medicine have carried on their pomp with their current methods, it nonetheless proves itself through their works that their "cleaning up" has no foundation. Look at the **French Disease** <note>original: "Frantzosen"; Syphilis.</note>, how strangely it arose: namely from a **leper** <note>original: "außetzigen"</note> and from a **slimy harlot** <note>original: "Schlierigen Mätzent"; "Schlier" refers to diseased discharge or mucus.</note> who, through her unchastity, poisoned others, who then fell into the French Disease. Thus, from "slime" and leprosy sprang the disease of the **pox** <note>original: "Blatern"</note>, in the same way that a **mule** <note>original: "Maulthier"</note> is born from a horse and a donkey. 

Now, as this has been proven and confirmed—that the pox arose from those two and entered no one except through the acts of **unchastity** <note>Margin C</note>—it spreads and is inherited, and subsequently enters into the open sores and transforms them into a different nature. It has also happened many times that through the acts of unchastity, two kinds of disease have been joined together, which together have made a new one, different from either of the two. For who would contradict this? Since unchastity is the "mother" of the French Diseases, why should other diseases not also be born in such a form and shape? Furthermore, since it is clear as day that unchastity corrupts much in humans and brings about causes [of illness], it is necessary that such diseases be well recognized and understood, so that they may be more easily healed through their appropriate medicine. For experience has given this much in the discovery of medicinal arts: that **Mercury** <note>original: "Mercurius"; Paracelsus was a pioneer in using mercury to treat syphilis.</note> is the **Patron** <note>The guiding principle or primary remedy.</note> for healing all diseases that manifest in open sores and take their origin from unchastity. Thus, the physician who wishes to have a foundation and understanding of the truth should know how to distinguish such an origin from other origins, and that Mercury alone is the **Arcanum** <note>original: "Arcanum"; a secret, powerful healing essence or "mystery."</note> in which unchastity rejoices <note>Meaning Mercury is the specific remedy that "matches" or masters the disease caused by sexual contact.</note>.

### CHAPTER VIII.

#### Regarding the discovery of certain secret main principles by the proven physicians of old, and how the unproven have patched in their sophistry.

So that you may well understand my undertaking, I speak here of open sores. And because the French Disease also occurred and its nature was still unknown, the medicines used to drive it out were those commonly used for open sores. However, because the origin came from unchastity, and not as the origin of open sores is accustomed to be, those same medicines could not be effective, but were rather more harmful. See—

It has, however, happened time and again that **mercury sublimate** <note>original: "Mercurius sublimatus"; a highly toxic alchemical preparation of mercury used as a potent, though dangerous, medicine.</note> was also used, which among other substances was taken up here. Among these substances, it was found that when it was introduced into the body, it drove out diseases through the **salivation of the mouth** <note>original: "geifern deß Mauls"; mercury poisoning causes excessive drooling, which physicians of the time wrongly believed was the body "leaking out" the disease.</note>. It was not that the drool itself was the disease, but rather the disease was mixed within it, much like how **saffron** sits in water: the water itself does not turn yellow on its own, only the saffron does it, yet the two become united as one.

<margin>B</margin>
Now, because many artistic uses were found for Mercury, and it alone proves itself to be the "principal piece" of medicine, the **Sophistical doctors** <note>Paracelsus’s derogatory term for university-trained physicians who followed ancient Greek theories (like those of Galen) rather than experimental alchemy.</note> could not restrain their own dishonesty. They attributed powers to Mercury that were not appropriate for it, and thereby they destroyed many people. For the secret and the entire treasure lies in Mercury alone, without any additives: but it was so "sophisticated" <note>In the sense of being corrupted or over-complicated by false reasoning.</note> that no more attention was paid to the true foundation. Once such [corrupted] medicine took hold, the correct healing of **open sores** <note>Chronic wounds or ulcers.</note> was completely forgotten, and only **pox-medicines** <note>original: "Blaterische Arzney"; treatments for "the pox" or syphilis.</note> were used. However, because these sores did not always arise from **unchastity** <note>original: "Vnkeuschheit"; a reference to the sexually transmitted nature of syphilis.</note>, the patients remained uncured.

I point this out so that the medicine may be properly distinguished: we must bring back the treatment that belongs to open sores, which has until now been ignored by the Sophistical doctors. They treated everything with pox-medicine, through which they have ruined and shamed a great many people. Otherwise, my writing here is not about the "pox," except as an example to show how the pox caused the cure for open sores to be forgotten. To ensure that open sores are healed, one must abandon the pox-medicine and consider the "foundation" mentioned in the previous chapters—not just looking at the locations where such sores break out. The foundation of medicine is not as the Sophists write; it was not ordained by God to proceed in their way, but rather in the **Order of Nature**, which the Sophists have never recognized.

And even though open sores may change their appearance, anything born outside of **unchastity** <note>i.e., non-venereal wounds.</note> should by no means be treated with pox-medicine. Even if a certain quality of the pox were incorporated through unchastity, if the obvious signs of the pox were not there, Mercury should be left idle. For the origin of the **French Disease** <note>original: "Franzosen"; a common 16th-century term for Syphilis.</note> had a special influence—not just a natural tendency, but also a decree from God, His disposition to put a "bridle" on such extravagance [promiscuity]. Just as the **Plague** does not come by nature alone but also as a punishment to prevent something worse, it cannot be denied that the French Disease is a plague of unchastity. Therefore, it is perhaps a divine providence that the Sophistical doctors exist and must be there to further plague the sick along with the disease. One must understand that open sores are not subject to such a plague; they are of **natural origin**.

### C A P V T IX.
<note>Chapter 9</note>

### How the Origin of Open Sores is Mineral, and Not from the Humors, and How Much Error Has Grown from This Misunderstanding.

<margin>C</margin>
I do not wish here to fully explain the true origin of open sores, but rather to give you to understand what the "precursor" is that gives birth to this disease. There is in man a **corrosive nature** <note>A chemical property that "eats away" at tissue.</note> that manifests and finds itself; this must be highly considered, yet it has been neglected. Hear how I present this to you: The sweat that comes from a person is salty. Now, the sweat itself is not the "true salt," but there is another salt from which it comes, and the sweat is merely its **excrement** <note>Waste product.</note>. Now it is necessary to know where that salt comes from: namely, from the same origin that the sweat comes from, the origin of open sores also comes. From this it follows that no "sharpness" is found in the whole body except in the veins—that is, in the blood itself. If, then, the salt and that same sharpness which creates open sores are found in the blood, it is only right to seek the origin in that same place: for in the veins lies the origin of all open sores.

It should be remembered that the salt in the blood must have a goal and a measure to perform its office, and no more. What is contrary to nature is expelled through sweat. But if we consider further that nothing follows "order" perfectly—rather, all things strive against it, both in the intellect and in the animal limbs—it follows that even in salt, Order does not always prevail. Therefore, the physician must speak of maintaining that order and bringing what has fallen out of order back into it. If a disorder is found in the limbs, it is good to remember that there is something in the body—that is, in Nature—that creates such disorder and corrupts good things in the body, just like an **apothecary** who takes many things and mixes them together, ruining them all. Therefore, we should know how to correctly recognize this disorder. Thus we find that all open sores come and arise from the blood.

Now, this is **Mineral** in nature, for the reason that salt reigns in that place, and salt is the origin of these diseases. Therefore, we should not discuss **Humors** <note>The ancient theory of the "Four Humors" (blood, phlegm, yellow bile, black bile) which Paracelsus rejected in favor of chemical/mineral causes.</note>, but rather a **Mineral** and **Minerva** <note>Minerva was the Roman goddess of wisdom and spinning; Paracelsus uses her name here to refer to the "wisdom" or "alchemy" of the mineral world.</note>. How can a Mineral or a "Minerva" be a Humor? See now how greatly this has been overlooked in medicine, and they do not want it to be exposed. Is it not a great error to say this is a Humor? They claim a "Humor" is something else, and so they categorize open sores into four types according to the **Four Humors**, when in fact there is only one cause for all open sores: namely, the salt in the blood.

It is not embodied in **Melancholy** <note>black bile</note>, nor in **Phlegm**, nor is it **Cholera** <note>yellow bile</note>. No "fictional humor" <note>Paracelsus’s dismissive term for the traditional four humors of Galenic medicine.</note> reaches that place, about which only fictional things have been written.

# CHAPTER 10.

## How a seed is sown within man, which seed compels and forces him toward the end of his harvest; and it is Predestination, toward a forced, future illness.

疼 瘡 瘻 <note>These Chinese characters—meaning pain, sores, and fistulas—appear in the margin of some editions of Paracelsus, reflecting his interest in universal or "Oriental" medical knowledge, or perhaps added by a later scholarly annotator.</note></margin> It is no less true that when we are born and conceived, we are **predestined** <note>original: "prædestiniert"</note> for death. Now, it follows further from this that we fall into illnesses that do not come out of our own nature and being, but from something foreign: just as one sows a foreign seed in a garden. We should understand it thus: we know that the Plague comes against Nature and without the nature of the body. Now, it is a seed that is sown by a foreign person <note>or "foreign entity"</note>. In this way, all diseases are sown, each by its own "husbandman" <note>original: "Bawmann"; an agent or force that "cultivates" the disease.</note>, of which there are many kinds. For it is true that man was made healthy and well, for all creatures pleased God well. But he did not remain long in that "wellness"; rather, he departed from it, and something else became of the well-made man, and he was so transformed into misery that God regretted that He had created man. There occurred the origin of all disease. And just as the entire Earth was sown by God, so too were diseases sown in man; thus, every man is born into his illness. Since birth now compels an illness to grow through the "sowing," this is the first origin of all illness, and there is no other origin to speak of. Nothing at all. The illness that is subject to the physician has its seed outside of Predestination; it is sown from the fact that we are **fragile** <note>original: "zerbrüchlich"</note>, and that fragility sows the illness for us. 

But so that you may understand this regarding **Open Sores** <note>original: "Offnen Schäden"; chronic ulcers or wounds that won't heal.</note>, there is no disorder in the body except what is provoked by the seed—of which we shall speak presently—just like a man who starts a riot out of his own head, which riot gives no visible or tangible origin. Thus, no one knows what it is that brought the First Man into that same material. For no one knows how the mind and reason are defended, or what it is that makes a man this way or that way. Thus, nothing can be grasped by the intellect as to what it is that makes Nature contrary within itself, whereby it corrupts itself. So there is something that cannot be written down, which makes a thing ready and prepared, and orders it so that it can carry out such an undertaking: like the **Salt in the blood** that comes out of its nature and **complexion** <note>the specific constitutional makeup of a person</note>, and becomes prepared in such a way that it can eat away flesh and skin. <margin>C</margin> As much as can be understood in the "Light of Nature," it may be grasped that a **secret man** <note>original: "heimlicher Mensch"; the "Inner Archeus" or hidden biological blueprint.</note> stays within the man, whom God created, perhaps to arrange such things; and He ordained such readiness in man, endowed with arts and skill, to thus be contrary to man, who must then be surrounded by much misery. But concerning all these things, we should also know that it is in vain to recognize the first origin other than as has been mentioned. We may well know that Salt alone in man is the cause of open sores. But what it is that gives the Salt the "skill" to work in such a form cannot be found, other than that a **hidden smith** <note>original: "verborgener Schmidt"</note> must run along with it. He is to be understood in the same way as can be recognized in a seed: it grows into a tree or another plant. Who sees that same sculptor? Or who is the one who sees who it is that can prepare it so? Thus, you should also understand that something is innate in man that makes all illness, and it is known to no one. But that thing in which it works—that is subject to the physician.

# CHAPTER 11.

## What the Elements in man are, and what they work within him; what their power and might are; and that "Humors" may not be found there.

You should also know how the Ancients said that there are **four humors** <note>original: "vier Humores"</note> in the body, which are then supposed to be the cause of open sores, as has been mentioned many times. You should not think that it is so. For there is but one cause: Man is formed according to the **Great World** <note>the macrocosm or universe</note>, so that he has the **four Elements** essentially within him. Not that this is an "element" or that it is "hot and moist," etc., but that it is an element that has the Essential Nature in it. Like the **Earth**: it has the power of the earth. Not that it is cold and dry alone, but also hot and dry, hot and moist, cold and moist. For that is...

the element of Earth—that which comprises the earth and its growths. It is the same with the element of Water—that which is water and grows from it, or what may be transformed into water. So also is the element of Air—that which is wind and air, and not merely what belongs to a <term>complexion</term> <note>In ancient medicine, "complexion" referred to the balance of bodily qualities like hot, cold, moist, or dry.</note>. So also is the element of Fire—the firmament of the heavens and everything contained within it, whether hot or cold (like the Sun and Moon) or dry and wet (like snow and water), etc. We should also recognize this in man: that man is likewise placed within the four elements, as follows: What concerns his mind and senses is the element of Fire; what grows from the dry body is Earth; what grows from the <term>liquor</term> <note>the bodily fluids</note> is the element of Water; and what grows in the void, where there is no substance, is the element of Air.

From this it follows that cramps in the belly arise from the Air. And those whom you call **Melancholic**, you should instead call **Lunatic** <note>original: "Lunaticum"; meaning governed by the Moon rather than black bile.</note>. Those whom you call **Choleric**, more rightly call **Martial** <note>original: "Martialem"; governed by Mars, the planet of war and heat.</note>. Those whom you call **Phlegmatic**, better call **Aquatic** <note>original: "Aquatium"; governed by water.</note>. The same applies to their diseases, which need not be fully identified here, except insofar as they concern open wounds. You should know that there are no <term>humors</term> <note>The four bodily fluids (blood, phlegm, yellow bile, black bile) that traditional medicine blamed for all illness.</note> in the body. Furthermore, you should note: if a lesion breaks out on the liver, attribute it to the liver; if it breaks out in the head, attribute it to the head; if it breaks out in the spleen, attribute it to the spleen—not to "Melancholy" or "Phlegm" or the blood. For many diseases occur in places where none of those three humors reach. Diseases take a different origin than the "fictional fantasies" taught by the theory of humors. Every star in man can create disease; how then can a "humor" be introduced as the cause?

Just as leaves and grass grow from the earth, so do diseases grow in man. Who then can say that "Melancholy" is a cause? The same applies to the other elements. It is a great error when people say a disease comes from "Melancholy" just because the disease and the melancholy share the same nature or complexion. In truth, that which grows from an element
<margin>B</margin>
does not necessarily share the nature of that element. For example, the plant **Flammula** <note>original: "Flammaula"; likely Spearwort, a type of buttercup known for its "burning" or stinging juice.</note> grows from the earth, yet these are two contrary natures (hot plant, cold earth). Also, a child rarely takes after the father’s complexion without having a wide difference. Therefore, it is possible for a "hot" disease to grow from the element of Earth within man. Likewise, a contrary nature can arise from the element of Water, such as **Marsh Flax** <note>original: "Linum palustre".</note>. The same is true for the others.

What causes the "shattering of reason" in man comes from his own internal firmament, not through heat or cold, moisture or dryness. It is just as if someone threw a stone into a flock of birds or a pack of dogs: each one snaps up in its anger. This is caused neither by cold
<margin>General Judgment 4, chapter 39.</margin>
nor warmth, but by the stone itself. Similarly, a sword does not wound through the power of cold or heat, but through the property of the steel, in which such a <term>predestination</term> <note>The inherent, divinely-appointed purpose or "destiny" of an object's nature.</note> exists. In the same way, the reason of men is shattered according to the nature of those stars, and likewise according to the Moon. Therefore, you must not purge "Melancholy"; you must instead only restrain the Moon and stars, for they are what create the disease. This should also be understood regarding open wounds: they do not arise from humors, as is commonly said.

### CHAPTER 12.

->How artists were so eager to explore the secrets of nature, and how they<-
->sought experience through faith, as well as through the<-
->power of nature.<-

<margin>C</margin>
Since I wish to base my foundations solely on experience, it is necessary that I bring forward those who have shared this opinion. Therefore, it is proper that I recount and present those arts through which experience is gained. I mentioned in the previous chapter how the ancient writers relied on a useless foundation, through which no one could gain experience except by being forced down one path and no other. But experience will tolerate neither God’s compulsion nor man’s force; it must be free, for human reason cannot govern itself. Therefore, you shall understand the methods for experiencing the arts, as they were among the righteous ancients and as is still proper today.

First, through **faith**. That is, many have sought to see through stones, such as **crystals** <note>original: "Brillen"; while this usually means "spectacles," in 16th-century occultism it often referred to lenses or "shew-stones" used for divination.</note> and the like, and through them to fathom experience in nature. Now, you must first know what is to be seen in such visions: there is nothing there that is against nature or against the property of created things. What is there is natural. Whether it is so or not remains a matter for their faith. However, it must be mentioned here that a righteous, diligent desire to seek the art of nature and to fathom her secrets and the works of God will cause a man's own assigned **Ascendant** <note>original: "Ascendens"; the astrological sign rising at the moment of birth.</note> to reveal things to him, according to what kind of man he is. They stand revealed as far as they both stand toward each other, for one is like the other. 

Therefore, such excellent, well-formed, and upright artists have sought to find arts through crystals, mirrors, fingernails, birds, etc., according to how their heart was, and so also was their Ascendant in that very work. Thus faith, which is a love for the art, acted toward the one who sought love there; and he was paid with love. Thus many arts have been opened, both righteous and unrighteous, according to how each person was born in his Ascendant. Therefore, know that the system of "fictional medicines" contains no discovery of art, for they are contrary to the true Mother <note>Nature</note> for finding the art. Furthermore, nature has made herself known through **Anatomy**, **Chiromancy** <note>palm reading</note>, and **Physiognomy** <note>judging character from facial features</note>, in the sense that she has joined together in her order both the enemy and the conqueror. In this manner, no disease...

# Surgery: The First Treatise

<margin>A</margin>...not that she <note>Refers to Nature or the "outer anatomy."</note> has distribution and a whole limb. If such is the case, her enemy stands in the same image as well; thus, it is immediately found what one thing is that drives out the other. As an example: In the same measure and form as the eyes maintain their <term>anatomy</term> <note>In this context, Paracelsus uses "anatomy" to mean the internal structure and external appearance that reflects an object’s essence.</note>, so does **Eyebright** <note>original: "Eufragia"; a herb traditionally used to treat eye ailments because its flower was thought to resemble an eye.</note> maintain its own. From this it follows that Eyebright allows nothing harmful to happen to the eyes, for they are kindred and united in the blood, both originating from one seed, changed only in their visible essence. Thus, the kindred blood strengthens its cousin. Therefore, it is necessary that the anatomy of all things be well understood—how the limb stands in its image—for then one finds where the kinship lies between man and external nature, and how they are to be compared. For every disease and its medicine share the same <term>physiognomy</term> <note>reading the character from the face/form</note>, <term>chiromancy</term> <note>palmistry or reading signs in the hands/structure</note>, and anatomy; otherwise, no one can be a physician unless he possesses this understanding and foundation. If we are to seek and find arts, there must be something through which they are found that is equal to nature and proves itself uniform with the **Light of Nature** <note>A central Paracelsian concept: the innate wisdom placed by God within the natural world, accessible through observation rather than books.</note>, whether it be **Astronomical** <note>Meaning through planetary influences.</note> through faith, or through the uniform image of nature. However it may be, it must be discovered in this way, unless something should fall in "crosswise" <note>Meaning by chance or sudden inspiration.</note> through which arts are wonderfully discovered, as will be mentioned in the following chapters. However, I point this out because the fictitious doctors have no way of discovering art and the like. Therefore, they are rightly to be hated, as they are so entirely contrary to the discovery of the arts; moreover, they have created an order against the arts in which nothing proceeds on its own except that which fakes and cheats the art.

## CHAPTER XIII.

->How the arts are wonderfully found, and how the one who gives the art does not let himself be known, but acts in an unknown, marvelous way.<-

<margin>B</margin> Even though the fictitious doctors might bring in many open wounds and test themselves through their established principles—proposing an art through which they claim to know how many **degrees** <note>Galenic medicine categorized all substances into four "degrees" of heat, cold, moisture, or dryness.</note> every herb is cold or warm, dry or moist, as their *Dioscorides*, *Avicenna*, *Serapio*, and others of their kind have indicated—yet the art of such discovery was never known to them. Furthermore, there is nothing to be found in such degrees, and it is a mockery to write of them. They are those who wish to cure all their diseases through such arts and principles; it is time to contradict this. For through those same principles, no sick person can ever again be made healthy or healed. Nevertheless, they categorize medicines for open wounds against nature and the needs of the sick. This makes it right for me to show another foundation for finding art—namely, regarding those arts found by "chance" which the Highest Good <note>God</note> gives, yet He does not wish to be recognized as the giver. As an example: When one gives alms, the **left hand should not know what the right hand does** <note>A reference to the Gospel of Matthew 6:3.</note>. This means it should not be blown with trumpets. Since the Giver of all arts is the one who set and gave this commandment, He is the first to pull that same yoke which He commanded us to carry. From this it follows that no one should make a hypocrisy of his works, but do them so that no one knows but Him in Heaven; thus it pleases Him. From this foundation, I may now speak further, since the secrets of nature fall upon us so wonderfully, and through man, wonderful works are discovered, which God allows to be granted to the artists without seeking His own glory. This is truly seen in how many things are found by **Alchemists** which do not spring from their own skill, nor were they born with such great subtlety. Yet it happens in so many ways that they themselves did not understand it until the time comes for the one to whom it is destined.

<margin>C</margin> The reason I have begun this chapter is that the fictitious doctors want to cling too much to **Pharisaic** <note>A criticism of those who focus on outward rules and legalism rather than inner truth.</note> customs, through which they find nothing true. They should sense and recognize that the arts are found not according to their own mind, but according to my indication. This is the purpose of this chapter: that God does not want to let the right hand be known to the left. For man is the left hand and does not recognize the goodness or where it comes from. For the left hand is so inclined that if one needs water in a field, one does not cry out for the right hand, but for the rain. If the grain comes well into the barns, one praises the good weather, not the right hand. Therefore, the left hand does not know what the right does. Since God wishes to be so hidden in His works, it is right to consider this further and to follow such an innate quality, seeking art in whatever way it may be found—not minding how they prove themselves, but only that they are found. Because of this, I cannot despise certain **Canons** of the **Astrologers**, nor the art of **Geomancy** <note>Divination by means of earth or geographic features.</note>, and other such things which would only be mockingly received here in this book. For even if the art itself had a "foolish nose," if the right hand allowed something to reach the left through it, who would despise the goodness that God has given? Therefore, I want it to be known that I also have art here for open wounds which did not fly in according to the principles of the fictitious doctors, but with a more substantial and greater foundation. I boast that in the discovery of the arts, I am differently gifted than those who are not fond of me, and

# CHAPTER XIV.

### How, first and above all things, a physician should recognize and know the ailments, diseases, and condition of external creatures, and thereafter those of man.

**N**ow I must speak further: because the "Humorists" <note>Followers of Galen who believed disease was caused by an imbalance of the four humors: blood, phlegm, yellow bile, and black bile.</note> attribute the origin of all open wounds to wherever they please, yet have no other ground or knowledge than what they find in their invented humors: It is therefore only fair that they be directed toward **Philosophy**—that is, into the growth of the earth—so that they might know from whence the ailments of earthly growths come. For they also have diseases and similar ailments. Here, the **Philosopher** <note>In Paracelsus’s time, a philosopher was a student of the natural world and its hidden powers.</note> and the **Physician** are distinguished: the Philosopher recognizes the disease and nature of earthly growths, and the Physician recognizes the internal—that is, the nature and disease of man.

He who wishes to be a physician must and shall first be a philosopher, and know philosophy, and only then know man. For whatever cause makes wood, grass, leaves, etc., suffer, that same cause also makes man suffer. Now, there are no "humors" in leaves and grass and wood; that is, in wood, grass, herbs, leaves, and flowers there is neither <term>Melancholia</term> <note>black bile</note>, nor <term>Phlegma</term> <note>phlegm</note>, nor <term>Cholera</term> <note>yellow bile</note>, nor—as they claim—<term>Sanguis</term> <note>blood</note>. Rather, there is only a single moisture; that is a <term>Liquor</term> <note>Paracelsus’s term for the vital fluid or "mercury" of a substance</note> in which they exist.

For all things are composed of **Three Things**: **Salt**, **Sulfur**, and the **Liquor**. These three make up every single thing; the smallest part of them cannot be missing, nor can it endure more [than its share]. Thus, in growths, there is only the essence of these three things: and so it is also in man. Therefore, these three must be that which causes sickness, whether in external growths or in man. This is now spoken regarding the *materia* <note>the physical substance</note> of diseases.

<margin>B</margin> What actually creates the diseases, however, must first be understood and recognized according to Philosophy; and after Philosophy, through **Physics**. But if a physician does not come into medicine by way of Philosophy, he cannot be a physician: for he does not enter through the right door, but climbs in through the roof. Therefore, they become murderers and thieves—that is, they become ignorant physicians, through whose ignorance they kill people and lead them to harmful destruction. Furthermore, they think only of money, not the right path to health.

Thus, Philosophy is the discoverer of earthly growths and diseases: why wood rots in a green tree; for what reasons worms grow in it; what it is that causes leaves to be riddled with holes and pierced at their time in the hazel bushes, etc.

Therefore, as this is so, and as the foundation is established, the following should also be understood: the <term>Corpus Physicum</term> <note>the physical body</note>, which is the <term>Microcosmus</term> <note>The "Little World"—the human being as a reflection of the entire universe.</note>. Thus, the cause and origin of open wounds are discovered: it is proven that wounds arise partly from **Salt**, and partly from the **Stars** <note>original: "Gestirn"; the influence of celestial bodies on health.</note>. What comes from the stars, the Philosopher lets lie; but that which comes from Salt, he treats. But a physician should let nothing lie, but should be just as much an **Astronomer** as a Philosopher. For therein arises the foundation of medicine.

I point this out only so that the humors are not taken as the cause, but rather the Philosophy in the growth [of nature], which proves to us that man does not consist of four humors, but only of three things: **Salt**, **Sulfur**, and **Liquor**. And in the same way that wood, grass, herbs, and leaves have accidents and ailments, so also in such a manner is man to be recognized like them. I leave this for now to Philosophy. This is the gate into medicine; this is the way into it; thus must it be taught. And whatever is outside of this is an invented thing, a fantasy without foundation. Therefore, the wind blows it back and forth like a reed—that is, they can find no constant foundation that is certain, even though they refuse to build upon a rock.

<margin>C</margin>

# CHAPTER XV.

### How wisdom and art flow into a person who learns nothing from others (as mentioned above), and how a physician’s birth should also be.

**I**t is seen and publicly proven that man has come into the world without any wisdom, understanding, or art, yet has completed, invented, devised, and proven wonderful works. For thus have all arts that exist on earth been found: good and evil, useful and useless, etc. And not only the righteous—that is, the righteous arts—but also the unrighteous ones have both been invented.

But know now that the unrighteous have set their foundation such that nothing further may be found, but rather what is found shall remain as it is. But the righteous search on and on, and wish to improve their art. And so it happens that the latest painter is better than the first, the latest miner better than the first, and so with all things among the righteous—that is, those who walk in the right way.

But in medicine, those same people will not admit this, claiming there is no other foundation than what **Avicenna** <note>An 11th-century Persian physician whose "Canon of Medicine" was the standard textbook in Europe, which Paracelsus famously rejected.</note> and his followers teach, who yet are not on the right foundation of diseases. Therefore, it is proper that the foundation of man's wisdom, art, etc., be spoken of—from whom he speaks—and it is thus:

Heaven and Earth, through man, make the man; and man is their son,

<margin>A</margin> Son / daughter / child: From Heaven he has understanding, from the Earth the body. Now, as he is of the Earth, so is he in his body, and so must he return into it. Likewise, what is from Heaven—that is, from the <term>Firmament</term> <note>In this context, the "Firmament" refers to the celestial influences or "stars" that Paracelsus believed shaped a person's character and innate talents.</note>—is also like the Firmament, and remains in the Firmament. Beyond this, however, follows one more thing, which is a gift and an attachment from God: that man should live and walk in that same gift, and not according to the Firmament alone. But the reason I mention it here is natural: how man is born skillful from the stars, yet also deceived. Although that which comes to man from God is above all, nature is nonetheless gifted within itself. Now, naturally, it follows from this that man is born according to the stars for arts, or for non-arts; for wisdom, or for folly; for this or for that way of life. From this it follows that some men, by innate nature, have discovered and proven many things, and may still discover and prove them in such a way. So too are those born who are <term>Sophists</term> <note>Paracelsus used "Sophists" as a derogatory term for university-trained doctors who relied on old books and clever rhetoric rather than practical experience and the laws of nature.</note> in whatever they touch: for Evil and Good always run together. Therefore, because man has an innate nature from the Firmament—from his own birth—to find subtleties or other things, he is born into that: just as Christ was born into His purpose, so too was Judas into his. But from this it follows that it would be better if the evil man of the stars had not been born: yet they also write, they also learn, and they do all things just as well as the righteous.

<margin>B</margin> Therefore, we should first of all look at what Christ says: "By their works you shall know them" <note>Matthew 7:16</note>; that is, who is good or evil, by their fruits. From this it follows that the physician who performs signs and works, and brings his labor to the end for which it is <term>predestined</term> and ordained, should be followed. He who does not bring it to that end cannot be called a physician: rather, a foolish star, a fantastical <term>Constellation</term> <note>original: "Constellatio"</note> gave birth to him. It would be better for him if he had never been born than to thus lead the people astray. Therefore, the Wise Man, who learns from God, overcomes the stars in his judgment—be they good or evil—through Divine Wisdom; otherwise, no "Wise Man" who is solely of nature can overcome them. And those who have learned from God are the most learned; those from the stars, the least; those from the <term>Light of Nature</term> <note>The "Light of Nature" (Lumen Naturae) is a central Paracelsian concept: the intuitive knowledge of the world gained through observation and alignment with natural laws.</note> are in the middle, for they have the physical object before them from which they speak, regardless of what the stars intended for them. Thus there are three ways by which we learn and are taught: and yet a deception always mixes itself in alongside the righteous way. Therefore, regarding <term>Open Wounds</term> <note>original: "Offnen schäden"; refers to external injuries, ulcers, or lesions requiring surgical care.</note>, I may well say that alongside those born to medicine, physicians have been born who have written of it who are not physicians from the stars, but "presumed" physicians; not from the Light of Nature (which makes a physician), but from their own fantasy. Of God they have little, for they perform few signs.

### CHAPTER VI.

-> How the ancient righteous physicians fell into the righteous arts without understanding and knowledge of the origins. <-

Thus the stars gave birth to the righteous physicians in the Light of Nature, and they were born to it in such a way that they themselves discovered righteous arts for Open Wounds through reflection and thought. And this was so grasped by nature that it directed the <term>Constellation and Influence</term> <note>original: "Constellatio vnd Influentia"</note> first into <term>Alchemy</term> <note>To Paracelsus, alchemy was not just about making gold, but the art of using fire to extract the medicinal virtues from plants and minerals.</note>, which is an art of discovery by means of fire: specifically, what is possible for fire to do, and what may happen through fire for the benefit of man. Thus the art of Alchemy arose, in which there then occurred wonderful transformations, preparations, different essences, different types, and different natures. When such was found, the innate skill was there, and it joined together the discovered medicine and the Open Wounds. For thus the constellation of the Firmament and the innate nature of the Earth were united, so that he who has the skill from Heaven also has the nature of the Earth embodied within him, and also has a love for the Earth. Thus the growths of the Earth and the Heavenly skill came together in one body, followed by the <term>Influence</term> of love for mankind from above. These three together give birth to a physician.

<margin>C</margin> Thus the Earth, out of innate love in its growths, has given man the use of his skill from the Firmament, and that same skill for the benefit of man. Thus the physician is created: as he is born, so arts become sufficient for him, and he finds every day what is necessary. Such is the origin of a physician. But there have arisen those who were not born into medicine and yet undertook to describe and know it: these are the ones who have made great books: for with much chatter they have maintained themselves. But in all things, <term>Astronomy</term> <note>Here used in the sense of Astrology or the study of celestial influences on human vocation.</note> should be learned better and more thoroughly than it has been <margin>* up until now.</margin> <note>original: "fort à noch biß her"</note> learned for mere pleasure; for it is a certain and true art that teaches one to recognize that into which a man is born. Therefore, man should experience that same art fundamentally, so that through it, it might be shown what a man is born to do, so that he might do that very thing; then wise, learned, and skillful people would come from them. For such knowledge may well be understood from the first astronomers, that they gave such indications to the people: therefore many brave, powerful men, and also women, were found who did many and great things. For they were drawn and taught in that which they were born for.

Accordingly, they discovered more and greater things out of their innate type and nature. But where such is not considered, and a child is raised against that into which it was born, and must enter into another "birth" than the one it was born into, then it becomes a perverted, erring, and dull being.

He criticizes "Sophists" who lack this innate calling and advocates for using astronomy to determine a person's natural vocation to avoid creating "dull" or "perverted" practitioners.</summary>
