# The Second Book of Great [Sores]

oldest and the most persistent among all other open sores. And where they are not rightly and well managed with **diet** <note>original: "Diarta"</note> and **regimen** <note>original: "Ordinantz"</note>, they end in **dropsy** <note>original: "Waſſerſucht," an accumulation of fluid in the body</note>. But where their order is good, there are also people who are burdened with less sickness. It is also the highest **preventative** <note>original: "Preſervatif"</note> that may exist out of its own nature against the **plague**, **pleurisy**, and the **French disease** <note>syphilis</note>.

There are likewise several open sores which, as said above, arise but change over time into a dryness and parching, and after that, a pain: this also happens often in **vitriolic sores**. And the cause is this: that the **alum** <note>original: "Alumen"</note> or **vitriol** <note>sulfate minerals</note> **calcine** <note>to reduce to powder by heat</note> themselves; after which calcination they transform into such a shape and take on another essence and property than they had before. Now this calcination happens over a long time, thus: when the moisture from the body is entirely resolved and leaves the dry salt lying there. In the same way as when **alum** <note>original: "Alas"</note> or other heat-sources are dried in. And although in vitriol [the pain increases] every time from such calcination, the pains become even greater, and the [corrosive salts] eat together and consume the skin, subsequently the bones also, and they come from their own running and flow, becoming dry and parched: unless it be the case that a moisture sinks down there from **food and drink**. So it is also with alum, when its effect is in a **calcined nature** and property.
<margin>B</margin>
So also are several other **salts** <note>original: "Salia"</note>, such as the **common salts** <note>original: "Communia"</note>, which manifest in their destruction just like alum: with wet moisture, with the drying in of pits, but with more pain, and yet without heat and great aching. Such causes arise from this: when the **common salt** is destroyed by warm moisture, then nature desires to expel such from itself, and thus rubs it into the outermost limbs, and makes a passage for itself therein, and gives it a [path] where the salt arises, having its usual way to the exit. [These] are called **common [salts]**. However, they are of the same effect and order as has been said: they are also of the kind that they themselves may be **rectified** <note>original: "Erricciert," likely meaning purified or corrected</note> again; as soon as the rectification occurs, it is easy to come to health. But where calcination occurs, there it is worse and harder to heal. Thus are the open sores—of vitriol, of alum, and of common salts—recognized in their raw and calcined nature.

->CHAPTER XI.<-
->Tells of the evil sores, which are difficult to resolve.<-

Now there are several other **salts** which lie in the best powers of man, in the same way as **arsenic** <note>original: "Arſenicus"</note> lies in gold and silver. Now if such salts are separated and sorted from the best powers of man through their own natural power, [it is like] whoever [separates] the mentioned **arsenic** <note>original: "Realgar," specifically red arsenic sulfide</note> from gold: then it follows thereafter that the **microcosm** <note>original: "Microcolmo," the human body as a miniature universe</note> expels it into the outermost limbs, in the same way as a wind ordained by God drives the **smelter-smoke** <note>original: "Hütterauch"</note> out of the foundry. For just as it is the nature of the smelter-smoke to desire the distance of its own accord, so man is created in many kinds of temptation and toward many kinds of destruction against him, so that he is rightly called the **microcosm**, for the reason that all the things of the great world are contained and comprised within him.
<margin>C</margin>
Now it is no less true that these **arsenics** <note>Realgar</note> are not essentially created in man, but they are first prepared within man: arsenic, and gold, and **chyme** <note>original: "Chimus," here referring to a vital fluid or alchemical essence</note>—these three are one ore. Now each has a special kind and power: but because they stand together, unhealed, each has neither the power nor its property to fulfill. In man it is likewise so, that such a **horizon** <note>original: "Orizon," a boundary or limit of existence</note> lies there, but not in the powers; rather, that the complete creation is within man.

Now it follows further, that Art drives man through **Divine Providence** and **predestination**, so that man separates the gold, especially through his **lightning-bolt** <note>original: "Fulmen"</note>, likewise the **slag** <note>original: "Chiſchlacken"</note>, and thus the arsenic in the manner of smoke into a **sublimated body**. Thus he separates the gold especially, as a gold, in its **exaltation** <note>alchemical refinement</note>, and the chyme likewise, and the arsenic in its nature; thus each fulfills its power.

As is to be understood there, so likewise there is one in man who performs the office of the Arts, and prepares and completes such separations and destructions of the bodies. And although I call that same destroyer of bodies by a special name, previously unheard of, as **Archeus** <note>the internal "alchemist" or vital force that directs biological processes</note>. For medicine had not reached so far among the philosophers that they would have understood who the destroyer in nature was, or from what ground the knowledge of disease arises. Note this: that the same **Archeus** in man performs all the **Vulcanic arts** <note>alchemy/chemistry, named for Vulcan, god of the forge</note>, orders, sends, and fits all things by virtue of the arts given by God into his essence, each into its **final matter** <note>original: "letzte Materia"</note>. For that is the final matter, when a thing stands alone in itself and rejoices in its exaltation, in the same way as gold which is separated from the other two, as mentioned.

# The Second Book of Great Things
## Chapter XII (Continued)

And when a counsel or plan is touched upon, it immediately falls into its progression, and establishes an exit and a center in that very place. Then, when the Realgar <note>A term used by Paracelsus to describe various toxic, arsenic-like mineral substances that cause corrosive diseases.</note> attaches itself there, it begins to create sores, breaking open, collapsing, burning, tormenting, and eating away at everything around it, gnawing further either into the depths or the surroundings, according to the German language. Whatever is in the face or neck, that same thing is called *Syren* <note>original: "Syren"; likely referring to a "siren" or "serpent-like" eating sore/lupus.</note> or "The Eating," and whatever is on the front or back of the body, one calls by the name *Cancer*: and whatever is below the belt, that is called in common country-German *St. Rüris* or *St. John’s Penance* or *The Smoke*: for the reason that it was held to be a plague that no human could help, unless he be a saint—that is, unless he be more than the physicians of old.

So know now also, that it sometimes happens that marks or similar buds grow for another reason, not harmful, but rather useful: However, these are often undertaken to be driven away by the so-called physicians, through cauterizing or cutting, and subsequently the aforementioned plagues and damages follow, which would not have come if the so-called physicians had not shared their unfathomable "art." Such, however, is its nature, that they do not arise unless the Realgar has a property and nature from the Salts <note>original: "Salibus"</note>; where such external oppositions meet it, it is ignited, and from such cauterizing or cutting it perceives an "air" <note>A draft or opening.</note> which it follows, and acts further according to the nature of its villainy, in every way as was mentioned above regarding the Realgar of metals. Thus you should also know that there is yet another kind of Realgar, besides the two mentioned; that same Realgar comes from Rice, some from Talc, some from Pearl <note>original: "Margarita"</note>, some from Bismuth <note>original: "Wißmat"</note>, some from Antimony, some from *Cachimia* <note>An imperfect metallic ore or slag.</note> and the like from others more. But since their healing goes into the aforementioned cures <note>original: "Curas"</note>, it is not necessary to write specifically about them.

### CHAPTER XIII.
->Tells of the transmuted damages, which are transformed from one being into another.<-
<sig>B</sig>
Now I must proceed further regarding a special kind, which I prove to you through examples. Just as man externally in the Great World <note>The Macrocosm/Universe.</note> knows many kinds of art—to change one thing into another that was not there before, and can through the art of preparation destroy external bodies and make them into other bodies and beings: as may be understood through raw and transmuted honey, how far they are from one another in both body and being—so it is with the Small World <note>The Microcosm/The Human Body.</note>, since the greatest treasure of man lies within him and not outside him, and what acts externally comes from within. And since this is the matter from which he is made, and he sees himself externally in the Light of Nature, he should recognize himself internally: who then would deny that which I rightly present in this chapter?

So now, just as one can prepare outside of man—nature against nature—and the art comes from within, and is the trial, and the trial receives experience from the outside, and thus the art grows, as the trial goes out of the Small World and works so long until it comes to the proof: who then would blame me if I mentioned that work also goes on inside the Small World of man, just as well as outside? That also internally, nature transmuted against nature, changed and made other beings. For more lies in the internal than in the external. Also, man is twofold: as his person is a worker in the Great World, so within him is also the Small World, and in that same world he has his spirit, which is the "Other Man." Thus, that same spirit works the art and adornment of man, just as well as man works in the external world: thus man works outside and inside. And if I called that same spirit *Adech* <note>Paracelsus's term for the inner creative spirit or "inner archeus" that directs the body's functions.</note> for the sake of distinction, who would blame it? Thus understand that man works in two places: through his person, and through his laborer, *Adech*.
<sig>C</sig>
Thus, according to this, there are externally certain Salts <note>original: "Salia"</note> which are made by art: such as the Alkalis and Sublimated Salts, which are prepared through compositions, which must also be. For Nature has not created enough for all arts in simples <note>original: "Simplicibus"; single-ingredient medicinal herbs or minerals.</note>, but has left it to Art, that it may put things together according to Nature, and destroy the same, and prepare for itself another, making it a "simple" for its purpose. Thus many kinds of simples are made, from which subsequently a composite <note>original: "Compositum"</note> is made, which does more and differently than Nature was able to do on her own. For Art is another Nature, also a special world. Since now such is sufficiently understood in the Great World, this is only a figure <note>An illustration or metaphor.</note> that in the Small World, through the *Adech*, such undertakings also exist, from which internally all kinds of diseases grow, which are necessary to mention here. Certain types of special damages grow which were mentioned in the previous chapters, because they are not from the simples of Nature, but are prepared artificially from the composite; and it is right that they should have their own page.

As mentioned, man can perform good or evil arrangements externally, and so also internally: and according to how he occupies a place or site, he carries out his work internally, and in that same place...

<sig>A</sig>
Should there not then be such powers in Heaven? For there is nothing in all things that is not also in the Firmament. Thus, life is drawn out of man, as is health, and whatever the concordance <note>The harmonious connection between the microcosm (man) and macrocosm (universe)</note> may encompass.

This includes all those injuries that defy common healing. Rather, they have their own Rule, which has grown solely out of **Astronomical Medicine**. For the Heaven works in man, be it for good or evil. For as a constellation is, so the constellation acts accordingly. If the Heaven can give snow, rain, thunder, and lightning, and can—according to the content of the weather and the time—make man weaker or sicker, and can toss him back and forth like a reed in the wind: then it is sufficiently proven that it can do not only the one, but also the other. For if it proves itself in the lesser, it also proves itself in the greater. But that Galen <note>Claudius Galenus, the ancient Greek physician whose theories dominated medieval medicine</note> does not think of the celestial diseases of the Heaven is more a shame to him than a praise, and he and his followers are the less to be trusted and believed.

### CHAPTER XV.

->Speaks of the injuries which, like a spring from a rock, have their flow.<-

<sig>B</sig>
So that the open sores may also be understood, which take their origin in the same way as a spring, consider some examples, and they are thus: Whether the Heaven or the Earth gives the spring cold or heat, it is found that just as a rock makes the water warm, so also there are fiery stars which transmit their effect into the Earth in such a manner. For nothing from the Earth is cold or warm unless it is so by the power of the Heaven. Even if some greater strengthening is added from the Earth, it is nevertheless originally given by the Heaven; moreover, in the creation of all things, such essences were separated from one another. Whatever belongs to heat or warmth, in Heaven or from Earth, was joined together. Likewise, whatever belongs to cold, and the like.

Thus you shall also understand that the physical [ailments] in open sores also have a union with the **Celestial Operation**, which cannot easily be separated from one another. Although man may not live otherwise than he intends, he cannot turn it away with the medicine of which Galen and Avicenna <note>Ibn Sina, the influential Persian physician</note> had no knowledge. For they do not even know how to heal a dog bite, let alone the celestial ones.

<sig>C</sig>
Thus they grow upon man, in the same way as springs out of a rock: no one knows how they grow into their origin. We know the origin of other growths, for the cause is proven by the seed and the planting. But in the origin of springs it is not so: for they run on and on, give no seed, but wait for the end of the world. The same is to be understood of the physical [sores], since they have no seed and do not take their effect from the man. Therefore it is proper to seek other medicine than what other open sores require. For the difference is great between those that grow from seed and those that spring up without seed. Man is upon the Earth, therefore he also has its properties in him. For if *Flammula* <note>Spearwort or Buttercup, known to cause blisters</note> and *Linum Aquaticum* <note>Water-flax</note> can grow on the Earth and raise great blisters on man, so also can such a growth spring up on man. For everything that is a property of the Earth is also in man: and that which does not harm the Earth harms man, because of his sensitivity.

As it is with the physical [sores], they bring it with them just like the springs. Now the types of springs are manifold, cold and warm, and have strange attachments, none like the other, also manifold types and properties. This is so that it may be known that such arrangements are also to be noted in physical [sores], and that for the sake of healing. For they differ in healing: some are of the cold, some are of the cold that puts to sleep; for all these are [types] and properties to be noted in healing. And although the physical [sores] are not [easily stopped], since no one can take the flow from the water, nor can anyone dig away the source of the spring like a root that comes from a seed: yet it is granted to man that no one can say that healing has been denied to him. Although according to the advice of other "Serpents" <note>A derogatory play on "servants" or "learned men" who Paracelsus believes are poisonous or deceptive</note> such will not be possible: but according to the advice taken from the **Celestial Influence**, it may well be. In other ways, it is understood in healing that you should understand this chapter well, so that you do not use the common course of medicine in such cases, as Galen and his like—the ignorant ones of the origin—have brought much useless chatter and rattling in their advice, which agrees less than fire and water.

# CHAPTER XVI.
Concerning Open Sores which arise from Wounds, Bone Fractures, Animal Bites, Burns, or from other Venomous Creatures.

Although other types of open sores occur outside of the aforementioned causes, they often arise following wounds, bone fractures, animal bites, or burns. This happens because the nature of the disease's corruption, or other accidents befalling the wound, causes them to be poorly managed with appropriate medicine at the site of the injury. Consequently, they suffer various complications. Just as when an eggshell is broken, the foreign air enters and corrupts the interior of the egg; so it is with man. As soon as he receives an opening in his body from the outside, without an internal cause, the external elements join with the internal ones. These two cannot stand alongside one another, for man—compared to the internal—is to be reckoned as a sensitive element, like a coarse pebble <note>original: "Rißling"</note> compared to a shining carbuncle <note>A glowing red gemstone, often used as a metaphor for purity or the soul</note>. Therefore, the coarse and the impure quickly poison and defile the pure and the fine, just as a clean, delicate cloth is quickly stained.

<margin>A</margin> Note this also: since the impure and the coarse stain the subtle and the pure, and since the impure always overpowers the pure—and man is the pure being while the [external] elements are the coarse and impure—it is right that one should prevent the external essence from entering the internal, especially when the firmament transforms the elements.

<margin>B</margin> When a man is opened, whether by weapons, fire, fractures, or animal bites, the external essence may enter the internal and poison it, so that it falls into a different state, similar to the aforementioned egg. Therefore, medicine is designed to intervene and act as a wall between them, so that this does not happen. But if the medicine were not created for this purpose, but were as unskillful as the external elements, the corruption would become even worse and more rapid.
Note also this: that the rot which arises from the external elements in the internal parts, or the rot which arises through bad medicine, turns into a rupture. In the same way, a rot occurs there as happens in a fresh egg; this rot persists until everything attacked by the external elements is removed, and only then can the uninjured parts be treated. These external effects of the elements must be understood, for they require a different medicine than what has been mentioned for other open sores. This is because the elements are of a different essence, nature, and property than the <term>pressures</term> <note>original: "preffiones" (likely *pressiones*), referring to internal pressures or humors</note> previously discussed. Therefore, the process held by the writers <note>The "Scribenten" or academic authorities of the time</note> is unjust, as they attribute all causes to the four humors and yet know nothing of how to prove it through works. The reason is that there are more and different causes than they imagine. One might well observe that if open sores arose exactly as they say, they would be able to cure them. But since there are other causes, their claims remain unproven, and no further heed is paid to what the elements do. In the same way that the internal body is poisoned by the external elements through various diseases, even unto death, so too can wounds be poisoned in this manner.

<margin>C</margin> Furthermore, it should be noted that if the external weapons are poisonous or united with the elements, the matter is all the more perilous. As with animal bites, which cause a faster poisoning of the internal and external elements; therefore, more care is especially necessary at that site. Likewise, even if a wound does not go all the way through, but through bad medicine it loses its health, or if a bone fracture receives an opening by itself or through other traction, a mixing with the external elements occurs. These elements are invisible and unfathomable, and they produce such a rot that is not easily removed. Therefore, it is proper to understand the origin of such open sores, so that the site may be treated according to the elements—that is, through their specific medicine. For just as a medicine is created for a wound according to its nature and property, so must that which is ordained and created against the specific evil always be used. And where the physician does not understand this, but always wants to "extinguish fire with water," he creates an error in the medicine and the destruction of the patient. Evil shall be driven out with evil, provided that the [medicinal] evil is specifically ordained against that [disease] evil.

As an example: the heart has within it a special constellation, just as the internal spirit, the <term>Archeus</term> <note>The internal "alchemist" or vital force that governs an organ's health</note>, is to be reckoned and compared against the external. So also in the womb there is a sidereal power, which...

### CHAPTER XX.
Concerning Leprosy <note>original: "Auffaß" - a historical term for leprosy or similar skin-rotting diseases</note>, and how it is born.

To further describe the origin and source of the leprous <term>decay</term> <note>original: "Feulung" - putrefaction or rotting</note>, first note the distinction between this <term>decay</term> and others. The leprous <term>decay</term> is a forsaken <term>body</term> <note>original: "Corpus"</note>, abandoned by the <term>salt</term> and <term>balsam</term> <note>In Paracelsian medicine, "Balsam" is the internal preservative fluid that prevents the body from rotting while alive</note> of the human being; yet it still has life within it, along with the other two parts, <term>sulfur</term> and <term>liquor</term> <note>fluid</note>. Other types of <term>decay</term> occur together with the <term>salt</term> and <term>balsam</term>, which is why they are less harmful. Regarding this, it should be known that where the <term>balsam</term> contains life, and man is placed in such varied states of destruction, there is such a distinction between them: when the <term>salt</term> departs, it forces the others at that same place, which are then <term>conditioned</term>. And whatever those two <note>sulfur and liquor</note> generate without the <term>salt</term>, that becomes <term>leprosy</term>; it appears in many forms, no two alike, and yet it is nothing but <term>decay</term>.

A. This <term>decay</term> receives a poison within it according to its <term>condition</term>. For just as a craftsman does not make the same <term>work</term> every day, but changes it as often as there is a newly born style, so it is in the <term>destruction</term> of man: one case follows another, this <term>leprosy</term> being one way, that one another. This is attributed solely to such an innate nature, which has only one origin and cause, but manifests in many ways. Thus <term>leprosy</term> is a <term>decay</term> that has grown without <term>salt</term> and <term>balsam</term>, worked and operated through <term>sulfur</term> and <term>liquor</term>, in such a way that these two—when without the third—produce no other <term>sickness</term> but <term>leprosy</term> alone. Although no other origin is to be understood, it is also possible for such <term>salt</term> to be poisoned and taken away, so that the <term>salt</term> is no longer transformed into anything else by the heavenly <term>influence</term> <note>astrological or divine forces</note>, which is the most painful <term>leprosy</term>. Sometimes the <term>balsam</term> of the body freezes through great cold, whether dry or wet, and shatters itself through that same frost, like wine that has frozen and can never return to its original essence: and so it is where that frost has occurred.

B. Likewise, some <term>leprosy</term> is born in the places of conception; and whatever is born from that same seed results in a leprous fruit, which cannot be blamed on the parents or prevented. But where the <term>balsam</term> is destroyed and no <term>balsam</term> remains, there no <term>medicine</term> is accepted; it behaves like a tree that rots in one place. What has rotted away, nature cannot bring back; nor can the physician. And just as little as a piece of burnt wood that has turned to ash can return to its middle creation, so little can a physician bring this destroyed <term>balsam</term> back to its function. If they could attack the whole body in the Three First Principles <note>Salt, Sulfur, and Mercury</note> as well as the <term>balsam</term>, they might remove the <term>decay</term>, just as a dead body is removed from the earth. For its undertaking is a wonderful and strange effect, which does not always attack the whole body, but sometimes only specific limbs, or sometimes only the lungs, or sometimes only a hand. Yet it is so poisonous that it drives its poison through the whole body and makes it insensible <note>numb</note>, one part or more, according to the power of the malice. For first, whatever is to die from the <term>leprosy</term> is earnestly put to sleep; but this sleep is an insensibility, not of a natural kind, but from the leprous <term>infection</term>, for which there is no help.

C. The <term>balsam</term> that loses the <term>leprosy</term> <note>likely meaning the body losing its balsam to leprosy</note> does not lose the weight of its body but remains in full quality. However, that which is the <term>balsam</term> within it is taken away and consumed. Just as an official who is removed from his office remains nonetheless the same old <term>body</term>, but no longer possesses the old power. So it is here. Although the <term>body</term> remains, every <term>saline body</term> is that which gives the form and shape. From this it follows that in the place where the <term>balsam</term> once was, damage, blisters, boils, knots, and other such strange patterns appear, according to the nature of the place where it breaks out. Thus, in form, no <term>leprosy</term> can be like another, being a <term>sickness</term> that could possibly exist in all animals. Man, however, is subject to <term>destruction</term> through <term>sickness</term> and <term>misery</term>; other animals are subject to blows and being strangled alive. And although other animals are also burdened with <term>sicknesses</term>, that is to be reckoned more as a punishment from God than attributed to Nature. For food was created pure by God. Although in the sow <term>leprosy</term> also appears, and that naturally; the reason is that she most closely resembles man. But regarding the <term>leprosy</term> of men, there is not much more to describe, because it can neither be prevented nor healed. However, what occurs through freezing, <term>preservation</term> will not freeze. Likewise, what the heavenly <term>influence</term> gives through the medicine of...

# Preface to the Third Treatise.

<sig>B</sig>

->**A**s the greatest little berry <note>original: "Beerlin." A metaphor for a small but precious fruit or seed</note>, and the noblest treasure is Healing, which in all medicine is above everything, and there is nothing on Earth that is greater, by all considerations regarding medicine, than healing the sick: And that has its reasons. It is a Commandment from God: You shall love God; that is the highest Good, above which nothing may exist in man. The second is: You shall love your neighbor as yourself; that is now the greatest after the first.<-

Now what is there on Earth toward one's neighbor in which more love may be shown than when a man, grounded in true love, recognizes the medicine of healing, and turns away from his neighbor his great pain, sickness, and death, through the power of medicine? Since God has created him for such love, there is nothing that is a greater love than to prevent death for one's neighbor, and to lengthen and extend his life, which God has thus ordained; and for men to take away such pain, to turn away the frailty of his body, and to bring him again into his power and strength, so that he may accomplish for God that for which he was born: which a sick man may not fulfill, [who suffers] and passes away.

Now you sick ones, be mindful of how great a gift and grace from God it is, that you (and the greater part of you) fall into the sicknesses of Open Sores because of your sins—as is proven by the French Disease <note>term: French Disease (Frantsofen). A common 16th-century name for Syphilis.</note>—and regardless of the malice and evil, He also allows medicine to be found: so that you stand up again, like Lazarus from death, from your rotting, stinking, ruinous sores and holes, into a healthy, capable body. The Physician <note>original: "Artist." Paracelsus views the healer as an artist of nature.</note> is your neighbor, and God is His neighbor. Should not such an art in medicine be thought of as great? What is more, what is greater? What is more useful? Or what is above a healthy body among temporal things? Nothing. Since you physicians are the neighbors of the sick, and should love them as yourselves, then hold yourselves as faithfully toward them as the Samaritan in Jericho, who not only shared his wine and oil as a medicine with the wounded man, but also his horse, his money, and all his security. Look at this, O you physicians all, whether medicine be an art for cooks, or given to women for vanity; judge and weigh it, for you shall be brought to account for it. How miserable and beyond miserable a thing it is now, when medicine and healing are thus the Highest Good, and yet by the fictional, presumed Sophists <note>Paracelsus uses "Sophists" to describe university-trained doctors who rely on logic rather than experience</note> are treated with malice and resentment...

## The First Part on the Healing
### of Open Wounds, by DOCTOR
->PARACELSUS.<-
->CHAPTER I.<-

Regarding the Tinctures that govern, renew, and rejuvenate the blood in humans.

<margin>B</margin> The philosophers <note>In this context, "philosophers" refers to natural philosophers or early scientists/alchemists.</note> have meditated upon long life and held long life to be a great treasure, in which they were neither fit for nor desirous of wars and bloodshed. Thus, they took great diligence in how they might sustain life. This drove them into the art of nature to experience those same powers, as has frequently happened, and they gathered together what lay in the mystery and nature of things. They separated themselves from those who were enemies of the wise and kept together. Thereupon, they sought a true and complete foundation in the preparation of things and powers from the alchemists, and found indications among them. There arose the preparation of medicine; there the philosophers and the alchemists lived together and took antimony <note>original: "Antimonium"</note> under their spurs <note>A metaphor for putting something to work or accelerating its use.</note>. For thus, with time, arts were found one after another, and such wonders that there was nothing left to do but to seek and find daily, sparing no diligence or labor.

In this search, as they sought in alchemy, it happened that wonderful things occurred through daily experience of medicine, pertaining to long life. Among others, these following pieces also appeared, in which they experienced great wonders; namely, God has endowed the blood with such properties. The following "Gold-makers" and "Moon-makers" <note>original: "Aurices, Lunifices" – terms for alchemists attempting to create gold and silver.</note> have broken in and understood this. What the light of nature works and is capable of is easy to grasp. I will let that same matter rest here, but I will take up as much as concerns health. The opinion has grown that if a change is made in metals, and one essence is transformed into another—a rough, coarse, impure one into a pure, subtle, healthy one, etc.—they also saw the "flowers" of metals, which they created nobler than the metals themselves, and other generations. And through these, many works and good things happened, and they meditated further upon these things.

<margin>C</margin> And because the heavens were also in harmony, and man was unstained, those things were created which they called Tinctures <note>Concentrated medicinal solutions, often believed to have transformative powers.</note>, and these sufficed for human health and demonstrated wonders through them. As the very old scraps of writing <note>original: "Scartecklin"</note> indicate, and the experience of my associates and my own has been at hand, it was found that the blood is purified by such Tinctures. The "sophistical" doctors <note>Paracelsus used "sophist" as a derogatory term for traditional academic doctors who relied on old books rather than nature.</note> lay idle for years and days, and it has come to pass that I, to their mockery, intend to reveal the Tincture in its powers. It is greatly to be lamented that medicine has fallen among the sophists and such noble virtue and power have been neglected. I consider that there is a cause for this, or perhaps God does not wish it to be.

Since I am laboring here to write about open wounds and present my art, which I have experienced in many ways: know then a distinction in my foundation and beginning. Such arts are known, but they are blurred by the process of transforming into gold and silver, which should not be. I have separated those from the ones pertaining to health. Furthermore, many errors have crept in through writings, through transpositions, and through omissions; I have also put those away. It also happened that through such searching, the arts were changed and went in other directions. For people never let themselves be satisfied with the first discovery, but sought further to improve and strengthen it, etc., and it became worse and weaker than it was at first, and thus the original was forgotten. I have also corrected this and it stands in its original foundation of essence. Whoever then seeks further, let him look at it; for to build and seek in a minor, inexperienced way cannot end with profit.

So that I may also instruct you on how it is possible for me to do this, you should understand it thus: from childhood I have pursued these things and learned from those who were the most grounded in the Adept Philosophy <note>The secret or "inner" knowledge of alchemy and nature.</note> and were powerfully grounded in the arts. Firstly, Wilhelm von Hohenheim, my father, who never forsook me. Thereafter and along with him...

...to him a great number, which is not easily estimated, together with various writings of the ancients and the moderns, who have exerted themselves: such as <term>Bishop Schenk of Stertzgach</term>, <term>Bishop Erhart of Hippo</term> <note>original: "Yppon"</note>, <term>Bishop Matthæus Schacht</term>, <term>Suffragan Bishop Nicolaus of Spanheim</term>, and more of the like, and many among the other doctors of Freising <note>original: "Physingen"</note>. ### CHAPTER II.

->How the <term>Tincture</term> is separated from <term>Gold</term> for medicine, to be used in open sores and to take away the outbreak.<-

<insert>T</insert>he <term>Tincture</term> of <term>Gold</term> is solely the color of the gold: If this same color is taken away, and its <term>Body</term> <note>original: "Corpus"</note> remains white, separated from the color, then all things are prepared for the formulation. The <term>Body</term> and color are two things, and may be separated, and thus they are of the <term>Pure</term> <note>original: "Neine"</note>, that is, the colors from the <term>Aurelien</term>, which is the body. Where this separation does not first occur, but both are undertaken together, that is an error, and cannot come to perfect power. Thereafter, when this has happened, the color, which is the <term>Tincture</term>, shall be <term>Clarified</term> and exalted into its <term>Grade</term> <note>original: "Gradum"</note>, which doubles itself five times, that is, five times into two times [to the power of] twelve. It rises no higher; that is how far the <term>Tincture</term> is brought, and further it cannot be. Accordingly, when it is thus made and ready, it shall be administered, for it is written concerning the administration. This is the highest purification of the blood in all sores, to take them at the outbreak, and through the <term>Tincture</term> to bring the whole limb into a new, healthy being.

### To bring this about, it happens in this way.

First, the <term>Body</term> shall be broken out of its <term>Metallic nature</term> and <term>Malleability</term> <note>original: "Maleation"</note> by <term>Salt Water</term> <note>original: "Aquam Salis"</note>: Then wash the <term>Residue</term> <note>original: "Residencs"</note> with <term>Sweet Water</term> <note>original: "Aqua dulci"</note>: After that, draw up the colors with <term>Spirit of Wine</term> <note>original: "Spiritu Vini"; concentrated alcohol</note>, and finally elevate the <term>Spirit</term> from the color, so it remains at the bottom.
The <term>Salt Water</term> is made thus: Take molten <term>Salt</term> that is the purest and whitest, by its own nature, without cooking, boiling, or other added arts by which salt is made, and let it flow several times: Then, having flowed small, and well beaten, then distill it after its resolution, and mixed with the <term>Sanguinea</term> <note>Likely a reference to a red mineral or "blood-stone" preparation</note> while it is green, and distilled at equal weight for the fifth time; then in the same, <term>Leaves of Gold</term> <note>original: "Lamina Solis"</note> purified by <term>Antimony</term> are dissolved into a <term>Powder</term>.

Wash that same [powder] with pure distilled <term>Water</term> until no more <term>Salt</term> is found, for the <term>Salt</term> leaves and does not essentially or permanently attack the substance, but separates away again; therefore it is separated as a hindrance, and becomes sweet, as it should be in itself.
The <term>Spirit of Wine</term> is made thus: Take a measure of <term>Wine</term>, the strongest and not [necessarily] the best tasting, and place it in a <term>Circulatory Vessel</term> <note>original: "Circulatorium"</note> of a size appropriate to the measure, so it may move well. This <term>Circulatory Vessel</term> should be in a <term>Water Bath</term> <note>original: "Balneum Maris"</note> according to the depth the <term>Wine</term> occupies, and then let it stand for seven days, closed and well-sealed; then put it in a <term>Vial</term>, distill it cold; when it gives its sign, then stop immediately. For what follows is <term>Burning Spirit of Wine</term> <note>original: "Bras-spiritu Vini"</note>; pour this onto the <term>Residue</term>, which is like an <term>Alcohol</term> <note>In this context, a fine powder</note>, so that it rises six fingers above it, and seal it well in a fine glass: Then let it stand in a <term>Warm Bath</term> <note>original: "Balneo calido"</note> for one month, so the color comes into the <term>Spirit</term>, and a white <term>Powder</term> remains at the bottom; let that [powder] melt, so a <term>Metallic Water</term> comes from it, and let the <term>Spirit</term> evaporate as the art requires, so a juice remains like a <term>Liquor</term> at the bottom.

# Wound Medicine: The Third Treatise.

## Wound Medicine: The Third Treatise.

<margin>A</margin>Furthermore, once that has been accomplished, you should perform the grading <note>Grading refers to the alchemical process of increasing the "grade" or potency and purity of a substance.</note> for the fifth time through its own retorts, according to the smallness of the substance and matter. Although it is true that such grading occurs solely through elevation <note>sublimation or rising of vapors</note> and the making of the substance subtle, do not allow it to be brought beyond the "Fifth Essence" <note>The Quintessence, or the purest medicinal core of a material</note>; that is to say, at 4.0, it would be further burnt away. Its use follows in the section on administration.

### CHAPTER III.
### How the Tincture is taken from Corals, also to cleanse the blood from the highest impurity.

So also is the color of corals the medicine and tincture to cleanse the blood. For in red corals there is a mystery and secret <note>original: "Mysterium vnd Arcanum"</note>, the likes of which are not many. And thus, in the virtues of one who uses them, it will not be possible for leprosy, impurity, or other unhealthiness to be found in his blood. It cleanses and clarifies the blood to such an extent that no open sore can work or remain internally, whether it be in whatever veins it chooses within the body or in the external limbs.

Now, corals are such in their tincture that only that which has colored them should be taken; that same thing is the tincture, and not the body <note>the physical dross or bulk of the coral</note>. Therefore, it is a matter of high consideration for a physician that the tincture be taken from those things that have their power within the tincture. As those things meant for the blood are most highly gifted in their color alone, therefore the color should be taken from the corals and graded into its exaltation <note>the highest state of medicinal power</note>.

<margin>B</margin>First, when this is to happen, it occurs by crushing its body into a subtle alcohol <note>In this context, "alcohol" refers to an extremely fine, impalpable powder</note>, thereafter the colors are extracted through the spirit of wine <note>distilled ethanol</note>, then the preparation is brought into its highest grade, and then used according to the instructions for administration.

### And the preparation of the Arcanum occurs in this way.

Now, as has been said regarding the extraction of the colors from gold, so it also happens with red corals. But when you have them thus, you must let them [distill] together sixteen times, and at the last, draw it off. Its ascent should happen in a bare fire <note>direct heat</note>, then draw it off in a water bath <note>original: "Balneo"</note>, poured over again six times, and keep the oil, and administer it through the Theriac Water <note>original: "Aquam Tyriacalem," a medicinal water based on Theriac, a famous ancient polypharmaceutical compound</note>; that is, in the same small measure <note>original: "Quintlein"</note> according to further indication of its ordained use.

And the Theriac Water is made thus: Take ten ounces of spirit of wine, five ounces of Theriac, two and a half ounces of red Roman Myrrh, half an ounce of Saffron from the Orient; mix it and distill it together once. Thereafter, do to it as stands above and is presented in the administration. And you should also know that when such a Coral Mystery is taken, it heals every fistula, cancer, "syren" <note>likely referring to a type of spreading ulcer or "serpent-like" sore</note>, etc.; it also heals the "wolf" <note>lupus or a devouring ulcer</note> at its very source. For such secrets and gifts can well find them at their origin.

### CHAPTER IV.
### How the Tincture is extracted from the Balsam and prepared in its highest virtue.

<margin>C</margin>It happens many times that those with open wounds—if they have suffered and endured such for a long time and are chronically ill, damaged for a long time by much medicine and pain—that it happens to them (even though the source might and may be renewed) that the site gives way to a rotting, and has grown into something like a leprosy at the source and is transformed into the same. Even if the medicine were suited <gloss>to</gloss> regenerate and renovate, the rot at that place does not helpfully allow it to enter. Where such is the case, its secret <note>Arcanum</note> must be administered out of the power of the Balsam. For only through the Balsam are those preserved who are heading toward such rot, or otherwise producing ulceration at the source. Where a corrosive nature also runs with it, it is healed; moreover, Balsam is of a nature the likes of which is not found in others.

Now its preparation and exaltation is thus: that you take one ounce of it and forty ounces of spirit of wine, and put both into a circulation vessel <note>original: "Circulatorium"</note>, and let it circulate in the sun for one month. Thereafter, let it be distilled through the alembic, which is better than a retort in this instance. And then this mixture shall remain in a composition, and you shall add to it another ounce of Balsam, and thus leave it well-sealed to digest <note>original: "Digerieren," a slow heating process</note>, so it mixes the same into itself so that it becomes perfected. For every thing that is to be graded must lose its essence in the physical body.

Furthermore, if that same thing is volatile, put another ounce into it again, and just as before, four ounces may thus be taken out and exalted into its highest grade. This is a great preparation of the Balsam, which leaves nothing suspended in the whole body that it does not penetrate and overpower, turning away all destruction and maintaining it in health. Although the destruction is subject to the medicine. For God is He who breaks, who...

# The Second Book of the Great
Physician who makes it whole again: Thus God wishes to let His wonders be seen, and wills that we have a knowledge of the secrets of Nature—what He has created within them for the benefit of man, who is surrounded by infirmity. Therefore, the physician should not be idle, but should practice his art, since all trades use these same secrets and often find in them the best, most useful, and most skillful applications, such as for <note>original: "merleut" - likely referring to mariners or perhaps a specific guild</note>, stone-cutting, etc. The physician is much more obligated to do such things.

->CHAPTER V.<-

->Concerning the Tincture of Antimony, how the same should be extracted for the health, renovation, and regeneration of man in open sores.<-

<margin>B</margin>
Although the physician must recognize the nature and power of all things, and thus should explore the art of medicine from the outward powers that Nature displays. As an example from Antimony <note>original: "Antimonio"</note>, whose nature and medicinal power have been found to be such that nothing cleanses gold except Antimony alone; and it leaves no impurity in the gold, cleansing and purifying it, for the impurity must depart from the gold. Since Nature shows and proves this to us, the indication is a challenge to the physician that he should take pains to learn from it: if you do this in gold, what then is your power and <term>Arcanum</term> <note>A secret, powerful medicinal essence or "inner mystery" of a substance</note> in man? For it will manifest itself in the same way. For this is a <term>Mysterium</term> <note>A divine or natural mystery</note> that lies before our eyes; it is right that we use it not as goldsmiths do, but as physicians. From this follows the preparation, in such a form that a Tincture is made from Antimony, and that it be prepared into a medicine, so that it may do the same in man as it does in gold. And just as it cleanses in gold, so it cleanses in man.

For an example: Nettles <note>original: "Neßlen"</note>, Spearwort <note>original: "Flammule"</note>, and Spanish Fly <note>original: "Cantharides"</note> manifest their effects openly, so that they cause scarring and burn up blisters. Now this is an external proof of their fine powers: but if they are prepared through the art of <term>Alchemy</term> <note>original: "Alchimiam"</note>, they do much more; they do not merely put water into a blister, but draw out—even before that water—every flux and condition that essentially lies there. The magnet attracts iron to itself: if it is prepared through alchemy, it attracts closed and fallen iron, even that which is neglected. <insert>And when it is finally reverberated, then take it and draw out its essence.</insert> Regarding the handling of these things, I have left it for the *Minor Surgery*. But every physician should know that Nature displays a power outwardly, and thereafter, to use it for the benefit of man, she points to the art of alchemy to possess that power.

<margin>C</margin>
Yet there is an insight now to be known: Antimony cleanses only gold; other metals it consumes entirely, and it itself loses great weight. Thereupon it is now to be known: Man is in the same way as gold, and is compared to gold in all his being and powers; therefore it cleanses man, just as it does gold, to his health and highest degree. Other things it consumes entirely, whether it be <unclear>something</unclear> or that which purges certain things, and certain things it loses entirely. This Antimony is a <term>Purgation</term> without bowel movement, which cleanses and purifies man in the most noble way, removing from the foundation everything it should take that makes man unclean, and purges him to his highest health: cleansing him from all sores or other diseases that may arise. The Philosophers <note>Referring to ancient alchemists and natural scientists</note> have dealt much with it and moved it in many ways: but the right way has not yet been found by them; rather, it is now brought to light, and it should rightly be an art that all physicians should know. For this cleansing is the entrance and beginning in all diseases, whatever they may be: and if it were used, so many would not be ruined as the "permanent" physicians ruin. For that reason I call them "supposed" physicians, because in all their things they only "suppose" <note>i.e., they guess or have opinions</note> and know nothing for certain, which is the highest mockery for any physician.

Now its preparation is thus: (but he who wishes to understand it must be subject to Alchemy, for I cannot bring it forth in a common apothecary manner). Take the Antimony, transformed into the very best <term>Alcohol</term> <note>In this context, a fine, purified powder</note>, then <term>Reverberate</term> <note>To heat in a furnace where the flames are reflected back onto the substance</note> it in a closed reverberatory furnace for one month; thus it will become a <term>Volatile</term> <note>A substance capable of being vaporized</note>, at first white, then yellow, and finally red of a brown color, light and subtle. When it is now red and finally reverberated, then take it and draw out its essence; <insert>when it is ready, separate it, and mix it with the Spirit of Wine <note>original: "Spiritum Vini" - concentrated alcohol</note>.</insert> This is the highest cleansing, and the most noble and praiseworthy, which stands above all else that man can find in man. If you find this medicine and Arcanum, there is no "supposed" physician, but a true knowledge. The Philosophers have sought much in Antimony, as have the Artists, but to have the foundation pure and clear—at the time of that discovery—they did not live to see it, for they died before me.

# Hundarney: The Third Treatise.
## CHAPTER VI.
### Concerning the Tincture, or the Salt of the Philosophers, and how the same is to be obtained.

The <term>Philosophers</term> <note>original: "Philosophi"; referring here to alchemists and natural philosophers</note> have sought the <term>Secrets</term> <note>original: "Arcana"; hidden medicinal powers</note> of natural things so rigorously and powerfully for the sake of health, that they have indeed discovered many of the arts. But due to a lack of perfect preparation, as well as a lack of complete knowledge, they were unable to reach the end. Therefore, it remains for us, living now, to seek and experience more, and not simply remain at their conclusion. For they did not reach the very end, but it was left to us; however, they gave the beginning and the true foundation which we should follow, seeking the end further. For there is a difference between the foundation and that which the humorists <note>physicians who follow the theory of the four bodily humors</note> lay down. Those same ones have long since reached their end, which is dead; for they only seek to finish, and that is very soon found. Therefore, they have nothing more to seek; their art is found.

Now, among the physicians of the right path, there were initially many lovers of the art who might have learned from them. But through negligence and contempt, that which would be more useful to us has not been preserved, whereby many noble arts must have been lost. First, they made a Salt, and in the same, they sought the highest foundation for health. For Salt lets nothing rot. Where such a <term>Preservative</term> or <term>Conservative</term> exists, how can man reach his end so soon, and not rather be more useful and better? Therefore, it is right to mention the <term>Salt of the Philosophers</term>. For 
<margin>B</margin>
there several of the principal <term>Secrets</term> come together: namely, the <term>Flowers of Antimony</term> <note>sublimated essences</note>, <term>Flowers of Gold</term>, <term>Flowers of Coral</term>, and that measured with salt in food. Also, not only in such things alone, but these men discovered how to make a salt out of every single thing; they have not so experienced and fathomed what might be in them, having also prepared a salt from them: from Melissa, from Celandine, from Angelica, from Irmiginia, and the like; and they took these together under one recipe and composed them into one, and then gave the same to the sick.

But now, because the discovery among the ancient first physicians was of many kinds, many kinds of recipes have also been ordered; therefore, there are many of them. From this it followed that as soon as a thing came into great renown, it could not remain without deception; thus, false recipes also came among the good ones. Therefore, one should take heed that names should mislead no one. Even if it is written "Salt of the Philosophers," do not believe it straight away, but you should have a <term>Judgment</term> <note>original: "Iudiciu"; the ability to discern</note> whether the <term>Secrets</term> indicate the name or not.

There is a saying from Solomon which says: "In a man of many words, sin is not lacking." For sin, take lies, deceit, and other such things; for the truth is contained in a small word and needs not much speaking; but as soon as a sea is to be made of it, then deception is born.

Now, at first, their recipes were such that they put good things together, as mentioned above. But yet, those same <term>Flowers of Antimony</term> are not to be accepted in the manner they are found in the <term>Philosophy</term>, as <term>Rupecilla</term> <note>Johannes de Rupescissa, a 14th-century alchemist</note> mentions, who cannot stop his chatter, nor the monk's cunning in the writings of the philosophers. Therefore, those same processes, and the process of the <term>Fifth Essence of Gold</term> <note>original: "Quinta Effentia Auri"</note>, are not in themselves as they see and describe them. That which the 
<margin>C</margin>
philosophers say is also not so, except it is to be noted that they used the same practice as <term>Raymond Lully</term> <note>famed medieval alchemist</note> sets down; and though Raymond has his foundation from them, it is not the final grasp in which to find the <term>Secrets</term>. It is sufficiently presented to us to seek further from one to the other as we are commanded. But I set down for you here two recipes for the Salt of the Philosophers, with their preparation; what is further may well be further understood and sought.

And the first is thus: of <term>Salt of Gold</term>, <term>Salt of Antimony</term>, <term>Salt of Melissa</term>, each <insert>take</insert> sixteen <term>Loht</term> <note>a unit of weight, approx. 15 grams</note> of rock salt; mix them together, and every morning take a portion given or more, and a little salt. And do not let it wonder you that I name <term>Salt of Gold</term> and <term>Salt of Antimony</term>, which yet are not salts: if you knew what you ought to know, it would not wonder you at all. The other recipe is: Take <term>Salt of Germander</term>, <term>Salt of Chicory</term>, <term>Salt of Valerian</term>, two <term>Loht</term> of each; 
<margin>X</margin>
<term>Salt of Wormwood</term> half a <term>Loht</term>, <term>Salt of Vitriol</term> one <term>Quintlein</term> <note>approx. 4 grams</note>, pure rock salt one pound; mix it, use it as stands above, etc. What further is needed, you will find in the <term>Administration</term> <note>instructions for use</note>.

### CHAPTER VIII.

->On the effect of the mentioned Tinctures, and their virtues.<-

Since man, among all sensitive animals, is alone the Gold, and is compared only to Gold: it is right that he be considered as Gold, and now also treated in that manner. For from this it follows that no impurity or filth should be taken from him in any other way than it is taken from Gold.

Where this is not considered, but it is understood [only] through purging and syruping, or "ersieren" <note>likely a local term for a specific type of evacuation or cautery</note>, in whatever way it may happen to cleanse the human being. # Surgery: The Third Treatise.

<margin>A</margin> To be considered. For example: If someone has an open sore, what does it help to daily purge him in his excrements <note>original: "in Stercoribus"; referring to the waste products of the body</note>, when the sickness does not come from them? What use is it to place him daily in abstinence <note>fasting or restricted diet</note>, when overindulgence <note>original: "Crapula"</note> did not cause the injury? If it is considered that only the "Tincture" <note>The vital inner essence or spiritual quality of a substance</note>—which is innocent in the sickness—is affected, then it is found that the other two <note>likely referring to the other Paracelsian principles like Salt or Sulfur</note> are left behind and remain unquestioned as those not guilty of the sickness.

Therefore, because the Destruction is more to be considered than the excrements, it should be recognized and reflected upon that Renovation <note>renewal/restoration</note> is more important than Purging. This is why I have written and presented these Destructions: because destiny, laxatives, and syrups are no cure for open sores unless the Tincture itself is renovated. Although it might happen that Nature renews itself—like the snake or the blackbird, which also renovate themselves—and in that same abstinence, the excrements of the Destruction would be added. But such healing happens through Renovation or abstinence: it happens all the sooner, however, if Nature is better managed.

<margin>B</margin> We have an example in Mercury, which is wonderful in its operations. Now you see, it is one that heals the open sores of the "French Disease" <note>Syphilis</note> and others, and that fundamentally from the roots. Through its virtue of purging, it makes one young; it is the "Overturner," it is that which renovates. Therefore, because it is the healer, it does much. Not that it possesses the "incarnative virtue" <note>original: "Virtus incarnativa"; the power to grow new flesh</note>. That is found in the Balsam of Nature: but it renovates and clarifies the body from all filth. Therefore, the natural Balsam follows after, more than Mercury can reach; where it should not go, it renovates nothing and heals nothing: as is explained and made understood in his book on this subject.

Upon this, it is now necessary that the Tinctures be considered, for they are what make a man—who cannot be a man—into one: That is, a man who has filth and the like in him is not worthy of a healthy man, nor equal to a man; he does not stand at the grade <note>level of perfection or purity</note> where he should be. When gold does not have its proper grade, it is purged and purified through antimony <note>original: "Antimonium"; a semi-metal used in alchemy to purify gold</note> so long and so often until it attains it and stands at the highest. So also should it happen with man: first he should become what he is meant to be, whether he stands high or low in his grade, and then his purification occurs through antimonial power—in whichever Tincture it is found—so that he attains his highest grade; then he is healthy in all his limbs.

Although these grades have been described by no one—which is a great folly—nothing is omitted by me in the *Archidoxis* paragraphs <note>Refers to Paracelsus's work "Archidoxis," concerning the mysteries of nature</note>. For once and for all, it must be that man has nothing impure in him; that is, as mentioned, there are two kinds of impurity: one of gold and one of nature. I speak only of the golden kind. For just as gold has a filth in itself that takes away its grade—and as it is taken from it by antimony and turned into dross in man—so is there such a filth in man also. Gold is fine and dries nothing, therefore man has all the more sickness in him from the same; I do not treat anything here except the excrements which lie in man as they do in gold. This is a reason why the minerals are compared [to man] because of the likeness and metaphor: also according to the Creation, since man is born of the earth.

<margin>C</margin> Therefore note: since a mineral cause is present, it may well be helpful for driving out and [healing] drinking bouts: also abstinence and good purging may help against hindrances. From this it may well follow that such mineral sicknesses can exist, but they do not last. The healing lies alone in mineral medicine where nothing else can act: which mineral medicine is only in Tinctures, such as in Antimony, in Gold <note>original: "Auro"</note>, and the like, also in Mercury, etc. And if the mineral medicine has accomplished its task in this way, then there is no need for purging or laxatives: those same wastes and excrements are consumed and taken away by themselves. Because I have used Renovation and Transmutation <note>The alchemical changing of one substance into another</note> through experience, and it has encountered me externally in the figure of the Microcosm <note>The "little world"; man as a reflection of the universe</note>, so it also arises perfectly in the human as in gold, which has this nature alone in itself and feels nothing else.

But such is the effect of the Tincture, as you see, that it purges and cleanses all filth from the clean: so also the Tinctures. And because in wood and the like there is no purity, man is figured [differently]; therefore it burns, and the gold—which is not [wood]—the antimony takes that [impurity] away entirely, so nothing remains. And so it is also obvious that there is a "Cement" <note>original: "Cementum"; a paste used in purifying and grading gold</note> that grades the gold to the highest: so also there are Cement-like things of the upper nature of Tinctures, which are themselves perfect and round. But all in such a form as mentioned: how fire and fire, and Tincture are one thing, and that they help each other to renovate and cleanse from all filthy mineral types, essences, and dross, in which the first and highest healing lies.

# The Second Book of Great Matters

### CHAPTER IX.

How the Tinctures should be given and used, each according to its nature, and how to recognize them by their signs.

## On the Administration of the Tincture of Gold.

The administration of the Golden Tincture to stop the destruction of open sores <note>original: "Offen Schäden," referring to chronic ulcers or non-healing wounds</note> is as follows: you must mix it, one quintlein <note>a small historical unit of weight, approx. 3.6 grams</note> into one ounce of the best Theriac <note>original: "Trior," a famous ancient poly-pharmaceutical herbal jam used as a universal antidote and carrier</note>; and thus give one scruple <note>approx. 1.3 grams</note> of this on an empty stomach, then cover the patient warmly so they may sweat. Now, know this method of administration: in such a dose, the source of the disease is changed, and whatever is useless and against nature takes its harm and carries that harm out—sometimes through bleeding, sometimes through other flows—so that the effect of the Tincture is found and seen within the open sore itself. You shall only continue the administration until the open sores no longer bleed or flow, which usually happens in ten or twelve days. Then you may easily heal all open sores with light and simple medicine. For thus, through the medicine, the source is taken away, and that which is useless is driven out through the open sore, where it is found as long as it remains there.

## On the Administration of the Tincture of Coral.

The administration of the Secret Remedy <note>original: "Arcani"</note> of Coral is this: you shall give it alone, mixed in water of Chicory or Germander <note>original: "Cichorea oder Gamandrea"</note>, three lot <note>approx. 45-50 grams</note> into twenty lot of water. Of this, give a half-lot weight to drink morning and night; in the morning after fasting for five hours, and five hours after the evening meal, and this for six or seven days in succession. During this time, you shall feed the sick with humble food, and little of it, placing them in great abstinence. For the sake of the sick, it would be best to drink only water of Fumitory <note>original: "Fumi terræ"</note>, Chicory, and the like, and no other. And when a powerful flow arises from the open sore, and when that happens and the sore thereafter becomes dry and loses its pain: then enough of the Tincture has been given. Cease its use upon the sores as they reveal and prove themselves. Then you may decrease or increase the Tincture accordingly.

## On the Administration of the Tincture of Balsam.

Every Tincture of Balsam should be handled thus: as it is in itself, five grains of wheat <note>a tiny measure of weight</note> should be given in old white wine as often as the patient eats—that is, a thousand times <note>likely a hyperbolic expression for "regularly/frequently"</note>. And this for so long until you notice such a dryness in the open sores that absolutely no moisture of any kind is there. For when the source is removed, healing occurs from the inside out. You should also know that the Tincture of Balsam heals the entire sore if you persist with the administration until the end, using only a little medicine alongside it to manage the discharge from the sore.

## On the Administration of the Tincture of Antimony.

To take the Tincture of Antimony, it is best when wine-must is put into a barrel, adding one lot of this Tincture to every twenty measures of wine, and thus letting them age together for three or four weeks, or longer, according to what you recognize as necessary. Its effect is such that it cleanses and purifies the sore, just as a surgeon works on wounds, and begins to grow new flesh <note>original: "incarnieren"</note> and close itself up; no matter what form the sore takes, it heals it like a fresh wound. You should use no external medicine for it, other than covering the sore with common plasters. I wish for my part that this were in use instead of all the apothecary and scribbled recipes <note>original: "Stribenten Recepten," likely a derogatory term for poorly written or overly complex prescriptions</note>; thus the medicine would be more honorable and the sick would not be led into noticeable ruin. For this is a miracle-drink <note>original: "Wundertranck"</note> for sores, to which nothing is equal.

## On the Tincture of the Salt of the Philosophers, how it is to be Administered.

This Salt is called a Salt because it is a Salt, and should be consumed like a Salt. Therefore, its use is that food should be salted with it. When this is done, the effect is such that it internally takes away and consumes the source, and

## Wound Medicine: The Third Treatise.

A. Through that same consumption <note>referring to the action of the medicine "consuming" diseased tissue</note>, the place and the site are purified of all poison, so that new, fresh, and healthy blood follows, from which the new flesh is generated: And it requires no other help than the salt alone. Although there are other tinctures: but this one does so much that no pimple, cancer, sore, nor ulcer <note>original: "Finel/Krebs/Syren"</note> can remain, whether it be young or old, and in whatever form it may be. For when the origin is taken away, the diseases of the origins are removed, incarnated <note>flesh-forming</note>, and consolidated <note>wound-closing</note> without adding anything else.

### CHAPTER X.
How health should be maintained, achieved, and conserved after healing has occurred.

S. Now, as has been mentioned, the healings have occurred, and yet a person who is healthy can fall into sickness, much more so one who was previously inclined toward and afflicted by diseases. Therefore, the conservation of the healthy person in such injuries should not be neglected. The conservation <note>preservation of health</note> is thus: that from the same tincture a proper dose is taken, according to the appearance and condition of the sick person, and that it be given at the beginning of Aries <note>the zodiac sign, marking the spring equinox</note> when the sun enters into it, and likewise to persevere in every way with the process as if the person still had open wounds, until they become even healthier. Thus you may take whichever tincture you wish, and proceed according to the demonstration as has been taught, and do this once every year, and do not neglect it.

Now it is no less true that there are many more tinctures, such as those of the Swallow-wort <note>original: "Irundinaria"</note>, of Mummy <note>a medicinal preparation of preserved flesh</note>, of Germander <note>original: "Gamandrea"</note>, and of Mercury, as their process and order are, though they are not specifically written here. For the Mummy is prepared like the Balsam; Swallow-wort and Germander are prepared like the Salt of the Philosophers <note>original: "Salc Philofophorum"</note> or the Antimony. However, because their effect is not so very strong, nor so powerfully mastered in their effects, I have omitted them here. The tincture of Mercury is excellent and a mighty secret: but it is included in the book on the *French Healing* <note>referring to the treatment of syphilis, often called the "French Disease"</note>, therefore it is not necessary to use it in open wounds, except specifically in the French ones. There are also many other tinctures, such as Celandine <note>original: "Chelidonia"</note> and the like, which are not shown here to be mentioned.

### Concluding Speech to the First Part.

S. Such foundations with the tinctures, as mentioned, of Gold, Corals, Balsam, Antimony, and the Salt of the Philosophers, should in no way be neglected, but rather put into practice, so that the true and entire Art may come to light. Although it is true that it may not be understood by everyone: yet there is nothing more to be seen or made more intelligible. Therefore, a physician should have learned in such a way that he has mastered these things; otherwise, they may <insert>not</insert> understand it. Also, the "fathers of the schools" <note>the traditional academic authorities</note> do not need to know or have learned them, for they only fill their little brass boxes and use them forevermore. It is a great deception in medicine that a physician believes he is not obliged to know more than simply being a "Doctor," and that what is learned in the high schools is enough: yet that is nothing but an unproven foundation that is not complete, nor proven and compared in the Light of Nature. And the others who are surgeons <note>original: "Wundarzt"</note> believe they have enough of their art if they can make brown, blue, green, and white ointments in little brass boxes.

C. He who wishes to be a true physician and useful to the sick must know, learn, and be capable of more than all those from whom they learned, and far beyond, so that their learning and high schools become as disciples compared to them. As long as that does not happen, it is entirely lost and in vain. If this is to happen, they must have the instruction so that their preparations and cookery in medicine can be sent forth in such a manner. When it comes to that, then it will be well with medicine, and the sick will be made healthy who otherwise would be corrupted, harmed, or strangled. Some might perhaps think that it cannot come to the point where the apothecaries become "muddlers" and the sophists "archers" <note>metaphors for incompetent practitioners and those who miss the mark of truth</note>: let them only consider that the Art has no enemy except those who think they know it. For they persuade themselves and prefer the light of corruption rather than the making of health. If they did not have such things in their hearts, they would learn and seek something better, and despise nothing that concerns Art or the like: reading everything with diligence, judging it, and loving it. But they are so sighted and of such a nature that they despise that which makes them true physicians: and yet they cannot let their lies be shamed, but defend them daily. I thought, however, that an oversight would be made by the authorities: but since there are many matters pending, and they do not know these things, and everyone may do what he pleases: it is no wonder if even worse things happen than what is already occurring. But regardless of all that, the right certainty is to be praised, and blessed is the man who walks with piety.

# The Second Part / on the Healing
## of Open Sores / by Dr. Paracelsus.

### Preface.

<image-desc>Decorative initial capital W with intricate floral and foliate designs, featuring a bird-like creature at the top and a human-like face within the foliage.</image-desc>
<margin>A cause of the 435.</margin>
<margin>Cause.</margin>
Although no one should deviate from the first principle of healing, but rather everyone should follow it—for a higher principle cannot be found—nevertheless, because the physician is often inexperienced in such arts and <term>tinctures</term> <note>alchemical medicinal preparations</note>, it is necessary, for the sake of the sick, to indicate another way so that they may follow it, as follows hereafter in this part. It is no less true that it often happens that the origin [of a disease] does not lie deep within the body, but exactly at the place where the injury is. Where such a thing occurs, this counsel must be followed. Therefore, I present to you another method according to the nature of open sores, how they are divided into <term>species</term> <note>original: "Species"; types or categories of disease</note>, and then the appropriate medicine according to the content of those species, as each belongs to the other. This is accompanied by a brief explanation of the nature and signs of the injuries, so that they may be more easily recognized.

<sig>B</sig>
Now, it is also true that I am introducing a process here that is foreign, and of which the ancients thought little—almost nothing at all—and of which the <term>sophists</term> <note>Paracelsus's derogatory term for traditional academic physicians who relied on logic rather than experience</note> in particular have no knowledge. Only one cause compels me to write such a new foundation: the fact that the ancients wrote and taught no final, certain foundation, and yet medicine has a certain and true foundation. Since it was not described by them, it is right that another should do it. Not that I alone boast of this, but—God willing—more shall come. But faith is so firmly placed in <term>experience</term> <note>original: "Erfarnheiten"; practical clinical observation</note> that it will not be moved in haste, but only with time. For the way I indicate is for learning; it does not go along with laziness. For the skill that belongs to a physician will not allow a twenty-four-year-old, immature calf to be made into a Doctor.

However, since all the high schools want to make everyone a Doctor, and one must study for twenty years—since it is such a common trade, he must be a Doctor, but he must know nothing. For how can one study in so few years—in three, or perhaps five—so that he may become a Doctor? He can no more philosophize, nor experience <term>astronomy</term> or <term>alchemy</term>, than he can be a physician. Furthermore, he should be a <term>perambulator</term> <note>original: "Perambulanus"; a traveling scholar or wandering practitioner</note> for the reason that he may explore the world; those who stay in one place like a <unclear>blind-flow</unclear> <note>original: "Blenflos"; possibly a regional term for a stationary plant or organism</note> and <unclear>monks</unclear> <note>original: "Klosen"</note> without time are given the title of Doctor as they are: so it goes, and so the sick feel it. Therefore, I acknowledge none of them; they do not frighten me, since I know that they do not destroy me and are against the art of medicine. Thus, let the experience follow which I have encountered in treating every open sore, according to the content of the right foundation and truth of medicine.

### CHAPTER I.
#### On the healing of the first kind of open sores, according to the division
#### of the second treatise.
