Should it happen that a sick person comes to you with one or more open sores, ask about the first origin at the beginning of its arrival. If it be the case that he says: "It first came upon me with a shivering chill, then with heat, and that several times—not just once, but repeatedly—it created a redness at the site of the sores, with swelling, heat, hardness, and open <unclear>throbbing</unclear> <note>original: "Schläff"</note>, etc.; it shifted here and there on the body, not remaining steady in one place; after some time it took root in such a manner and thus created a <term>boil</term> <note>original: "koch"</note>; now the sickness of the <term>weathering</term> <note>original: "Witterung"; likely referring to the atmospheric or bodily "humors" affecting the wound</note> is there." Divide his healing into three parts: First, when it is not yet a boil or open sore; second, when it has become a sore; third, when it is healed, how the healed part is to be maintained.

For the first healing, do this: when the chill comes, let it pass and pay it no mind, even if it seems <term>pestilential</term>; but when the heat comes, then pay attention to where the <term>center</term> <note>original: "Centrum"; the focal point of the infection</note> wants to settle. At that same place, take half an ounce of red myrrh, let it be small and well-crushed; then half an ounce of white frankincense, also thus crushed; put each into a special little bag, well-fastened, and let them boil in half a measure of vinegar and a measure of white wine. After that, take a cloth, and while it is warm, lay it over the center; when it has dried, repeat this until all the heat is consumed. You cannot have a better remedy in heavy "weathering"; let it boil well, you may warm it again, and also pour more [liquid] back in and boil it further. You need not worry about dealing with other things; if only the heat is drawn out, then all things will be healed.

### CHAPTER V

### CHAPTER VI.
->On the Healing of Foul Sores that Stink Badly.<-

If a sick person comes to you who has a foul leg, such that it is not of a corrosive nature but is rotting away itself with great discharge, swelling, stench, and filth, ask about the beginning. If you learn that he was perhaps struck, pushed, or wounded there by a stab or otherwise, and from such a beginning this has arisen, then do this for him.

First you must cleanse him, then consolidate: nothing more is necessary. And the way to cleanse is thus:

Take thirty new fir cones that are still young in May, also very resinous and juicy; boil them in water until all the resin comes out, then boil down the water until only the pure resin remains, in the form of a turpentine. From this resin and rosin make an "eggshell" <note>likely referring to the consistency or a specific vessel</note>, mix it with the *Calcinate* according to the state of the matter; thus it cleanses itself, and after the cleansing, consolidate thus:

Take one pound of wax, half a pound of *Colophony*, and a quarter-measure of the wax you have boiled; melt them together. Then put into it this powder: Wood-root <note>likely *Sanicula*</note> and Comfrey <note>original: "Walwurß"</note>, one *Loth* each; half a *Loth* of mastic; one and a half *Loth* of myrrh; three *Loth* of yellow amber <note>original: "Agstein"</note>; four *Loth* of varnish: form it into an ointment and bind with it morning and night. If necessity requires a means of healing to cleanse, do not omit it, so that you always have a fresh base; otherwise, all healing would fall backward.
<margin>C</margin>

You should also take heed, where such sores are, whether another malady might be mixed in, so that you may recognize the signs and act in other ways that are not written here, but in their own chapter.

There you should also follow the healing by sending the sick person to a salt-brine <note>original: "Salßfultzen"</note> to bathe therein for ten days or more, so that this foul nature may pass away. For it comes from the moist cold of alum, which is overcome and warmed by the salt-brine.

### CHAPTER VII.
->On the Healing of Open Sores, which are the Most Difficult.<-

You shall recognize the shell <note>the nature/casing</note> of open sores that are the most painful and agonizing by these signs: when a sick person comes to you whose sore never allows any rest because of burning and "eating itself" <note>corroding</note>, such as "The Wolf" <note>Lupus/skin ulcers</note>, "The Cancer" <note>original: "Krebs"</note>, etc., also in the legs and the like; otherwise you can take no other recognition. These are healed thus:

His medicine is divided: firstly into soothing, secondly into making a fresh ground, thirdly into consolidating, and fourthly into driving away whatever complications may occur. Now, the nature of such sores is that they can endure no medicine, nothing mild, nor the like. Therefore, before all things, the soothing must happen first; thereafter follows the medicine that belongs to it.

Many have claimed such sores to be incurable, which is a mockery and a shame: the reason is they have not had nor known the basis of healing, nor known the origin. So that they might answer for their folly and ignorance, they have said it is incurable, and thus lied about the art of medicine and misled the sick, for the reason that they might hide in lies and that they could do nothing.
<margin>R iij</margin>

# The Second Book of Great [Surgery]

The mitigation <note>The process of soothing or lessening pain</note> is done in this way: Distill the oil through a retort. Take a quarter-measure of cloves, half a quarter of juniper berries, half a quarter of sulfur of vitriol <note>original: "Sulphuris Vitriolati"; a preparation of iron or copper sulfate</note>; distill these, well-sealed. Afterward, pour in oil of bricks <note>original: "Oleilaterani"; an empyreumatic oil used in old medicine</note>, half as much as there is; then the three greater mitigatives <note>soothing agents</note> in a fourth part, as much as all of them together, and taken in equal amounts; distill it a second time. Whatever you smear with this oil loses all its pains <note>original: "Wehetagen"</note> in injuries, of whatever kind they may be.

Now that you have done this and taken away the pain, you must know the cleansing, which is performed thus:

Take twelve ounces <note>original: "loth"</note> of oil of arsenic, eight ounces of oil of cloves, one ounce of clear realgar <note>arsenic sulfide</note> and crystalline precipitate: mix these together, dip a small cloth therein, and afterward lay it upon the injury, over everything as far as it reaches and wherever it is. Renew the cloth every twelve hours, so that the scabs <note>original: "Schelffen"</note> fall away and a fresh base appears beneath them. After that, take a little of the cleansing agent again, as I have said regarding the calcined material and mentioned in the other injuries, to be bound three or four times.

After this, bind it only with sticking plasters until the end of the healing, for you need no longer worry: the first medicine and the first cleansing create a fresh foundation and wounds that heal very easily and willingly.

You must also pay attention to accidents <note>complications</note> that lie in such injuries. They commonly eat away the bone or turn it black, sometimes the vessels and veins and the like. Where you might notice or see such a thing—namely, that you come upon the bone itself—you must not scrape those same bones away or knock them away, as is the custom among the "imaginary" doctors <note>A jab at traditional academic physicians who relied on theory over alchemical practice</note>; otherwise, let them remain. And continue further with the healing, so the flesh will pull itself over the bone without any harm. For it is a great folly to scrape and file with chisels <note>original: "Schrotteisen"</note>, acting like a hangman, since God has taught another medicine, and they have not learned it, nor do they wish to learn it, to their own shame.

The medicine to restore such bones that are burnt or eaten away, etc., is done through this medicine: Take oil of camphor made through egg whites, take half an ounce of oil of cloves, mix them together; bind it with this along with the other dressing until everything is covered with flesh.

### CHAPTER VIII.
->Of the Nature and Skill regarding Open Injuries that<-
->Eat Away in Breadth.<-

If a sick person presents an injury before your eyes, such as on the face, shoulders, chest, ribs, and the like, appearing like a dry lichen <note>original: "Flechte"; often referring to skin eruptions or herpes</note> on the body, then look and observe thus: If it goes into the width, eats around itself, gnaws away what is there—the flesh, everything—and then presses so strongly into the veins and the flesh that it gets behind the ears, exposing veins and many parts, eating away the ribs, shoulders, and the like; it is so harmful that among all open injuries, there can be no more miserable state.

Then heal it thus; there are two pieces that heal such fistulas: namely, the oils of the metals and the "sweetness of mercury" <note>original: "süsse Mercurii"; likely calomel or a non-corrosive mercurial preparation</note>, so that they are washed or smeared with it twice every day. These oils kill the salt at the root which causes this injury, and they heal from the ground up. The best is oil of lead <note>original: "Olen Saturni"</note>, followed by silver <note>original: "Lunae"</note>, then iron <note>original: "Martis"</note>, then copper <note>original: "Veneris"</note>, and best of all tin <note>original: "Iovis"</note>. But above them all is the sweetness of mercury, which is also formed like an oil. It is no less effective than in the beginning; then there is the Royal Secret <note>original: "Arcanum Regis"</note>, the Mercurial Waters <note>original: "Aqua Mercuriales"</note>, and experiments that heal quite freely. But every person should know that these are healed with minor medicine. Therefore, it is necessary that every physician strives for the best medicines: for these are heavy injuries, and moreover in ends and places where there is no deformity.

To make their medicine is somewhat too skillful and not for everyone to undertake, which is why I omit it here, so that the many [so-called] doctors shall not misunderstand what a physician writes or advises. They sneak about prematurely, saying "it is Alchemy," as if they should not know it, and as if it were a shame for them if they knew and could do it. You may well recognize such ignorant people in the field of medicine.

Yet there is such instruction: that the metals should be "broken" <note>chemically dissolved or reduced</note>, as was said of the tincture of gold, and thus prepared according to the same manner into a Secret <note>Arcanum</note> to be used for itself without addition. But regarding the preparation of the sweetness of mercury, no oil without all sharpness and corrosive nature is mentioned: the realgar and mercurial waters are sufficient to be recognized.

### CHAPTER IX.
->Of Healing the Nature and Genus where one Kind<-
->Transforms into Another.<-

A sick person who presents his complaint to you and says: "My injury once looked like this in the beginning, but afterward it changed into another form," thus it changes further and further into another being and never remains constant, and there always comes something new, something different, something strange: then you have instruction enough on how you should act and what it is.

### Wound Medicine: The Third Treatise.

Thus shall you act and deal with the medicine against that which stands before the eyes <note>visible symptoms</note>, and against that which has passed. Thus the healing is established in Mercury <note>original: "Mercurium"</note> alone. This is the first principle, and it does not deceive. Thereafter, healing is found in rosin <note>original: "Colofonia"</note>, litharge <note>original: "Lithargyrium," a lead mineral</note>, and gum. By these two ways you must heal them.

The preparation of the Mercury is this: you must coagulate it through alum water <note>original: "Aquam Aluminis"</note>, and grind that same coagulation into a powder, very clean, which is without any pain or aching. Mix that with "Fulco" ointment <note>original: "Vnguento Fulco"</note>; with this, smear the injuries thoroughly until you have a good foundation.

Then cut a plaster: one pound of litharge <note>original: "Gletten"</note>, one pound of oil, one pound of wax. Into this plaster or wax-cloth <note>original: "Cerot"</note> let one pound of rosin flow. Afterward, put in three pounds of frankincense, and then five ounces <note>original: "Loht"</note> of varnish. Then dip a plug <note>original: "Zapffen," likely a surgical tent or pledget</note> into it; from this make plasters, with which you should bind the sick as has been frequently mentioned.

You need not worry further about more medicine; it is enough for the sores themselves, and they will accept the healing easily. You need not take heavy worries upon yourself; just let the medicine proceed.

Nevertheless, if such injuries were not fundamentally grounded for the benefit of human nature, it would never be possible for them to be healed. For when they change too long from one essence into another, the conclusion in the end is often leprosy <note>original: "Außsag," meaning Aussatz</note>. Therefore, heed the signs, so that you do not undertake more than nature’s command and ability allow.

->C H A P T E R X.<-
->On the Kind of Heavenly Influence in Open Sores.<-

Regarding the sores of Influence <note>original: "Influenz," referring to astrological or atmospheric effects</note>, you must understand them only if the patient informs you of the time, hour, day, and year. Upon this, you yourself shall erect the heavens <note>cast a horoscope</note> and recognize whether such is a heavenly impression or not. As is known to astronomers, the time, hour, and day of future heavenly illnesses must be known in such a manner.

If you recognize such a thing, you must take two medicines before you: One, if the course of the heavens has consumed and left itself behind, you proceed with another natural medicine. But if not, and the impression were still there, then you must use the medicine that is natured according to the heavenly impression.

Thus there are two kinds of ways in medicine: the natural and the unnatural. The natural is the earthly; the unnatural is the heavenly. Now, the medicine of natural powers is firstly to cleanse, and thereafter to consolidate. These two medicines occur in the form and way as was previously spoken of regarding other open sores; apply this alteration in comparison to another, and take that same process for it.

But if they should still be under the Influence, you must act astronomically; that is, through those things that act against earthly properties and essence. Such things are as if they were sorcery, as the Pellitory <note>original: "Perlicaria"</note> does, or the wild Adder’s Tongue <note>original: "Naterzungen"</note>, or the Flixweed <note>original: "Sophia"</note>. For their effect is such: you take them and draw them through cold water, lay them over the injury, and afterward bury the herb from the injury into fresh earth and lay a large stone upon it, so that it soon rots. As it begins to rot, the injury begins to heal; and when it is entirely rotted, the sore is entirely healed.

This is not that it is a sorcery, but rather a natural effect in the power of the stars, which thus accomplishes such an effect, ordered according to Divine Order. But because the self-styled physicians have not learned what they should have learned—namely, Magical Astronomy <note>original: "Astronomiam Magicam"</note>—they have brought it into contempt, and thus such injuries are robbed of their healing through the misunderstanding of such unlearned people. For anyone who does nothing but invent and fantasize, what use is he to himself? He leads them out of right order into error.

->C H A P T E R XI.<-
->On the Healing of Bodily Fluxes.<-

If a congenital injury <note>original: "geborner Schad"</note> should befall you, learn to recognize it in this way: whether it is hereditary, that is, born from the parents. If it is so, then it is a bodily flux. Likewise, if it were natured according to the property of the person's complexion <note>original: "Complecion," the balance of humors</note>, and if it is of the same essence, kind, and property, then recognize it as a bodily injury, that is, a bodily flux.

To speak of its healing cannot be done as with other injuries; rather, one must go further than what is now well-known and obvious. No one can stop a spring; one must let it have its course and let it have its power. This is all that my discovered cure has within it, knowing the way in that same manner.

One sees that often a spring is dried up by the sun, or by the medicine which goes out from it. In such a manner there are also natural suns—that is, natural medicines—which have this power; these must be sought. Likewise, there are some people of such a kind that they consume much of such flux, so that it may not go to the open sores. One way is like drying out where the sun is, naturally; the other is from the nature of the person, therefore that same way is to be left alone.
<sig>R iij</sig>

# The Second Book of Great [Surgery]

Abstinence <note>original: "Abstinens"; here referring to the restriction of fluids or specific diets</note> must be practiced above all things. For what would be the use of drying something out if the sun dries it up and then it rains back into it? Accordingly, if abstinence is maintained, then the subsequent drying out is beneficial; however, if the dried parts fall into decay, it is harmful. Furthermore, I know of nothing better to dry out the "sweet springs" <note>a metaphorical term for weeping sores or lymphatic discharges</note> than that which **Saffron of Mars** <term>Crocus Martis: a red oxide of iron used in alchemy and early medicine for its astringent properties</term> accomplishes. And this is sufficient regarding the open damage; let it be cleansed and remain so, so that the flow has an outlet, whether it flows or not.

It is also no less true that one may divert a spring to another path, and likewise the "body-sweets" <note>bodily fluids/discharges</note> to another path. But you should know in such cases that such diversion can only happen with great difficulty. For even if it is possible for a time and does occur, it eventually breaks the same **Thami** <note>likely a corruption of 'dam' or a specific anatomical barrier</note> and becomes a greater harm than it was at first. It is also no less true that purging the flows from the body is good and useful, for it dries out the body, and subsequently the flows can be more easily consumed. However, it is also to be feared that **purgations** <note>medical cleansings, often via laxatives</note> in other places may do more harm: but better one than two.

### CHAPTER XII.
->On the healing of damages arising from bone fractures, burns, wounds, etc.<-

Such damages are recognized by what the patient himself says about the beginning of his fracture, or wound, or burn, or animal bite, and how it subsequently fell into corruption. This is commonly the fault of the ignorant sort alone, who through their lack of understanding are corrupted therein. For they wish to learn nothing until its proper time, from which follows such evil and woe. But whether help is possible there, and whether the bone can be brought back to its right alignment, or the damaged limb, that you shall recognize through skill, as I have written in the **Wound-Medicine** <note>referring to his larger work on surgery</note>. But if you <sig>B</sig> cannot be of use to him with that, then do as follows.

First, cleanse and purify the internal from the pure, as this may proceed. Thereafter, heal it through the **Impression** <note>the celestial or spiritual influence</note> of its **Wisdom** <note>original: "Sophie"</note>, in **Smartweed** <note>original: "Persicaria"</note>, etc., as was recently indicated. There is no other way, for such is the final process. But apply yourself to the study of surgery and instruction.

### CHAPTER XIII.
->On the healing of the nature of open sores from a narrow Constellation.<-

The recognition of such damages is most certain in this point: that they will in no way heal by what is merely earthly power and property, such as **Comfrey** <note>original: "Consolida"</note>, **Mummy** <term>Mumia: a substance made from embalmed bodies, believed to have vital healing powers</term>, **Plasters** <note>original: "Empflastra"</note>, or **Ointments** <note>original: "Vnguenta"</note>. Rather, they require a **Constellated** medicine, born of the stars, so that both constellations stand against one another.

Such medicine must be "constellated" from its own nature; that is, it must have an innate nature of the constellation, such as **Greater Celandine** <note>original: "Chelidona"</note>, **Oak leaves**, or **Plantain** <note>original: "Plantago"</note>. For the medicine must be made from such things, for they are certain and do not fail.

But that they may accomplish a daily and powerful effect happens in two ways: The first is when they are prepared and used as coarsely as they may be. But where this will not suffice, make this recipe: Take three handfuls of **Celandine**, two handfuls of **Oak leaves**, crush them together, and let them rot in manure; thereafter distill it into an oil. Wash the sores with this, and to encourage the **incarnation** <note>the growth of new flesh/granulation</note>, sprinkle crushed powder made from them into the wound. Thus proceed to the end. And do not despair with this medicine; it is the most certain cure for <sig>C</sig> constellated sores.

### Concluding Speech.

In the healing of all open sores, the highest principle is: First, to take away the pains; second, to heal the damage so that nothing contrary remains in it; and finally, to heal and close it. Now the medicines for all four mentioned have been well presented. If a physician is established in these, what is there that might withstand him (unless God wills it otherwise)? I say this much, and may well do so from my experience, that it is to be believed that I have considered only the benefit of the sick and not craftiness. For I can find in myself full experience only for the sake of the patients' benefit. Therefore, the sick should strengthen themselves to recognize the true physician. For where the Good is, and where the narrow benefit lies, there they find no certain, proven art. There is only so much there among those [false doctors] to bring out the money; further than that, they regard no diligence. From such, it might perhaps be entreated that my recipes might be presented as being right and good by them, and thus given to you sick people; and yet they might not be so, for there are few who understand them, so that it is more a harm to them than a praise. But I say this: therefore my experiences should be used, not written by untimely "clubs" <note>original: "Kolben"; a derogatory term for ignorant or blunt-witted people</note> or by their names, but by experienced people who have studied their craft to the end and walk upon the right path. # The Third Part / of Healing
## concerning Open Sores / by DOCTOR
### PARACELSUS

## Preface.

Although in the second part, healing and everything pertaining to it was sufficiently indicated: yet because physicians know so little of medicine—which is more a shame to them than a praise or honor, since every man should be able to keep body and soul together without being torn apart—and because the infirmity is present and shows itself openly, it is necessary for the sake of the patients' health to further describe the common medicines. I intend to reveal and present them in the most useful and best way, as they are known today. For they involve a simple process and do not require much special wisdom, other than simply applying them. However, a great deal of experience and practice is found in the other [methods]. Therefore, whoever finds the preceding part too difficult or misunderstood—as I expect the majority will—let him follow and proceed according to the contents of the following recipes, so that the sick may be delivered and come to health, if not entirely in all cases, then at least in some part.

Now, it is no less true that if I were to record and describe these according to the Ancients <note>Paracelsus famously rejected the traditional teachings of Galen and Avicenna in favor of observation and alchemy.</note>, as such recipes came to me, and as I also used them in my childhood and youth as one inexperienced—like other inexperienced men—they would appear useful to very few in this part, as happened to me and others at that time. This caused me to learn further and to experience another foundation, which appears more truthful, more just, and more godly. Therefore, I do not wish to teach the Old, but rather the New, upon which I have placed proofs and signs through experience—not those [remedies] that have failed in their work, but those well-examined, tested, and confirmed by me. Thus, I may comfort and instruct every surgeon regarding open sores, so that as much as is possible by Nature and such medicine, nothing may be spoiled or harmed, but indeed will be useful and profitable for all diseases.

This is my advice, since there are so many kinds of open sores that appear incurable: follow such recipes, the <term>Arcanis Mysteriis</term> <note>Latin: "Secret Mysteries." Paracelsus refers to the hidden healing powers within natural substances.</note> of Nature, which I mentioned in the second part and faithfully presented, so that universality may be practiced, not <term>particularity</term> <note>Paracelsus preferred "universal" cures that addressed the root cause rather than "particular" cures that only treated specific symptoms.</note>, which does not suit a physician so well.

But regardless of the physicians' inexperienced though "proven" preparation of medicine, it is no less true that what is written hereafter is "particular": your simplicity and little knowledge force me to it, because through your far too much particular, experimental, and little knowledge, many sick people are ruined and harmed. So that such things do not happen, I write this particular process, of which there are two ways: One that applies to all open sores, whatever they may be, for I cannot abide that no help should be found.

The other way is that I [will provide] several special short techniques for open sores: such as in <term>Cancer</term>, <term>Fistula</term>, and the like. Only be diligent, that you truly protect the patient and do not neglect him through your inexperience and negligent manner, but with all [your heart]. If there is no lack in you, then God will also not forsake you, but will be profitable to you for your faithful heart. Therefore, if you will not learn further nor exert yourself, at least [refrain] from the miserable, material work through which you ruin and torment the sick. [Proceed] with a gentle approach, and not against Nature.

## CHAPTER I.
### How Open Sores are to be Healed through Cleansing.

There are several <term>Simplicia</term> <note>Simple, unmixed medicinal ingredients, usually herbs or minerals.</note>, from which <term>Composita</term> <note>Compound medicines made of multiple ingredients.</note> are made, which cleanse without any pain. Now, first you must have the knowledge of which open sores can be healed through cleansing: for not all are suited for it. But whatever is naturally disposed toward healing in such a manner will be healed well and thoroughly.

Thus, in all open sores, you must know this: when you wish to act "particularly," you must recognize as much about the open sores as about the medicine, so that you bring like to like. For where that is not the case, you must not be mistaken, but you must know that you are leading the patient [astray], and thus he is tried with one medicine after another, and thus often fifteen or more are used one after another, and none shall do anything, until finally one comes that hits the mark by chance.

He emphasizes the importance of clinical experience and the use of "cleansing" medicines that work in harmony with Nature.</summary>

that he, without knowledge, joins like to like and thus heals; so it would have happened to you also, had you asked in the same way at the beginning.

Therefore, know further: if the open sores have no burning salt in them, nor a corrosive nature, then they are suited for this healing, and nothing will be denied to you. The process is as follows: Take <term>Turpentine</term> <note>original: Terpentin</note> one pound, <term>Egg yolks</term> <note>original: Eherdotter</note> twenty in number, beat them well together into a small salve, then add as much <term>Honey</term> <note>original: Honig</note> as there is of both the others; let it boil over the fire, well-stirred, until it becomes a brown pulp. With this, bind the open sores morning and night; this cleanses and takes away all filth and stench.

Now that this has been done, you have laid a foundation for healing, so that the right medicine may heal the sore according to its nature, and it will not be that the medicine makes them resistant. But where this beginning does not occur, you might not reach the foundation of healing.

Now note this: such cleansing is not entirely perfect for healing; therefore, the recipe follows hereafter which makes it perfect until the point of complete healing, and it is made thus:

Take one pound of the aforementioned mixture, half a pound of beaten and washed <term>Turpentine</term>, beat them together as purely as you can, but do not boil it. Put into it pounded <term>Galbanum</term>, <term>Opoponax</term> <note>original: Oppoponacum; a gum resin used in pharmacy</note>, <term>Bdellium</term> <note>a semi-transparent oleo-gum resin</note>, two <term>Loths</term> <note>a historical unit of weight, approx. 15 grams</note> of each; cut and crush them as small as you can, and the mixture will take them up. Then add three loths of pounded <term>Wood-root</term> <note>original: Holzwurck</note> previously boiled in vinegar, and the mixture will take it up. Mix well: thus you heal all open sores in which there is no corrosive or salt-deposit.

### CHAPTER II.

->Of Healing through Calcinates in Open Sores<-
<sig>B</sig>
<insert>D</insert>esignated here is another special effect in <term>Calcinated</term> <note>substances reduced to powder by heat</note> things (I mean those that are not corrosive); these heal open sores wonderfully and with power from the outside. But you must know beforehand, and understand the knowledge, that they serve only those open sores where the <term>Salt-deposit</term> <note>original: Salzseßung</note> or the <term>Corrosive Salt</term>, from which the origin comes, has been lifted and has died off. For this often happens, that a burst occurs like a cloudburst, and in a hurry and in haste makes an open sore, and then does nothing more nor acts further. Upon which follows—if the right medicine is not used—that it is made even worse by the wrong medicine, and thus a permanent sore arises from it. Therefore, such sores as remain, you shall heal through the <term>Calcinates</term>, and in this way: Take <term>Egg yolks</term> ten loths, well mixed together, and bound therewith morning and night. From this salve you will see and do wonders, how powerfully it heals and cleanses.

It is also no less true that if the open sores are not so very large or too deep, you may heal any such sore with the plaster alone. But where it has depth and width, you may well apply the above-described salves by spreading them with lint-plugs, and the plaster over the same; thus you heal all sores according to such knowledge of their nature, just as a cloudburst comes suddenly from heaven and then ceases again. You should also know that you should first let it run its course. For many diseases are spoiled and become so unruly that they will no longer accept any medicine until many years and days have passed. Therefore, a physician should well mark the point: that in no way should the raging [sore] be attacked while it is in its labor, until it has completed its work and becomes tired. For all things become tired and desire rest at last; then, when it has run its course into sleep, that gives a successful healing, to the patient and the physician, profit and honor.

#### On the healing of Open Wounds through the Balsam of Tartar.

*And it is no less true, regardless of what kind or nature the open wounds are, if the origin is at the very place where the wound is, then the most useful healing is through the balsam of tartar. But where the origin is not at that place, one finds many errors <note>original: "Vrsal"</note> have arisen among those who have dealt with tartar. They have used it in ends and places where it did not serve, and therefore they have led many astray. Likewise, they had great cause for error in the preparation of the tartar, by not calcining it, or not dissolving the calcined material, which is to be used as a white oil at the site of the break; rather, its proper preparation, as ordered by Nature, must be used.*

*For in a prepared tartar, as its balsam is, there are great virtues of consumption—such as for dampness, swelling, blisters, burning, and eating away—especially in "oil-shanks" <note>original: "Delschencklen"; likely a term for swollen or edematous legs</note>, where it is best and most useful, no matter how large, how swollen, how rotten, how hollowed out, or how eaten away they are. Firstly, the swelling is consumed and dried out, and through its wonderful advancement, it takes the whole sickness and withers it at the foundation and origin.*

## CHAPTER VII.
### On the Healing of Open Sores through Distilled Oil, Gum, or Water.

Open sores are also found which, with great burning and stinging pain, will not or cannot be helped by corrosive agents, calcined vitriol <note>iron or copper sulfate</note>, nor alum, nor any other good medicine; nor will they accept the "stich-plasters" <note>plasters for stinging pains</note> and salves, or medicines for sores, but rather they become more violent the longer they last. Now, where such sores exist, they belong solely under the medicine of distilled things. But if you wish to heal such sores with distilled things, you must also be certain that you have good consolidatives <note><term>Consolidativa</term>: medicines that promote the closing and knitting together of a wound</note>. For through the distilled things alone, the sores may not heal, but they are made ready and prepared, and in every way obedient to the medicine. Which ones are the best for healing, I will indicate a few at the last: only take heed, that under such medicine belongs only that kind which otherwise will yield to no medicine, and which leaves no rest day or night due to burning and stinging.

Now, there are not particularly many such things for distilling: in the raw body there is petroleum oil, turpentine, cloves, ginger, nutmeg, and the like. When such things are distilled and subsequently put into the sores, according to the nature and property of the holes, they take all their pain away and mitigate it so quickly that the healing is gladly accepted. So also are all things that are distilled from the sun <note>likely referring to solar distillation or exposure</note>.

Now this is a recipe for such open sores: Take ten lots <note>a historical unit of weight, approx. 15 grams</note> of cloves, two lots of ginger, one lot of nutmeg; distill them together through the alembic <note>a chemical distilling apparatus</note> and separate the grades <note>fractions of the distillate</note> from one another. And according to how the pain is, so use a grade.

Another recipe: Take one pound of tree oil <note>olive oil</note>, one lot of white frankincense, five lots of cloves; put the ointments together in a flask through the alembic, also separated according to the grade.

Another recipe: Take one pound of turpentine, half a quartern of petroleum; distill them together in a flask, also according to the grade, and use it according to the grade.

Another recipe, which together with the others incarnates <note>grows new flesh</note>, consolidates, and helps to close the end well:
Take frankincense, mastic, three lots of each; cloves, two lots; mummy <note><term>Mummia</term>: a medicinal preparation made from mineral pitch or, historically, preserved remains, used as a panacea</note>, five lots; bdellium, a half lot; galbanum, two lots; distill these things together and separate the grades by the drop. Further, distill tree oil, also separating the grades; thereafter mix both oils together in a glass in equal parts, place flowers of St. John's Wort <note>original: "flores Hypericonis"</note> therein until it is full, and let it stand; thereafter use it.

The use is that one should brush it on with a feather and thoroughly moisten the entire sore over and over, morning and night. And if, during that time, pain from burning or aching should occur, one should immediately brush it again in the same manner and not stop. And to cover the sores, the most useful is the "Plaster of Calamary" <note>original: "Emplaſtrum vom Calmarem"</note> which stands in the first particular part, or those in the other; it is sufficient for healing.

This kind of sore tolerates no attractives <note>medicines that "draw" out humors</note>, no turpentine, no plasters, no salves, etc., whether they be mild or not, except as stated above, that which is distilled and prepared through distillation. Therefore, every physician should be able to distill all things to the best of his ability, where apothecary cooking may not be called for, so that you are a better provider.

There are also certain collyria <note>eye-washes or medicinal lotions</note> for the eyes which show themselves wonderfully in such open sores, taking away all aches and killing corrosive salts, and consuming none of its power; especially those that are distilled are secret and useful techniques that appear wonderful in all sores.

There are also some, as mentioned, where balsam is distilled with corrosives, but they lose the corrosive nature and become milder through the distillation. Nevertheless, the nature is still there, and they are secret and useful techniques that appear wonderful in all sores, and the more they are used, the better they become.

# Wound Medicine: The Third Treatise.
<page-num>123</page-num>
<margin>Signature: E ij</margin>

### CHAPTER VIII.

->On Healing Open Wounds through Natural Baths.<-

Regarding baths or naturally springing waters, no one can say otherwise than that there are powers and virtues within them that are mightily useful to mankind. Although water is often little esteemed, great virtues reside in it: for what is prepared with water, in cooking and drinking, is healthier than what is preserved with wine. Likewise, beer is in every way healthier than wine; that is, beer causes less sickness than wine. Therefore, since it is found through experience that there are powers in drinking water, as mentioned: how much more may these powers be tasted and recognized in others that are external, such as the Alum-based, the Vitriolic <note>containing sulfates of iron, copper, or zinc</note>, the Warm, the Sulfur baths, and the like, both sour and sweet.

It is proven in medicine that the plants of the earth have many powers, and it is also proven that waters are similar in nature to certain plants; in testing, various salts and the like are found, which need not be mentioned here. But the reason I point this out is so that their virtue should be esteemed as equal to those plants: from which it follows, that since other plants [heal], so do the waters, which are also "growths" of nature like any other. The fault lies only in this: that through the negligence of physicians, the waters have not been properly experienced but rather despised. It is a shameful thing that a physician despises what he should not despise, and what he ought to know and experience. But since pride, envy, greed, and self-interest have struck medicine, a fracture has occurred in the art: for nothing good comes from the aforementioned things and [vices].

Now, to speak of the waters and the baths, you should know this: that open wounds which take their origin from within the body, rather than only at the site where the wound is, should be guided to the baths. Furthermore, if the wound is Alum-like, that is, it should be an *Ulcus Aluminolum* <note>an alum-type ulcer</note>, and the bath should be an *Alum-bath*: when these two come together, then the healing begins. But where there is no concordance <note>harmony or matching of properties</note>, no healing will be found in that place. A physician should consider this, so that he joins them together correctly and knows how to recognize them.

It is also no less true that an open wound which has run its course and "hissed out" its venom is easy to bring to healing. If a physician recognizes such wounds, he should send them to such a bath; they are healed more easily than with other medicines. Likewise, other wounds are found which are also to be healed by baths, such as those that are still "young" <note>fresh or recent</note> and without flux or complications; for these, bathing is a perfect medicine, and they are healed sooner by such baths than by [apothecary] medicine. It should also be noted that the baths prove their own power—which are *Incarnativa* <note>flesh-growing</note>, *Consolidativa* <note>wound-closing</note>, and what their *Simplex* <note>single ingredient</note> or *Species* <note>mixture</note> is—therefore, the corresponding types of wounds should be sent to them.

You should also be on your guard, in case a person is naturally healthy and would easily come to healing in baths, but the wound is not one that [simply] needs healing, but must be addressed at its origin—and the origin does not lie where the hole is: in that case, do not let this person be killed or made worse. But if you find that hole to be caused by the "Weathering" <note>Paracelsian term for external atmospheric or astral influences</note> or its like, then allow it to be healed, and with the method that belongs to the Weathering; thus, through skill and certain art, one may always act with dexterity in all things, so that no one is misled or ruined.

***

### CHAPTER IX.

->On Healing through Time, which is itself the Physician.<-

Just as a rain sometimes comes that lasts a long time, one after another, and yet at last it stops by itself: so also are there certain wounds which open themselves up, and when they have fully completed the time of their malice, they then cease. But yet the wound is not yet healed; that is, Time alone does not heal: it has indeed removed the foundation and the cause, but it leaves the wound behind.

Now, at that stage, there is nothing more to consider than healing [the physical gap], for the *Materia peccans* <note>the "sinning matter" or morbid substance causing the disease</note> is no longer there, but is gone and away. From this it follows that many physicians have arisen who for a long time used many kinds of medicines, but the Time was not yet there, and therefore the patients were not healed. And when the Time comes, then a simpleton heals them, and it is said: "He has healed him." In this way, many such wounds are healed by blister-salves, by fumigations, by washes, and similar "hood-peddler" <note>quack or traveling salesman</note> remedies. Now, these medicines are credited with the healing, whereas the origin disappeared by itself. But where the origin [remains], their medicine is nothing. Therefore, many a man is "laid in the wood" <note>treated with guaiac wood for syphilis</note>, in sweating, in [misery], and it is shameful to heal in such a way—that is, where Time has already consumed the cause.

Therefore, pay attention in such healing, where the Time is, what you can and may do with such medicine...

# The Second Book of Great [Surgery]

<margin>A</margin> ...use, or sweating, or fumigating, or using "the wood" <note>original: "holßen"; likely referring to Guaiacum or "Holy Wood," a common 16th-century treatment for chronic diseases</note>. But where such things are not present, then desist, for you would only make everything worse. Although the aforementioned pieces are the greatest enemies, it is better that you conduct the healing through <term>Sparadrapp</term> <note>medicated adhesive bandages or plasters</note> and binding. For every open sore, whatever kind it may be, will be consumed in its malice by time.

Recognize such injuries by this: where you see that an open sore has spread to all the soft tissues and prepares to heal itself—that is, where it becomes resistant and leaves behind the old malice—then it is directed toward recovery, and you may heal it easily, for Nature herself helps. Therefore, if you wish to heal all sores because one has succeeded for you there, be careful; it is not always the right time, and you must provide for and protect the patient from ruin with "the wood" and the like.

## CHAPTER X.

### To heal open sores through Sparadrapp, that is, through the binding of the feet.

This is also a healing of open sores that are below the knees and have a "flow" <note>original: "Fluß"; referring to discharge, humors, or edema</note> from the body. Now, the art is very nearly the same, and not to be understood otherwise than the reduction of veins and injuries; except that there is a displacement, so that the flows may not occur because they are thus restrained, and so the sore below the knee is healed.

<margin>B</margin> But you should not only consider how you shall heal one injury, but also consider whether you make another and worse one. For here, the suppression of the flows is not in itself an upright art, but resembles more a deception, and should not be permitted to be used in all cases.

Where this practice is good and without harm is only where the flows wish to make a passage, not out of a chronic condition, but from a causal incident: such as in a place where it happens that an injury occurs on a leg through scratching, itching, bumping, etc., and the same was neglected and poorly cared for. In that case, the opening may be a cause for the "fruit" <note>humors or morbid matter</note> in the body to join there and take its course. Where such is the case, in such places and ends, the <term>Sparadrapp</term> may well be used until the hole heals shut. But where such a cause is not present, they should be used in no way.

The art of the <term>Sparadrapp</term>, how one should bind them with linen cloths and the like, has never been as it is now that a misuse has occurred; rather, they were made upon things that staunch the blood and the limb-water <note>serous fluid or lymph</note> in this manner: Take burnt <term>snail shells</term>, burnt <term>egg-bloodstone</term> <note>original: "Eyer-Blutstein"; likely a preparation of hematite or iron oxide mixed with egg</note> three <term>loht</term> <note>a unit of weight, approx. 15 grams</note>, <term>Armenian Bole</term> <note>a medicinal red clay</note> six loht, <term>sealed earth</term> <note>original: "Terra sigillata"; a medicinal clay pressed into cakes and stamped with a seal</note> five loht. Crush these all small together and mix with a dissolved <term>Gum Tragacanth</term> in <term>rose water</term>. Thereafter, draw a bandage through the pulp and bind from the bottom up to the top. This is still the best binding, though ten other things are taken and laid over it, but their folly is thereby revealed.

<margin>C</margin> When this has now been done, you should know that since the flow can no longer go down, the flows will settle above the binding. You must provide for these, be it with <term>abstinence</term>, with <term>purgation</term>, with <term>bloodletting</term> <note>original: "Lässur"</note>, or with "the wood," however you may <term>retreat</term> <note>original: "Erreterieren"; to withdraw or drive back the humors</note> them there. For it belongs thereto until you are certain of the course: so that it does not fall down again after the removal of the linen cloths, but that it has yielded and united itself again in a right way and nature. But that may not last, for it will all break open again and have no permanence; therefore, you should know beforehand where you should use it and where not.

## Concluding Speech.

In this third part of the third <term>treatise</term>, I have taken it upon myself to describe the <term>medicine</term> that the ignorant doctors misuse, with the intention of informing them of the misuse, so that they may use each medicine for the injuries for which it is ordained, and not attempt to handle all things with one kind of medicine. Rather, each medicine should be ordered where it belongs, so that ruinous injuries do not subsequently grow for the patient, worse than they were before. Such <term>particulars</term> <note>specific cases or remedies</note> are beautiful. Although there are more which I do not mention, I have [put them] in the Fourth Book on the French Disease <note>Syphilis</note>. In that same place, every doctor who wished to heal open sores would be well instructed in these ten particulars alone. If they used them as they are to be used, what great benefit would grow for the patients from them? How many a man would be gladdened who is otherwise ruined? May they allow themselves to be persuaded to learn what I hold in this, and not leave it, since I desire only to draw them from their folly and error, and to prevent the deception, falsehood, and mockery that goes out from them so greatly.

End of the Third Part of the Third Treatise.

From one day to the next, fundamentally: and it is enough that one day suffices for its own affliction <note>A reference to Matthew 6:34: "Sufficient unto the day is the evil thereof."</note>, and the next morning likewise, and so on until the very last. Rather, they must be brought into harmony in a concordance; that is what Science <term>Scientia</term> does.

# The Third Book of the
## Great Surgery of the highly renowned Doctor Theophrastus Paracelsus, concerning the French diseases, pox, sores, lameness, bumps, and other growths that arise from them.
### Written in honor of the most illustrious and most powerful Prince and Lord, Lord Ferdinand, by the Grace of God King of the Romans, Hungary, and Bohemia, Archduke of Austria, etc., our most gracious Lord.

#### CHAPTER I.
#### Concerning the Names of the French Disease.

<image-desc>Decorative initial drop cap 'M' with an intricate border featuring foliage and a face.</image-desc>

**M**ost first of all, and at the beginning of a book, the name of that which the book discusses should be handed down. It follows then, that I have desired to describe the names of this new and unheard-of disease before I write further of it. Now, every thing should receive its name from that which it is, so that the thing and the name are equal to one another. For to name a thing otherwise than the disease itself dictates by its own nature is against Nature, against Reason, and also against the Schools <note>The "Schools" refers to the traditional academic medical authorities like Galen and Avicenna, whom Paracelsus often challenged.</note>. Although names sometimes occur that are named partly after their nature, they are often not sufficiently grounded in truth.

It should also be noted that it sometimes happens that a thing cannot be fully grasped by one name alone, but must be addressed with several names. Where this occurs, it should not be neglected, but should be done in the most convenient way. Therefore, if a name encompasses something, even if not entirely, it should not be rejected. Now, when names are established in this way, it is proper that those names which arise from the knowledge of the thing itself be used as surnames <note>i.e., descriptive titles</note>, and an external name, which is comparable, may be given. # Chapter One Hundred: Concerning the French Disease.

Neither philosophers, physicists, nor alchemists yet exist who truly understand or have mastered any of the arts. They wish to appear great, yet they know nothing. He who is born of the disease is not the disease itself; rather, the disease creates that person. Now we see what your understanding of the French Disease <note>syphilis</note> amounts to: you are entirely ignorant of the *Matter of the French Disease* <note>original: "Materiam Morbi Gallici"</note>. You place your trust in "the wood" <note>likely Guaiacum wood, a common but often ineffective treatment</note>, but by doing so you only arouse the excrement and secretions. Where medicine is not such, what is it but one *Opposite* protected by another *Opposite*? <note>A critique of the Galenic method of treating "contraries with contraries," e.g., treating a hot fever with cold herbs.</note> Therefore, do not wonder that I do not use that "ink-mule" <note>scholastic book-learning</note>, for Nature acts according to the order of Alchemy, and I describe the illness accordingly. For medicine must be described based on its own art, falling away from the disease itself. For even if all the wood-shavings are taken away, the wood is still there. # Surgery: Of the French Disease.

### CHAPTER IX.
#### On the Recognition and Signs of the French Disease in General, as well as in Specific Types, that is, Universally or Particularly.

<margin>A</margin>
Furthermore, the necessity of recognizing the French diseases <note>The "French Disease" was the common 16th-century term for Syphilis</note> requires that such a task never be neglected. First, know this fundamental principle: Just as a mule is contrary in all things—it does not have the docile nature of a horse, such that it follows the rider like a horse, nor is it like a miller's donkey—so I wish to show here a general recognition to be used universally, as follows. The French disease arises out of surgical diseases. Now, when such a disease arises, pay heed to how it manifests: if it shows itself as mild, gentle, natural, and tame, and has the form of a surgical disease, then you may generally recognize it as surgical and not the French disease. But if it is contrary, stubborn, and has an "attachment"—that is, more complications and pain than a typical surgical disease—take this as an example: There are surgical pustules <note>term: Pustulæ (blisters or pimples)</note> and also French ones. The distinction between the two is recognized thus: Surgical pustules arise of themselves, accept medicine kindly, and are easy to drive away. The French ones also come in this way, but with them, they have a special affinity for four places: the genitals, the forehead, and especially where hair grows. Furthermore, they come with great weakness of the limbs and the like, and upsets in the stomach, along with a wasting discharge; this shows you the one parent. Thereafter, the French diseases have more "attachments" than the natural ones. This is the nature of the "mule" <note>Paracelsus uses the mule as a metaphor for Syphilis being a "hybrid" or "bastard" disease</note>. By such attachments, you shall also recognize all other species.

<margin>B</margin>
Recognition: all surgical diseases that cannot be healed without quicksilver <note>term: Recksilber (Mercury)</note> and without mineral tinctures are also of the French sort. For all diseases have their remedies and perfect cures <note>Latin: curas perfectivas</note> without quicksilver. It is necessary that a surgeon knows every surgical disease; then he may recognize by the outcome what kind of disease it is. And although surgical medicine does not heal the French disease, French medicine heals the surgical disease—with the distinction that the preparation for a surgical disease must be guided into the French nature. Thirdly, there is yet a general recognition: those that are known to have taken their origin through the venereal act <note>Latin: actum Venereum (sexual intercourse)</note>, and where the surgeon feels it is a surgical disease, yet it is nothing but the French disease. Thus there are three ways you may generally recognize the French disease. Furthermore, to know the species particularly, you must recognize how they behave in their increase and peak <note>Latin: Augmento und Statu (stages of disease progression)</note>, and what their essence, property, form, and shape are. You must recognize this as well as you know a horse from a donkey. For if you do not recognize those, you will not recognize the mule either. The distinction they have teaches you what each one is. Thus you must know them in surgery. If a surgical disease occurs, look for what surgical signs <note>Latin: Signa</note> it has; if it deviates, judge it as the French disease. Now see whose "ears" it resembles, whose voice, and whose body <note>Latin: Corpus</note>; thus you find its parents. That is, you must look at the wasting discharge, which shows you the one parent; thereafter the French disease has more attachments than the natural ones. This is the "donkey" side. By such attachments, recognize all other species.

<margin>C</margin>
Of the flesh: there you have the other parent. Now you can determine the species based on which two surgical diseases they were born from. For example, if a *Leonina* and a *Lupus* <note>Two types of skin afflictions, often associated with leprosy or severe ulcers</note> are together, the form strikes into the shape of leprosy <note>Latin: Lepram</note> and into the nature of the "wolf" (Lupus). Now, there is no perfect leprosy there, nor a perfect essence, but a mixture. Therefore know, particularly with all...

# The Third Book of the Great [Surgery]
<margin>To Princes 146</margin>
that natural diseases do not change, but rather their essence changes according to the body in which they reside. For example: suppose jaundice should occur, and that same person were "French" <note>original: "Frantzöſiſch"; a common 16th-century term for someone suffering from the "French Disease" or syphilis</note>. Now, if it were a man afflicted with the French Disease, the jaundice would take on a different character. Thus it is with both medical and surgical diseases: though they are born according to their own nature, they are broken in their essence when they enter a "French" body. Even if they are still recognized as jaundice or other ailments, they lose their innate character and properties. And although the ancient writers have written and read of a "perfect cure" <note>Latin: "Cura perfecta"</note>, that same cure can achieve nothing helpful in a place where the patient is "French," for a different Medicine <note>original: "Phyſica"</note> and Surgery must be undertaken. Where that does not happen, the physician will be troubled in trying to fathom the process and the cure in such diseases; he must be an expert in this matter, and otherwise no one else may manage it.

For teaching has no end, and yet we teach so that we may surpass those who came before us. Therefore, understand me on this point: that medical and surgical bodies have a different essence; for though their nature remains, they are "French," yet they are never as they should be. Therefore, the physician must be experienced in the secrets <note>Latin: "Arcanis"</note> of the mixing of these diseases, so that he may act against them. Now, if this is to happen, the French Disease must also be cured, otherwise the body will accept no cure; and if the French Disease is not cured, then the original disease remains. Thus, the two diseases must be healed as one, and if it does not happen so, then no health follows. For example: if someone had the French Disease, and "gnawing herpes" <note>Latin: "Herpeta mordax"; a term for spreading skin ulcers</note> occurred. The French Disease has its particular property, and the gnawing herpes also has a particular property. Now, the French Disease will not allow the healing of the Herpes unless the French Disease is first driven out, or unless both are driven out together. It may well be that the French Disease is healed while the Herpes remains; but if the Herpes becomes incurable <note>original: "incarabillis"</note>, it is a sign that the French Disease was not truly driven out, but only masked by an "imperfect cure" <note>Latin: "imperfectivam cutam"</note>, appearing as if it were a healing. Thus, bodily diseases and wound-medicine are so intertwined with the cure of the French Disease that they cannot be separated according to the process of the ancient writers. Therefore, there is more to be taught, for they must act upon the truth and not make a pretense <note>Latin: "Fucum"</note> of medicine. This is the reason why I direct you toward Alchemy and the "decay of the bunglers" <note>A derogatory reference to unlearned practitioners who do not understand chemical transformation</note>, as I have mentioned. Not that I teach the making of gold or silver in my writing, nor the "Philosopher's Stone" <note>Latin: "Lapidem Philoſophorum"</note>, for that is a "great sea" <note>Latin: "Mare magnum"</note>; rather, I teach the preparation of medicines, and that is my purpose. And if I could bypass Alchemy to avoid the bunglers, I would. But since that cannot be, the physician must be an Alchemist; he must be experienced in it, and otherwise no one else may manage it.

### CHAPTER II.
#### On the Communication of the Firmament's Influences and the French Disease.
<margin>In Building</margin>
<margin>建</margin> <note>This appears to be a later addition or a printer's mark; it is a Chinese character meaning "to build" or "establish."</note>
In this, we should understand the influence <note>Latin: "Influxion"</note> of the firmament, namely that it works in man just as it does in the earth. For example: the firmament does not rest but is in daily operation, bringing onto the elements what is within itself. On the earth it brings the grass, on the water the minerals, etc. And just as the firmament brings these forth, so it is also in man: the heavenly influences bring forth their properties in man, which he possesses in his elemental nature. In this way, just as you see the sun shine through a glass and produce heat, it also shines into the earth, and likewise into man. Now, whatever the sun finds in the earth, it moves toward growth; similarly, what it finds in man, it moves in the same way, whether it be a lily or a thistle. Now, if men are burdened with the French Disease, and the French Disease wishes to be still, like frozen water, the influence of the firmament nevertheless acts upon its essence, turning it into passions and pains, just as it brings forth flowers and grass in the spring. When such a conjunction occurs, the influences of the stars and the French bodies are so united and conjoined that many strange things arise from the French Disease, which cannot be healed with common specific remedies <note>Latin: "particularibus"</note>. Here, the physician must be a master of the "Great Medicine" <note>Latin: "Magna Medicina"</note>, otherwise no patient will become healthy. And even if the physicians do not understand this, it is well for them to learn, so that they do not perish miserably along with their "humors" <note>The four bodily fluids of ancient medicine</note>. And although their invented religion and their behavior have been considered honorable and well-regarded, and their "mirror-work" <note>likely a reference to superficial or deceptive practices</note> viewed with great reverence, it does not rest on the fact that they were righteous. For it is still a question in medicine whether their religion is a benefit or a stroke of luck, or whether nature heals itself by chance. It is not within their faculty, as their works prove, especially here in the French Disease, where it is clear as day how they have no foundation regarding the "species of the French disease" <note>Latin: "Specierum morbi Gallici"</note>, and have no certainty in the cure <note>Latin: "Cura"</note>. And when their art is at its highest and best, it is nothing but greasing and smoking...

# The Third Book of the Great Surgery

<margin>S. S. M. 34.</margin> <note>Likely a reference to a specific aphorism or section in Paracelsus's system.</note> It has its own operation. Now, this "projection" <note>A term from alchemy meaning the transformation of a substance</note> of the French Disease projects its operation into the body itself: if it is projected into the **Sulfur**, that type of Sulfur is affected; if it is projected into the **Mercury**, then the body becomes Mercurial. A tree standing there in the forest is also fixed in these three bodies <note>The Three Primes: Sulfur, Mercury, and Salt</note>: if it departs from them, it enters into **putrefaction** <note>decay</note>. The same happens to man, and so much more severely and worse, because the French "tincture" <note>The infectious essence of the disease</note> forgets itself and infects. Now, if the tree's Sulfur is withdrawn or becomes sick, it enters into **incineration** <note>reduction to ashes</note>, so that nothing remains. It is the same in man: if his Sulfur is infected, he proceeds so that nothing un-calcined remains in him. Likewise, if the **volatility** is taken from the tree, it will henceforth be a tree no longer, but a withered stump. So it happens to man if his Mercury is struck—and so much worse, for he suffers more accidents because the tincture has been attacked. It is like a forest set ablaze by a lightning bolt: it is worse than all other fires. Therefore, take note, so that you recognize the **Philosopher** <note>The true physician-alchemist</note> rightly: in which body each thing is placed, and what the "French Lightning Bolt" is. Then you will find three more species of the French Disease than I have already mentioned. And although this does not apply **universally**, it applies **particularly** to that specific limb. For even if one tree becomes sick, it does the others no harm. I point this out so that the **cure** may be conducted in these three species: one alone against the Sulfur, one against the Mercury—and do not act so ignorantly with **quicksilver** <note>original: "Argento vivo"</note>, through which you have killed many in such ignorance of the fundamental principles.

Such "mirror-doctors" <note>Doctors who only look at appearances or "smoke and mirrors"</note>—whose equals in lack of **knowledge** do not exist—shout and blubber so that their mouths have no rest all day. But what is this but a whining and a screaming, while all the hospitals and alleys lie full of miserable people? Out of fifty, they do not make one healthy; people come away more miserable from them than they went in. Now, what kind of **religion** <note>Used here to mean a "system of belief" or "professional code"</note> is this, where no fruit comes forth, only ruin and harm? The Germans also try this along with them, acting in hospitals so that they are no longer hospitals, but a **den of thieves** <note>original: "Spelunca Latronum"</note>, a place of robbery and plundering one after another. It would be better if they did not exist than to arrange for the sick to be led to their ruin in such a fashion. It is not accomplished by "My Lord Doctor's Reverence" riding on a donkey, while "Master Hämmerle the Ass-Scratcher" <note>A derogatory name for a low-level barber-surgeon or quack</note> hands out alms. They should ask God for more grace so that their alms might be effective, and not act in this "den-like" way as is now common everywhere—where Doctor Starwadel <note>A satirical name, perhaps "Staring-Tail"</note> and his donkey are well-kept, while Master Hämmerly carries his **painted boxes** in which the salvation of the sick does not reside.

->TO THE READER<-

<margin>C</margin> No more of this Third Book of the Great Surgery was available at this time, dear reader. Whether it was entirely finished by the **Author** <note>Paracelsus</note> is not known for certain. Also, the true Fourth and Fifth Books belonging to the Great Surgery (namely, one on external growths and defects, and one on external ulcers) which Paracelsus described (according to the disposition set down at the beginning of this volume), are also not known for certain.

However, the other surgical books—which in previous **editions** were substituted and (unwillingly) passed off by **Doctor Adam von Bodenstein** in place of the true Third, Fourth, and Fifth parts of the Great Surgery—now follow in the other volumes in their proper places. For they are not the true books of the *Chirurgia Magna* <note>Great Surgery</note>, but are separate **small works** <note>original: "Opuscula"</note> on surgery, each arranged and described by the author for itself. As can be seen from several **prefaces**, the first two true books of the *Chirurgia Magna* were written in the year 1536, and the Third in 1537. But the previous, incorrect Third part on "Open Sores" and the Fourth on the "French Disease" were finished long before, namely in 1528. And so it is with the others. The gracious reader must be informed of this so that he knows the reason why the surgical books have been arranged differently in this **New Edition**.

<margin>A</margin>
# The Three Books of Theophrastus Paracelsus
## Regarding the French Disease.
### The First,
Concerning the <term>Impostures</term> <note>Deceptions or fraudulent practices</note> which are committed in the healing of the French Disease.
### The Second,
Concerning the <term>Correction</term> of the <term>Medicines</term> which have been used for the French Disease until now.
### The Third,
Concerning the <term>Restoration</term> and healing of those illnesses which have been ruined by the medicines used for the French Disease.

<margin>B</margin>
# To the Honorable and Respected Lord Lazarus
## Spengler, City Clerk of the Praiseworthy City of Nuremberg,
### My especially favored Lord.

<image-desc>Large ornate initial capital 'G'</image-desc>
*F*avored Dear Lord, it is a most praiseworthy order that everyone who intends to serve the common good and be productive should first (to avoid being handed over to scrutiny) present their work. Since I, however, out of special trust in an honorable Council, have hoped that I might present this work in medicine to Your Honor as one appointed to consider the common good, I have herewith fully dedicated it to the same, in your honor and for your special pleasure. This work is divided into three parts. In the first, I recount all the medicines that

<margin>C</margin>
have been used, one after another, in what way they are erroneous and false in their <term>Imposture</term> <note>original: "Impostirt"</note>. In this, I have not regarded custom, pomp, or the ancient authority of the physicians, but rather what is virtuous and rightly recognized, having brought about a striking benefit. Although no one is made healthy through those [false] means, it is necessary to prevent the miserable destruction that has long been awaited as a great calamity. In the second part, I show what was first indicated as erroneous, yet had something useful mixed within it, which has been corrected and separated from the <term>Imposture</term>. In the third part, I urge the physicians toward mercy, to cut away from their destructive ways, and I conclude how the sick, who have been ruined by medicines, may be restored again.

I am not driven to such writing by my own need, for I am well, but rather by the poor and those who have come to heavy ruin through insolent practices. This damage will be a hindrance to my book, for the adversary—whom I mention briefly—does not regard the truth, nor the height of names, old acquaintances, splendor, nor pomp, but rather considers that medicine lies not in pride, but in experience. Nor should one regard the use of the knights of the ancients <note>Referring to traditional academic authorities like Galen or Avicenna</note>, for they are ignorant of these things. It does not matter that some wish to be held in higher esteem in medicine because they have consumed many letters [books] and break forth with them, yet have nothing but experience. Nor should it be considered that they have experienced a supposed <term>Philosophy</term> or <term>Astronomy</term> <note>original: "sedische Astronomien"</note>, or have a little knowledge of languages here and there, and practice similar polite customs. Rather, medicine should be measured solely in those things it is meant to be, which truly are hindered and not promoted by the aforementioned things. I hope this work of mine will be entirely pleasant to Your Lordship. I wish to remain commended to you and will always be diligent to show you all service and kindness. Given at Nuremberg, the 25th of November, 1529.

## Of the First Book / on the Deception of Medicine /
### By Doctor Theophrastus, Concerning the Diseases
->The French Diseases.<- <note>original: "Morbi Gallici." A historical term for syphilis, which was often named after rival nations.</note>

First, it is necessary above all things / for one who wishes to describe the foundation and true process of his profession / to first consider what might be contrary to him. For this reason / as long as that remains upright which is opposed to him and his foundation / in whatever way it may be / it makes those who conceive the right foundation and wish to do so entirely doubtful. And if the same remains / such a profession cannot be fundamentally understood without error / nor accepted with a faithful foundation. For present arguments create contrary discord / which gives the students in all their reading and learning an imperfect foundation on both sides / and the last becomes worse than the first. Therefore, my first intention is / to cleanse this following book / in which I wish to treat of nothing else / than of those whose deception <term>Impostur: the fraudulent practices or false theories of established physicians</term> might be entirely contrary to me / and thereby to overthrow them, which overthrowing is a protection of my proposed foundation: So that also those / who are called to be of the Sect of Theophrastus, may be protected and unharmed / while they read through my work / and remain free from all deceivers. In which first book I present to them all the deception: to which some still cling / some have turned away / some 
<sig>B</sig>
are contrary to them / for in that which can be attached to it / I think the name of Theophrastus has been inserted. I have rolled together all the deceptions of those same adversaries of mine / so that they could do nothing / except only to destroy my diligence and labor / and so that they could do nothing / except only to destroy my diligence and labor / <note>The repetition here appears to be a printer's error or for rhetorical emphasis.</note> and the betrayal of my sect by them / but also to turn back those who have been entirely perverted by them and bring them back to the right foundation. Although the old, ingrained habit is difficult to withdraw / it is yet to be hoped / that death will separate what is impossible for man.

## The First Book of Deceptions / in what way the sick are ruined.
-><-

### The First Deception / which rises against me are the
->Doctors.<-
<sig>C</sig>
<image-desc>Decorative initial D</image-desc>
These are rightly the first / for they were the first / who attacked this disease / so they are also the first / to occupy the upper places at the table / whose prestige is also the greatest. Upon this they first established their foundation / through which they undertake to drive me out of this profession. Namely / the Four Humors <note>original: "Pieren," a corruption of the Latin "pyra" or referring to the four "piers" or pillars of Galenic medicine.</note> / to be the mother of all disease / whose names and essence are sufficiently known according to their claims. From these humors all diseases are said to be born / these are the children of the Four Mothers: that is / four kinds of mothers / and likewise four kinds of children. From these mothers and children they claim to boast of medicine. To which I am opposed in this way / First, that the physician should eat upon the anatomy of the earth / in which there is only One Mother / which in like manner is also in man. For as the earth / as a single mother, brings forth from herself many herbs / many flowers / many trees / many shrubs / and each one manifold in its kind: So also the mother in the body bears her children in no other way. And therefore recognize the beginning of the disease from the kind of mother / and not from the nature of the quality <note>Paracelsus rejects the Galenic "qualities" (hot, cold, moist, dry) in favor of a unified chemical/elemental origin.</note>. Therefore, no medicine is so divided / there is but One Medicine / and that is the internal medicine. Although those people become unskilled because of their error, this division of medicine has followed. That is / that they have not been able to comprehend among their qualities / such as namely *Perlicum*, *Ethiomenum*, etc. <note>Technical terms for corrosive or spreading ulcers.</note> Therefore they have separated / for it would be an understanding of their diseases occurring from them / <note>The text repeats the phrase "for it would be an understanding..." multiple times, likely a transcription or printing artifact.</note> they could not, however, prove what that was / that there ate the mouth and the body / and burned the veins like a fire: Although they have sufficiently answered this question with common voices.

<header>concerning Impostures.</header>
