# Concerning Impostures.

Upon these four <note>The four Galenic humors: blood, phlegm, yellow bile, and black bile.</note> they have taken the ground to view the origin of the French Disease <note>original: "Frantosen"; a common historical term for syphilis.</note> as being of four kinds, and have created a strange kinship among them. Based on this practice, they have assumed four types: dropsy, to drive the French Disease out of the "aquosity" <note>excessive wateriness or fluid in the body</note>, and directed the pills toward the "flow of the head" <note>catarrh or discharge</note> to treat the flow of the French Disease. How these things rhyme together is evident in itself. There are not four kinds of the French Disease, but well over a hundred kinds; and nonetheless, in each particular one, there is a great kinship. If it were so created, then *Pills of Cochia* <note>A traditional purgative pill made with colocynth.</note> would be good for many things, and *Golden Pills* <note>Pills often containing aloes and saffron, used as a laxative.</note> would surely be emeralds. Thus, understand it according to the **Species** <note>original: "Art"; the essential nature or "seed" of a disease in Paracelsian medicine.</note> and not according to the **qualities** <note>The Galenic hot/cold/moist/dry attributes.</note>, which is like the single Mother: Consider the Nettle <note>original: "Vrticam"</note>, from what species it bites, from what species the Salt has its sharpness, and likewise from what Species the French Disease comes. Therefore, you should by no means "qualify" <note>assign hot/cold/moist/dry labels</note> in that place, but rather consider the Species as the origin of the disease.

No one contradicts that Colocynth <note>original: "Coloquint"; a bitter cucumber used as a powerful purgative.</note> should purge. But that which it is meant to take away should be gone. Thus, the French Disease will remain safe from the Colocynth. It is also true that Turbith <note>original: "Turbuch"; a root used as a laxative.</note> purges phlegm, but not the French Disease. This is to be understood by everyone: that which is written in the order of purging according to the four Qualities, Humors, or Complexions is by no means to be undertaken in these diseases. Therefore, they have written in vain about the French Disease according to the Four, and in helping the French Disease, all is for nothing. For no Humor is to be considered from the Four, but rather the single Mother of all Nature, who also casts down the foundation upon which they have placed their "body-coffins" <note>A derogatory term for their failed medical theories.</note>.

But yet one more thing (although it is almost overturned, yet the opposing thing remains unsaid), which must first be considered in all diseases. The first: Nature in its approaching degree. The second is the Species, which still lies hidden among you. The third: Time, of which they

B have never thought until now. These two paths they have: backwards into the qualities, never at the place where they have set it, and Nature itself is poorly "qualified." But to describe these Three, in which the origin of all diseases is born, and the Books <note>original: "Codices"</note> that contain such, with their Commentators: subsequently the writers of Practice, of which they have never experienced the truth. And it is difficult for them to grasp all diseases therein, even those they have never truly experienced. And it has hardly ever helped them, perhaps never even been seen; that is the way of all the young ones.

But so that the Truth does not succumb, and that it may be found what is true or not true, test the work to which I testify; the sick also praise it, who are witnesses to this Truth. Thus I hold faithfully before all those who are against me: that they should teach nothing other than what they can actually do. For to teach and not to do, that is small; to teach and to do, that is great and whole. For the physician should be whole: if not, let him stop learning that which he cannot do. Not "opinion," not "supposition," should be at home here. You physicians all seem like a pale-nut <note>A metaphor for something hollow or useless.</note> compared to a stonemason, who teaches his disciples more with his hands than with his mouth, and learns and does it together, and finds it useless to learn what he cannot do. Should he teach what his hand has not given, it is nothing but a doubt, left to dwell in the imagination. If so much depends on setting one stone upon another, how much more depends on the human being. For the physician is more than the stonemason. With this, I wish to have concluded the **First Imposture**, of those who wish to persist in the Medicine of Purging <note>original: "Purgandi"</note> or Syrupping <note>original: "Syrupi-zandi"; the practice of administering medicinal syrups.</note>, according to the custom and manner that the Apothecaries <note>original: "Apotecken"</note> have been capable of since olden times.

### The second Imposture, which is thought to oppose me, through Salving.

The imposture of Salving <note>original: "Schmirben"; the application of ointments, often containing mercury.</note> did not grow out of high understanding, but was taken haphazardly from common ground, as from the experiments of the old surgeons <note>original: "Wundartsten"</note>, which they used for the itch <note>original: "Kreße"; scabies or similar skin ailments.</note> and scurvy <note>original: "Keudigkeit"</note>. Because the pustules are somewhat similar to itchy sores, they thought the medicine would also be fruitful for them. With what indiscreet reasoning this was done is easy to measure. Should such be a reason to drive away the disease? Just because pustules look more like the scurvy-afflicted than a tanner looks like a fever? They acted before the disease had come to its right age or been brought to right health. Whatever stood the test for the itch remained the master. They did not consider their luck, but took it for their art; nor did they consider the downfall of luck, through which they might have measured that it is no art—for a constant thing has no end, whereas luck is lighter than a reed in the water.

They bring no special argument against me; they persist in their salving as it came to them, for as long as it may last. They do not desire to defend themselves further therein, except for what lies in the light of day; it is the loss they feel, which they dislike. Although it...

# On the French Disease: The First Book

However, there are two things I have against them: First, that they do not recognize the nature of the French disease, and are therefore forced to end it—or fail—as luck provides. If he <note>The practitioner</note> happens upon the right path, luck hits it well; if he goes wrong, he loses his chance. The second is that they throw their recipes together so improperly that if there were anything good in them, it would have to perish at the bottom. By this, they create such an opposition to Nature in the body that even if she were on the right track, she would be forced to collapse. For this reason, I have coupled together the main ingredients and most of their additives below, so that you may more easily recognize how I may defend myself against this imposture.

These are not the well-cleared and well-sifted simple medicines <term>Simplicia: single-ingredient drugs</term> that my conscience calls me to use. One would find no lack of clumsiness here if someone were to take the broom a little better in hand. But consider this further: they see in this list "Laranzi" <note>likely a corruption of a mineral or botanical term</note> and many more than are marked, which are rejected in special chapters because no such "Laranzi" is useful for the French disease. Furthermore, they cannot stand alongside the other pieces—such as litharge, minium, white lead, etc.—without the destruction of the body; and in the case of mercury, it is a poison and an inflammation that does not end without great sorrow.

The same is understood of the litharge, white lead, and bole, etc., that they cannot stand here with the others; while the power of the others is to penetrate the body, these have the power to block it, so that they cause constipation and the disease cannot find an opening. Now consider what is being concealed here and what kind of work it is. Likewise, there would be much more absurdity if their lack of understanding were not spared.

They use gums, the nature of which is nothing other than to heal where they lie with their "body" <note>the physical substance of the drug</note>; and they place the substance where it rots, and drive it into the body with their ointments, imagining it should go into every corner of the whole body, but it does not move from its spot. Thus they also use sandalwood of all colors for the sake of the color—as if the color helps the sick—and the others likewise. They use cinnabar also, but with more reason: that is, because it has mercury in it, which makes it mild, colors it, and makes the speech heavy; he <note>the doctor</note> might even swear an oath upon it that no "living" <note>liquid/metallic</note> mercury is present that the peasants would recognize.

<margin>How to use mercury artistically. Page 158.</margin>
Their main ingredient is mercury, with which they deal strangely. They pound it so long with grease or bear's fat until it shows their will. Now know that it gladly enters the body, and once it gets inside, it runs together again from the bodily heat and settles in the cavities of the joints, etc. The damage it does while lying there is obvious. Look at an example in Idrija <note>original: "Nidria," a famous mercury mining town</note>: all who live around it are crooked and lame, easily suffocated, easily frozen, and can never expect true health. Also, if you lay your hands on a wooden bowl in which mercury lies several times, you will find yourself so unhealthy that your spirit trembles at it; how much more so when such a weight lies in the body and you can never be released from it. From this spring hidden, incurable diseases; such things should not be undertaken unless it <note>mercury</note> is not used <insert>in this raw form</insert>.

Furthermore, since the peasants know how to test for mercury in the lard, they have devised another trick: they calcine it in *aqua fortis* <note>nitric acid</note> and put it thus, warm and fresh, into the ointments. Such a thing is double in its malice. For it is subtler and sharper; how then can it pass through with little damage? For its nature goes through the whole body and leaves nothing in the body unstained in such a form and composition as they use it.

They use it sublimated only so that the common man does not recognize it in the ointment; it causes heavier and greater side effects than the living mercury. Some use it coagulated and consider it to be without harm; they do not consider that this coagulate opens up again as soon as it feels the warmth of the body.

Regarding this original cause alone, they do not consider the effect of the medicine, which is twofold: one that drives the phlegm from the veins out through the mouth <note>salivation</note>, the other through quiet and subsiding heat. Yet these two effects are no way to heal the French disease; rather, there is a property in mercury against the poison of the...

# On Impostures.

A. Is of the French <note>original: "Frantzosen"; a common historical term for syphilis, often called the "French Disease"</note>. This is the manner of those who act without consideration: only the phlegm exiting the mouth is their primary goal, through which they believe all healing easily occurs. Therefore, medicine is a Good—when practiced according to the Art—a gift of God, and not a gift of luck. With this, I wish to conclude the second Imposture, which maintains itself by luck without any Art, while I adhere to the Art and not to luck.

## The Third Imposture which I oppose is by
->Fumigation.<-

B. This Imposture was not started by any learned or experienced man, but by a perverse and cunning hider of the power of Mercury <note>original: "Mercurii"</note>, intended to blind the eyes of the sick. For this man is a cunning impostor who saw that he could not sustain himself or his reputation with salves as he pleased; he fell from favor so that salves became unpleasant to the peasants. Then he took up another deceit and gave this Imposture a perverse path, as if it were not to be Quicksilver <note>original: "Quecksilber"</note> at all. He claimed he could make people healthy through smoke without any Mercury: and thus he made a new art out of old rags, just like one who lets a white coat be turned black, yet praises himself for giving his body a good appearance. Thus, he took Cinnabar <note>original: "Zinobers"; a toxic mercury sulfide mineral</note> and devised a trick, for the common man did not know what Cinnabar was. Therefore, he could easily say to those who did not know the nature of Cinnabar:

B. [I use] Silver, and am not a physician like the others who know nothing but Quicksilver; rather, I use a red powder that performs before your eyes; I throw it into the fire and it shall be called masterly for you. Thus was this Imposture held as a praiseworthy thing, until the teeth and many other parts rotted out, and the uvula was stolen away <note>destroyed by mercury poisoning</note>, and they corrupted one another, became lame, and died. Thus this art was finally despised as well, when it was realized that Cinnabar is merely Quicksilver disguised so that it may flow about.

<margin>Cinnabar</margin>
In this art, there is no master left who opposes me, nor does anyone desire to describe it further to those they command. But I have spoken against it for the sake of the destruction they inflict through their fumigation; in one way, they cause the teeth to fall out, and the feet <note>likely referring to the base of the teeth or mobility</note> lie in the mouth, so that the roots of the teeth and the uvula must rot; they heat and burn the chest. And let us consider that the sickness does not lie in that same place; parts where the sickness never resided nor reached are rotted and ruined by them, and the kidneys and livers are destroyed thereby, so that they must publicly confess that their art is nothing but an Imposture. But there is one more thing in their "beauty": they have sought out Simples <note>term: Simplicia; individual medicinal herbs or ingredients used to make compounds</note> to give the Cinnabar a sweet taste and hide the stench, so it would not be recognized (taken by nobles and commoners, women and men alike), and these are the pieces from which their art proceeds:

C. Cinnabar from the mountain <note>natural ore</note>, Cinnabar from the Art <note>synthetic</note>,
Calcined Mercury,
Sublimated Mercury,
<term>Alipia Mulcata</term> <note>likely a corruption of a botanical or mineral term, possibly related to spurge or a prepared salt</note>,
Frankincense,
Mastic <note>original: "Malix"</note>,
Myrrh,
Cloves <note>original: "Negelin"</note>,
Cinnamon <note>original: "Zummet"</note>,
Peony root <note>original: "Fentwurs"</note>,
Musk <note>original: "Bisen"</note>.

How these pieces can be a medicine is easy to learn. Put as much good as they want under the poison, the poison must still work and abandon all the good pieces. Now see how they will maintain their medicine against me.

## The Fourth Imposture, which maintains itself against me
->with Eating.<-

L. A common Imposture is at hand, which nevertheless wants to be powerfully defended, and has such hard, unmerciful, stubborn physicians that they do not even want one to speak to them regarding the Imposture of Eating <note>referring to restrictive or extreme dietary cures</note>, which is maintained with force and without any understanding, even against the innate nature of any physician. In this, truly, every man may judge for himself that the Imposture of these heads is reaching too far: and the business proves itself to be nothing experienced, and in all things an unhealthy medicine, adopted in a defiant, willful manner against its own nature and essence. In this, truly, is nothing other than a presumed defiance and boasting, as if to force the sickness through pride: "You must go away, and skin and bone shall go with you." And they undertake to subdue the sick and the sicknesses which it is not possible to overcome through such a struggle.

# Of the French Disease: The First Book
<sig>A</sig>
It is a pity that eating-washes <note>original: "Esen" or "Esung," referring to corrosive or caustic applications used to "eat away" diseased flesh</note> are used so insolently and without any understanding upon open sores, in which—especially according to all true physicians—no corrosive should be applied to open sores. There is no other reason for it than an unbridled, proud spirit: they do not want to acknowledge the good flesh that lies beneath it, and so they make it wider and worse than it is of itself. They shall not throw my argument back at me here, for in no way should these be produced, because they are as they are; they claim the nature of this "cleansing" <note>original: "Mundification," the surgical process of cleaning a wound</note> takes everything away. The flesh in itself is not evil, but in the conflict of the French "flow" <note>original: "Fluß," referring to the humoral theory of morbid fluids or miasma</note>, the whole flesh is used up. He who has this understanding, and uses corrosives until flesh and bone are gone, always presumes to help and does not consider the outcome. They also do not consider that the pains of the corrosive are a poison at that very site.

<margin>Physician</margin>
Therefore, I set down in the following with what corrosives they maintain themselves, so that you all may weigh for yourselves how great an imposture and how remarkably harmful it is to life when they use these in open sores. Through this, it will be found that I do not need to overturn them, but they overturn themselves.
<sig>B</sig>
Sublimated Mercury with burnt Tartar.
Sublimated Mercury with Vitriol <note>sulfate minerals</note>,
Sublimated Arsenic to the point of redness,
Sublimated Arsenic of the first attachment,
Common white Arsenic,
Common yellow Arsenic,
Common smoke of Orpiment <note>original: "Aurins Pigment," a deep yellow arsenic sulfide mineral</note>,
Sublimated Orpiment <note>original: "Oppermet"</note>,

The *Aqua Fortis* in itself,
The *Caput Mortuum* <note>The "dead head" or useless residue left after distillation</note> of *Aqua Fortis*,
The Alkali Anatron <note>Native soda or saltpeter</note>.
The salts boiled from lye, from lime and wood-ashes.
Burnt red Vitriol, which they call the "Red Heink," dissolved Sal-Ammoniac water, which they call the "Brullen."
A caustic oil of Tartar with Mercury, Sublimate, or Arsenic,
Burnt Alum,
Burnt Alum causticized with vinegar.
These are corrosives and "eating-vinegars" with which one could bore through the Pillars of Hercules and eat through horse-iron:

<margin>Physician</margin>
Of the aforementioned items, there is not one that would work only on a good person and not an evil one. For any rotten, dead flesh in which there is no life—the corrosive does not attack that, for it is already that which the corrosive intends to make it. But the living flesh that is still good, it works itself into that. For it is the intention and nature of every corrosive to harm the living and not the dead; it is also its nature to bring an end to life, as can easily be measured by the nature of any poison. One can see how they maintain their art of "eating." In the end, they "heal" a sore by bringing their folly and lack of understanding to light through their imposture, and many—before they ever reach health—are first ruined, tormented, and miserably burdened.

When the corrosive was not accepted or the gasping <note>original: "Keuchen," perhaps referring to respiratory distress from fumes</note> was rejected, they took those same substances and placed them in brandy <note>original: "Brentenwein"</note> and washed with it so that those poisonous pustules were drawn out. ### The Sixth Imposture, which undertakes to justify their cause against me with cutting.
->to justify.<-

<image-desc>Decorative initial capital C</image-desc>
C <term>Stupidity</term> <note>Erdrossenheit</note> of the time and <term>ignorance</term> in <term>medicine</term>, also the <term>pride</term> of having nothing to experience or learn, has devised a shortcut with <term>cutting</term> <note>surgery</note>. Thus, what their mad understanding thinks should be cut, they want to make <term>war-wounds</term> out of holes. How a mad mind considers itself, in a way, that the ignorance is there, not knowing what they should cut: furthermore, that the adverse thing should be taken away. But in the negligence of such faithful experience of <term>medicine</term>, they undertake to protect such <term>imposture</term> and wretched work with terror. Therefore, three have become healthy, and the two shall answer and suffice for that which the forty have paid for; and shall it be a greater art to keep two and ruin forty, than to keep forty and ruin two? A physician who should be born of a faithful foundation should use such unstable <term>medicine</term>. Although I admit their justification, they can do nothing better: how honest is the answer to a physician who should be so horrified that in these people it cannot be kept silent until death: that is a secret robbery under the guise of <term>medicine</term>, and is a true <term>poison</term> of contempt. How can they then excuse themselves that they are not of the number of the <term>Venetian soups</term>? Every physician should guard himself in his conscience so that he is not guilty of such things. From thousands, the <term>medicine</term> should be laid down, so that such contempt comes from none of <unclear>yours</unclear>. I will thus have their <term>imposture</term> sufficiently placed not in the rank of physicians, but of impostors.

Their art is not to be described, other than by <term>cutting</term> and hacking, which I entirely contradict in this way: that the right, true <term>medicine</term> is so powerful that it, without all <term>pains</term>, does away with that which they want to accomplish with <term>cutting</term>. And I will have them overthrown by this: that their <term>cutting</term> is a double <term>imposture</term>, arising from great <term>ignorance</term> and despair of natural help, and that they should not or may not be called physicians. For <term>cutting</term> does not take away the cause. Therefore it is only a deceptive healing, in which no lasting confidence or foundation of <term>medicine</term> has any origin or basis. To make a hole into a <term>war-wound</term> does not take away the cause and the <term>poison</term>. But one skill is to be praised in them: they lay it in the wood, in the <term>smithy</term>, etc. When they themselves...

### The Seventh Imposture, which has torn itself down with Sweating and Bathing, and yet at times tries to raise itself up again.

S Some have undertaken (most of all among the Italians <note>original: "Welschen"</note> / after which it also reached the Germans) to drive out the French Disease with sweating or bathing: But the disease would not yield. Therefore, they recognized the error of their art or medicine / and abandoned it again: Yet they often attacked it again / and yet could accomplish nothing. In such sweating, they have devised many things / so that they might maintain and protect their art. But who has ever seen the French Disease driven out with sweating? The substances they take for it serve only to remove the wateriness of the blood: What does that have to do with the French Disease? If sweating were to drive out the French Disease / then a warm oven / or a warm bellows would have been good for it / and the dog days of summer. It is a thoughtless undertaking by a physician / who attempts such medicine / and does not know the illness / wanting to use the medicine for the Plague against the French Disease: With what understanding this happens / proves itself.

<sig>B</sig>

### The Ninth Imposture, which seeks to overcome me through the Quintessence and Alchemical tricks.

<margin>S</margin> I have considered several individuals who, because they have seen that in medicine there have been certain secret techniques <note>The author refers to "griff" or "grips," meaning specialized manual or technical methods</note> which were hidden from all physicians, believed they should possess the power of addition and subtraction <note>The ability to manipulate the fundamental properties of matter</note> as it exists in Nature. Although through such sharp preparation the degrees <term>Gradus: the intensity or potency of a substance's qualities</term> of things are raised high into the subtle realm, and just as another thing might well occur through something striking. Now, however, there are three reasons why they accomplish nothing in this: First, that their work attacks the body too severely on account of its extreme subtlety. Second, that these same materials are not recognized according to the order of Nature, but are instead entrusted haphazardly to experiments—that is, to luck, however it may fall out.

If this is not to be an imposture, then make something better out of it; and if medicine is to be based on such certainties, then it must walk on stilts. If they wish to gain honor with this and defend the "French" practitioners, they must use strange tricks.

### The Eleventh Imposture / Those who set themselves up against me for the sake of the Saints.

Now that the game is becoming complete, I had expected that I would have had enough opposition from men; but as if that were not enough, alas! Saints must also be set against me—whose arts and medicine I might well have accepted. But since they do not represent their office themselves, but rather their "officials" <note>Referring to priests or shrine-keepers who claimed healing powers through saints.</note> do, I learned that their medicine was not humane, but knavish. But first, note which of the Saints' messengers set themselves against me:

Saint Vitus <note>original: "Sanct Fiecht"</note>—he answers for the French disease.
Saint Quirinus—answers for the <term>swollen legs</term><note>original: "Dellschenckel"</note>.
Saint John—for the throbbing open sores.
And Saint Dionysius—for the smallpox <note>original: "Blatern"</note>.
And many such others, like Saint Anthony, St. Veletti, and the like; truly, this happened without the Saints' command. They wanted, by force, to claim that as their officials, the diseases were commanded not to medicine, but to the Saints with their blessing.

I must briefly reveal some part of this. You know that sorcery is of many kinds. If it were to happen under the name of sorcery, no one would permit it, nor would it have any special respect, but would be a horror to the world. Now, one must blind the people and attribute the same thing to the Saints, so that it has some success; from this it follows that Saints have been found to be harnessed to such things. Thus, the resort to sorcery is stirred up, and faith is only then fully confirmed.

Some have applied themselves and moved with practices through which the sick have become healthy, and attributed that praise to the Saints, thus carrying out a blinded piece of mischief. To explain this rightly would require a book of its own.

How I feel about them, however, is easy to gauge; I wish to have sufficiently answered them herewith, as will be particularly found in the writing *On Superstitions* <note>original: "de superstitionibus"</note>.

### The Twelfth Imposture / which reached me from my own servants.

<margin>A</margin>
When I, out of faithful service, provided for and opened my heart to my servants—which they had not earned—they presumed that all my secrets were revealed to them, and that they possessed all my <term>Arcana</term> <note>Secret knowledge or alchemical mysteries</note>. Now, when they saw that through these very secrets I was able, and am still able, to overturn certain languages, arts, professions, and other matters, they prepared themselves and went back on their promises to me. This was not done with an honorable spirit; rather, they were ashamed that they should be conquered by knowing no more than what they had received from me. # On the French Disease: The First Book.

<sig>A</sig>

### The Fifteenth Imposture: Those who have set themselves up in many languages.

<sig>B</sig>
Several sects arose who wanted to overthrow me with Hebrew, Greek, Chaldean, and Arabic. Now, the matter rested on my interpretation; however, I cannot accept an interpreter based on words, but rather on works <note>Paracelsus emphasizes "works" (results) over "words" (theory).</note>. What does it help me to lie or to show interpretations, since I, as a physician of truth and not of lies, should be a Doctor? The works interpret themselves—they do not reward you—so firm and truthful is medicine in itself. This means I interpreted that which, in the Greek and Hebrew codices, also has its power in German. But since they interpreted much of the Greek (which is otherwise drawn with lies), they ultimately accomplish nothing. Why should that sweet chatter gladden me and the sick? No language is to be believed above another; therefore, interpretation should happen through works, for that is certain and not false. Lying and chattering are common to all languages and are described in all of them.

Now, however, regarding how to act so that those who know what *Chiros* <note>original: "Chiros" - likely referring to surgical hand-work or a specific manual affliction</note> is, and what *Hydrops* <note>term: Hydrops - Edema or dropsy, an accumulation of fluid in the body</note> and the like are, may also know how to help those lying sick with them: for *Chiros* requires much skill, and *Hydrops* a great cure. If they can heal it, then I thank the dear Greeks; if not, let them keep their theoretical chatter. For we Germans care only for the healing. It might perhaps be the same for you with other Greek things; far be that from the physician.

It is the greatest seduction of medicine circulating in my time: that many, who know nothing else but a little of the Greek language—as they learned it when they were schoolmasters and proofreaders, and when they were with Erasmus <note>referring to Desiderius Erasmus, the famous humanist scholar</note>—now, because some medical books have begun to appear in Greek, they imagine that because they govern the books, they also govern the sick. And so they teach how to read the Greek books, and when they have learned them by heart, they still know nothing, yet they become Doctors. They should not be called physicians, but Greeks. No physician should [act] with practice alone. Not even with a *Spagirlin* <note>term: Spagyric - The alchemical process of separating and recombining plant or mineral components to create medicine</note> are the Greeks more gifted; they think their language is the whole world. Take this as an example: there are peasants among the coarsest Swabians and the coarsest Bavarians who have brought about more healings than all your writers of the Greek language. And take this seriously, for it is true. If the Greeks were so good, then the proofreaders in Greek would have the correction of medicine alone in their hands, yet they all deal only with the letter of the text.

Who wants to know who the first physician was? Perhaps the first was never recorded, and perhaps only the one was recorded who picked up the crumbs under the table and wanted to make baskets full of bread out of them with heavy labor. Who is he who wants to rely on all his future [prospects]? Or who wants to trust their writings since the evidence does not hang there, nor any testimony that they are true? Enough has been written, but there is little healing. In addition, one must despair in such arts, since he himself claims nothing of the foundation; who then can [apply] the flail to such trifles? The facts and works overthrow them themselves, so that I have no need to be particularly concerned against them. They want to overthrow the "French Disease" <note>original: "Fransen" - a common term for syphilis in the 16th century</note> in my writings through the ancient teachers, but the ancients know nothing about it. Furthermore, they have recognized nothing at all of the heavens in their course—what they will give in the future—but have only considered the present. Moreover, they want to overcome me with Greek, yet the disease is German and not Greek, French and not Arabic.

### The Sixteenth Imposture: Those who almost missed out at the end; perhaps they waited for the grass [to grow], and these are the "leathered" pharmacists.

<sig>C</sig>
What an imposture, to have undertaken something so excellent. But as the foundation was, so it was ended: and they grew up in the pharmacies, those who were ashamed of cooking. They imagined they were worth more honor than to move about so deceitfully in the pharmacy. Although they did not take up an unskillful argument, in that they see the simplicity and trade of the Doctors, which proceeded without great art, of which they also had enough. Now, I cannot hold that against them as an evil, for they saw that there was no art in their writers, but rather a...

### Of Impostures

A <note>The letter 'A' likely refers to a specific section or argument in the author's broader treatise on medical fraud.</note> who [provided] a saddle for and riding in syrups and pills. And so, since they were accustomed to such things, they were able to do it, and saw that there was nothing there but a stroke of luck, which in such a form had succeeded for every <term>Remmetseger</term> <note>A regional or archaic term for a charlatan or a bungler.</note>.

In the same way, they have learned more arts from the <term>Impostoribus</term> <note>Impostors</note>, sausage-sellers, <term>Triackersträmern</term> <note>Sellers of theriac, a famous "universal" herbal cure-all often sold by peddlers.</note>, from barbers and bath-masters, all of whom were namely only the best: for the poor ones cannot speak in pharmacies. And so all arts have flown into the shops for them. How then can such an apothecary not be full of art? Now it happens so luckily for him—if they were fish in a net, he would cover the Black Forest with the bones.

Who wants to dispute with such a highly learned man, or how can I resist him, who has a great run of arts, while they hunger with the lice? It is well-regarded that the arts do not possess cities; all Germany would drown from them if one were only as large as a half-measure of wine. But I consider, since they are entirely invisible among them, they will remain invisible, and thus melt away with the <term>sernigen</term> <note>Likely "last year's" or "old"</note> snow.

But I remain undaunted, for the birds they carry in have been plucked. Therefore they may not keep their feathers either; they despise them, for they also know that they and theirs are the same; the pupil will be no better. Although they have a daily accustomed practice among them, which together would have a great advantage. But since they come into the pharmacies in the manner of marksmen, they must also remain marksmen. For their first discipline is pounding, then to decoct the <term>Sudelwerck</term> <note>Slovenly or messy work; a derogatory term for their concoctions.</note>. ## The Seventeenth Imposture, of Roller Bandages.

C A trick has been invented by the doctors, who have seen and noticed that the "fluxes" <note>Humoral fluids thought to cause swelling or discharge.</note> had attacked the open sores and legs; and so that they might earn their <term>Gelstlein</term> <note>Small amounts of money/fees.</note>, they took an example from little books, which leave an impression when they are misplaced. Thus they also devised a meaning and directed the fluxes, and extended them enough through such [bandages], so that they remain unprepared by fluxes in their open sores, as long as they drew out the money.
Now it is an imposture, for the reason that they consider their own profit and not the patient's, in that they delay, and know no understanding of their healing: And if it were the case that the body internally must pay for it—when medicine was conducted so cheaply, and the poison that arises from wrong medicine was never to be considered—then anyone might well use medicine with good honor.
The medicines they use are also not comforting; doctor and medicine go well together: In the trade they are to set up, a burnt glue from an old oven would do just as well. But the <term>Bosels</term> <note>A bungler or a specific type of tool/material.</note> has more appearance before the eyes. But in virtues, the potter is a good apothecary. Since they are not certain of their medicine, or may rot in a good end, I judge it to have been sufficiently overturned. I shall also be found free of them, as of others.

## The Eighteenth Imposture, of Cauterization.

So know herein, that it is a contrary, unrhymed art, spoken of by fools and by no wise men, who are always pleased with strange juggling tricks, and always pushed to the point that they torment the sick and cause pain. ## The Nineteenth Imposture
### regarding Lead Plasters.

<margin>L</margin> Several physicians have devised the making and applying of lead plasters. Although they may have some
backing from books <note>original: "Rucken von den Büchern," implying historical or textual authority</note>, they nevertheless have no justification for using such against the French Disease.
Now, it is an imposture because they use lead in place of mercury; for while molten lead is like mercury, it is not yet mercury. Although lead also has a mercurial nature <note>In alchemy, "mercurial" refers to the volatile, transformative principle of a metal</note> within it, through which it might be somewhat powerful in healing the French Disease, it is not so in this form, but rather in the preparation; therefore, it is an imposture. If they wish to use it in such a form, no mercury must be raised with it <note>likely referring to the alchemical process of sublimation or extraction</note> so that its effect may be opened and brought to use; this occurs through retraction. Thus, their simplicity reveals their own folly, which overthrows itself and is recognized as unfit, leaving me to stand further in my glory.

## The Twentieth Imposture
### regarding the Depletion of the Limbs.

<margin>L</margin> It is just as with the roller bandages; there has arisen another art which is supposed to divert the flows <note>humors or discharges</note> that have gone to the injuries by cutting off the path. Now, however, it is just as with the roller bandages: the cutting off of the body is ruinous in all French flows. Unless it be the case that you wish to ruin the body and keep the thigh healthy; otherwise, do not let yourself be seen with this imposture in the French Disease. Although this is an excellent cure in flows that are *not* French, it is all the more adverse in the French Disease. Therefore, let them be overturned, unless you know the nature of the flow and that the body is without harm.
<margin>B</margin>

## Conclusion.

<margin>A</margin> Thus, I would have everyone exhorted and requested, whoever is a faithful physician, to consider for himself the cause of the indicated impostures, and observe thereby what has also happened to him because of them. In which I also understand nothing else from you, learned physicians, than that a service has been done for everyone; my grievance is also your grievance, and in my excuse, I excuse both you and myself. If I *were* to ask them not to take this in a bad way, their bellies might perhaps grow large <note>an idiom for becoming puffed up with pride or anger</note>. But they will mumble and grumble, drawing their mouths together as if they had eaten sloe-berries and wooden spoons <note>a metaphor for a bitter or sour expression</note>. And those who do not wish to be considered impostors, yet carry it hidden within them, will make themselves manifest—those who are otherwise sought after as steadfast in their speech. And I wish herewith to have revealed all these impostures; perhaps they will cause more to be investigated.
<margin>otherwise</margin>
<margin>Prayers.</margin>
<margin>C</margin>

End of the First Book.

# The Second Book, in which is treated the medicines for all kinds of diseases that have been misused until now.

### CHAPTER I.

<image-desc>Large decorated initial 'S' with a face in profile and foliage.</image-desc>
Since I have now finished the First Book according to my intention, and therein recounted all the diseases that might oppose me, which also violated the arts of truth. So in this book, it is further my intention to begin completing the aforementioned impostures <note>The author uses "impostures" to refer to fraudulent or misguided medical practices</note> which they think to maintain. For I am indeed certain that they have established something useful through their imposture (and truly not much of it), yet they wish to be protected by it, and yet do not know how or in what way this happens; also out of such ignorance and lack of understanding, they wish to draw a piece of favor for themselves. So it will be further necessary to discover something in this. For I can well recognize that this art, which was previously rejected, cannot stand without excellent secrets <note>original: "Heimligkeit," referring to hidden natural powers or alchemical mysteries</note>. But for that reason, it is forbidden that they be called impostures, and why they are impostures would be indicated in this book, namely that they misuse the secret and are no further experienced than to pour poison and secret together.

Upon this, I will show what good may happen in their impostures, and show the same without any imposture, so that the virtue which God has given to medicine may not be rejected by me—as the impostors think—but rather to discover their secret as highly as possible for me, and to recount from chapter to chapter in particular how they mixed the secret and the imposture, and how the same should be separated from the imposture.

### CHAPTER II.

<image-desc>Large decorated initial 'J' with foliage.</image-desc>
In the following indication, you should know a common entrance, before you read the following chapters, that you carry in yourselves a prior knowledge of the anatomy of diseases—not of the body, but of the body of the diseases. Therein know such an example: How will a physician apply medicine to the parts of the disease while he does not know the site of the disease? Herein lies a great reason to fail in the healing of diseases. For example, who is he who could heal the one whom jaundice possesses in the body? But he will heal it well and easily who knows where the sites are to be sought in that same place.

<margin>Most practical 26. 104. 105. 263. C. 156.
<image-desc>Three Chinese characters written vertically.</image-desc></margin>
This is spoken regarding the fact that you smear the joints of the body, the shoulders, and the places that hurt or do not hurt with ointments. Likewise with washing, you wash the sites without considering what further arises from it. That is, you do not consider how far the anatomy of the medicine goes. If it goes further than the disease is, then it is a poison. If it does not go as far as the disease reaches in its anatomy, then it is too weak. Now mark this point well, that herein lies the first beginning of practice <term>Practick: the clinical application of medical theory</term>: if you smear the joints, your anatomy of the medicine goes further than the disease, as in washing. Now it follows from this that you should know the tree of the disease and the extension of its branches, and then remain only in the tree and not act further. If the disease is in the veins, such as an open sore that comes from the *salvatella* veins <note>original: "Salvatellos," referring to the vein on the back of the hand, then thought to have specific healing properties</note>. So the site will lie in these veins alone, and alone receive the medicine, and otherwise no other part of the body is to be disturbed. I indicate this here only so that the greatest imposture may be removed, and how the anatomy of the disease and the medicine should be understood is not my intention here, but is sufficiently shown in *On the Origin of Ulcers* <note>original: "de Origine Ulcerum"</note>, in which everyone should know themselves to be experienced.

### CHAPTER III.

Now know herein, that in the French diseases <note>Syphilis</note> the main components are Mercury and Marcasite <note>original: "Mercurius. Marcas."</note>, and without these, the French disease cannot be cured. Therefore mark that other compounds or simples <term>Simplicia: medicines made of only one constituent, usually a herb</term> which are added are in vain and without help. Since now the Mercurial nature is that which alone has the power in itself, and in what way its virtue and strength stand in that place, and...

how the same are to be administered. Although great medicine has been sought in other simples <note>Medicines made of only one ingredient, usually herbal.</note> and in many ways and forms, yet nothing appropriate was found, except what the time and the goodness of the sickness allowed. ### CHAPTER IV.

#### Concerning the First Imposture.

<margin>Lutius Cornarius book 21, chapter 188, page 249.</margin>
<insert>I</insert> have found in the first imposture the error of the doctors: that they purge the four humors <note>The traditional Galenic system of medicine based on balancing blood, phlegm, yellow bile, and black bile.</note> and seek the sickness therein, which has very little or nothing at all to do with them. For our "French Disease" <note>Syphilis.</note> should in no way be understood according to the writings of Avicenna <note>A famous Persian physician (980–1037) whose "Canon of Medicine" dominated European universities.</note> and his followers. Therefore, if those writings and those of his kind are cast aside, the very greatest imposture is gone. The reason is: they have adapted themselves to the wood <note>Likely referring to Guaiacum or "Holy Wood," a common but often ineffective herbal treatment for syphilis.</note> in such a way that they begin with purging, either according to the true Avicenna—who never had knowledge of the French Disease—or, if they did understand him rightly, they would not be healing the French Disease in vain. Thus they have also set themselves to smearing, smoking, washing, etc., and say: "One must first of all digest and purge," so that the medicine might finish that imposture, and they have made the same even greater. Therefore know, that in no way is such an order to be accepted, for they have no main point in all their purging that could attack even the least of the French Disease.

But if the French Disease cannot be opened up without purging, but must be purged, then know only one main point of purgation: and that is the Mercurial power, without which the sickness can in no way be attacked. Now, purging is not only through the stool—indeed, least of all through the stool—nor only through the mouth, but also through the pores, and the sweat, and the like. That is the right medicine, which drives out a sickness and distinguishes how to draw it according to its nature. For example, Colocynth <note>A bitter cucumber used as a harsh laxative.</note> wants to go out from below, and even if the sickness does not have its emunctory <note>An organ or opening that carries off waste, like a sweat gland or kidney.</note> at that place, it must still go out. What good comes of that is easy to imagine. Likewise Hellebore <note>A toxic plant used to induce vomiting.</note> wants to go out from above; now the sickness must follow it. These are all contrary orders which you should guard against, and only take for yourself the medicine that shows the sicknesses their own emunctory; for otherwise, in other ways, it does not happen without harm.

If purging is to go through the emunctory of the sickness and not through the emunctory of the medicine, then you will find in all of Mesue, Rhazes, and Avicenna <note>original: "Melue, Lumine, Rafi, Avicennæ" - referring to the great medieval medical authorities.</note> that they have nothing at all for purging the French Disease; rather, you must undertake a new foundation. For this is a new sickness, and this is a mineral medicine, and the minerals stand in three parts, and so also the French Disease and its medicine. Therefore, those who have open sores want to be purged through that same emunctory; and that which lies in the roots will be brought to the emunctory. And thus, as each thing requires its emunctory, one must act accordingly. Therefore, nothing purges more highly, more fortunately, or more thoroughly than the *Essentia Mercurialis* <note>The essential spirit or chemical essence of Mercury.</note>, when it is prepared into the power of the laxatives, which laxative names are called as follows:

### The First.
Vitriolated Sulphur,
Mercurial Sap,
Precipitated Mercury of Metals.

### The Second.
Liquefied Vitriol.
Laxative *Chimolea* <note>A term for certain types of earth or powder used in alchemy.</note>.

### The Last.
Extracted Mercury of Minerals.

## Explanation.

**Vitriolated Sulphur** is a sulfur that separates itself from vitriol, which is similar to the dregs of Black Hellebore.
**Liquefied Vitriol** is the vitriol that is drawn out of the ore and does not allow itself to be coagulated.
**Mercurial Sap** is a water made from the aluminous minerals in which Mercury is born.
**Laxative Chimolea** is a powder that is rubbed off from the "flowers of the emperors" <note>original: "Blumen der Caissern" - likely a specific alchemical precipitate.</note>.
**Precipitated Mercury of Metals** is a restoration of metals into their first matter, subsequently precipitated within itself.
**Extracted Mercury of Minerals** is a substance that is drawn out from ores, silver, and gold, etc.

<summary>Paracelsus rejects traditional Galenic purging (humoral theory) for treating syphilis, arguing instead for a "new foundation" based on mineral-based Mercury. He lists specific chemical preparations—such as vitriolated sulfur and precipitated mercury—that align with the body's natural exit points for disease.</summary>

## On the Recipes for Fumigation.

<sig>A</sig>
<note>The initial 'S' begins the sentence "Sehr gehöret habt..."</note>
You have heard much regarding how your imposture <note>The author frequently uses "imposture" to refer to the fraudulent or incorrect methods of contemporary doctors</note> persists in its ways regarding the recipe and process of fumigation, and that you should entirely abandon both. Although it is true that you occasionally effect a cure, nevertheless, because it happens so improperly and only ends well by great luck, it is such an unskillful practice that no place or room should be given to this lack of skill. It is true that all Mercury <note>original: "Mercurius"; refers to the element mercury, central to Paracelsian medicine</note> shows its effect in many ways: in its smoke, in its vapor, its chaos, its steam. And this is explained by the fact that Mercury is so subtle; moreover, just as warmth comes from a stove, so a vapor goes out from the body of Mercury. And if one sits near it constantly, etc., and does not touch it, but only its warmth which goes from the body, when it touches the vapor of Mercury, then the power of Mercury is within it. Therefore, Mercury is to be wondered at in many ways, for such a nature belongs to it alone. But for that reason, no one should involve themselves with it just because it is a strange thing and think that it is therefore good.

So know this: that through such smoke or vapor, the *emunctoria* <term>emunctoria: excretory organs or pores through which the body expels waste</term> should be recognized, through which that same flow shall have its exit; the vapor should be applied to that same exit. Know also that where the exits have natural holes, they should [be directed] to specific holes; otherwise, the fumigation of Mercury at that place is in vain, for it cannot accomplish its intended exit.

<sig>B</sig>
Now, if something is to be treated through such vapor of Mercury, the Mercury must be prepared into an *attractive* <note>a medicine that draws out morbid matter</note>. And know herein that there is more which should be of the greatest concern for you to know in the practice of Mercury: that Mercury is so natured that it may be directed to constipate, to purge, to soothe, to consolidate, to cleanse, etc. And in whatever way one has need of it, it should be brought to that state. Just as some "Frenchmen" <note>referring to those afflicted with the French Disease/syphilis</note> are treated by means of gold-tinting <note>original: "dorierung"</note>, some by diaphoretics <term>diaphoretics: medicines used to induce sweating</term>, etc. In such matters, they should be submissive in the application, if one wishes to heal them. Therefore, know also at this place that in the form of smoke, it can do nothing else than like a sublimate <note>a chemically purified solid</note> that goes to the heart and kills, or like its physical body ruins the entire corpse.

<sig>C</sig>
But if this way is to be used, you shall prepare it in the manner that the sickness requires for a proper expulsion. Then, as stated above, observe the time and the place of the eyes. Now the preparation of Mercury for smoke, or in the manner of vapor, as this chapter contains, is thus: The Mercury shall first be "roasted" with sulfur, like a cinnabar; then sublimate it from the sulfur with as much saltpeter as they both weigh. Thereafter, take the Mercury and put it into an instrument that is two spans high, made of fired earth, wide at the bottom and narrow at the top. And arrange it in such a way that the *emunctorium* from which [the disease] is to be drawn and the narrow opening of the instrument fit together with skillful understanding. Then arrange a fire and the instrument so that the Mercury becomes hot, but does not smell <note>likely meaning it should not reach the point of acrid combustion</note>; do this according to the appearance of the person and the sickness, and the content of experience. Through this warm vapor, as the instrument takes the effect from the Mercury, it acts upon the *emunctorium* without any harm, just as well or better than if the Mercury itself were there in the body. And guard yourself in every way so that the physical body and substance of Mercury is not used, but only the vapor alone; then nothing further shall happen to you as happens to those who drive the Mercury with its body and spirit into the body. From this, know that because the Mercury now lies in the body with its physical mass, new diseases are born there continually. This should always be understood so as to be avoided.

## CHAPTER X.

Just as it is the custom of those who know nothing to try many things out of the suggestion of their

## CHAPTER Xl.
->On the Correction of Sweating and Bathing.<-

It may not be contradicted, since sweating is an *emundatorium* <note>original: "Emundatorium" - a cleansing or purifying agent/process</note> through which are purified
certain kinds of the French Disease, that it is not right to omit the indication of its correction.
But not with theriacs or pestilence-waters, but rather by pursuing the main piece, which is
Mercury: the same shall then be brought into the *diaphoretic* <note>sweat-inducing</note> state; only then is it possible to heal the French Disease through
sweating.

Therefore, know herein that you should transform the nature of Mercury so that
it becomes a "bath-room" <note>original: "Badstuben"</note> out of itself; that is, that one sweats without a bath-house,
brought to that point solely through the Mercury. Then, when the Mercury causes sweat, it is certain
that this sweat is a health for that person. And without the Mercurial nature, all sweating is in vain.
Although many "sure-necks" <note>stubborn or overconfident people</note> have been somewhat helped by sweating: know, however, that nothing fundamental or firm is to be built upon it,
nor is such an art to be trusted. For it never signaled anything other than that at the last, when the sickness
was gone, or in its own undertaking to drive it out through its own sweating power, to which the external sweating
gave a little promotion, however it may have happened or been undertaken.

<header>ON THE CORRECTION OF IMPOSTURES</header>

## ON THE CORRECTION OF IMPOSTURES

A Therefore know, that where Nature does not drive out the sweat herself, all arts of sweating—except those of Mercury—are in vain. The preparation of which is thus: Take a **coagulated Mercury** <note>Mercury solidified or fixed through chemical processes</note> that has been coagulated with tin, and then lay it in a small golden bowl that stands mostly in strong wine vinegar. Upon this, pour a **distilled wine** <note>original: "Branten Wein"</note> that is most subtle in its spirit; light it and let it burn. Do this several times, and the Mercury, wine, and tin will turn into an oiliness. Keep this, and give one grain of it to drink in strong wine—the best is Traminer or old Alsatian—and sweat, and attend to the matter well, and hold fast to experience therein.

## CHAPTER XII.
### On the Correction of Roller Bandages.

S I have for a long time tolerated those who use roller bandages, for the reason that they have healed many fluxes and open sores by blocking the paths through which the fluids previously fell down, and through such blockage, the open sores were healed. Yet it is but an art for the thighs, and good for no other injury except flowing sores, which few undertake to heal. Therefore know, that this **imposture** <note>Referring here to a deceptive or superficial medical practice</note> should be put away, so that it is not used except for through-flowing sores; do nothing without this understanding. Now know, that in this imposture it must be prevented that the blocked flux does not collect in the body and become ulcers, from which death grows. This is done through **clear Mercury**, directed so as to resolve the **French sores** <note>Syphilitic ulcers</note> which collect internally in the body from the French fluxes.
B To make roller bandages is in itself no great art, for healing after such blockage may easily occur. The danger is that ulcers are caused, leading to a future recurrence. Such sudden accidents shall be averted through clear Mercury, according to this instruction: Take the Mercury and powder it, distilled through egg whites as often as necessary until it turns to a coral color; then give eight grains in a good confection. This takes away the fluxes that are displaced by roller bandages, as well as other fluxes swung through similar paths. This should all be done according to the nature and property of the flux, though it must often be administered.

## CHAPTER XIII.
### On the Correction of the Quintessence.

S Who is he who may correct the books and writings which they call the **Quintessence**? <note>The "fifth essence," a highly concentrated medicinal extract sought by alchemists</note> For they and others do not know what the Quintessence is; rather, their books are full of great, very great boasting without any foundation, and neither the works nor the names agree. For if one searches the *Quintessence* of **Arnoldus** <note>Arnold of Villanova, a famous medieval physician</note>—who is he for whom even the smallest letters therein are true? Likewise the books of **Rupescissa** <note>Johannes de Rupescissa, a 14th-century alchemist</note>, from which nothing in these writings can be proven; neither the **inventors** nor their **scholars** ever understood their own purpose. Since they have made a special practice of it, it can be clearly seen that they never understood the ground of the diseases, but merely followed a form. Therefore they devised strange labors and followed strange writings, and from their excessive squandering and boasting, their lies are revealed. For with them, one notices neither the understanding of the **philosophers, astronomers, nor physicians**, but rather an unthinking flood of sin is introduced, with no better foundation.

Although excellent secrets come from **Alchemy**, it has not reached this point without **sophistry** <note>Deceptive or fallacious reasoning</note>. For there are many therein who wish to learn with their eyes while being inexperienced in virtues. When they have seen one thing, they have made four hundred out of it, and thus chattered in confusion, mixing lies with truth so that nothing good is to be found. Therefore know, that the highest correction is that you give no belief to any boasting unless it be proven by sight. For where this art fails, it leaves very foul stains; it requires a great understanding born of experience, and not as the monks and "interest-alchemists" <note>original: "Zinsalchimisten," likely referring to those practicing alchemy only for profit</note> boast.

But know that in Alchemy are the secrets by which Mercury is prepared and brought forth, and from it the medicine is fashioned for this disease. And all medicines called the "Main Pieces" for the **French Disease** <note>Syphilis</note> cannot be made without alchemical preparation. No **apothecary** will cook anything good here unless he be excellently instructed in alchemical preparation, namely in the preparation of **salts, vitriols, alums**, and the like. In these things are found the secret virtues which alone contain the healing for these diseases. It is not necessary to "correct" this part, for their **method of preparation** <note>original: "modus præparandi"</note> holds true, and the hair-splitting of the presumed alchemists cannot turn it aside; in truth, there is more understanding in it than they themselves presume. For it happens to some faculties that they crow too early—shouting and dividing into thirds before the snow has melted—and being full of themselves, they boast of the virtuous earth before the grain has even been sown.

# On the French Disease / The Second Book.

### CHAPTER XIV.
#### On the Brass Boxes / that is / Barbers or Shearers.

The way in which the barbers or shearers—who carry those brass boxes <note>original: "Mesinen Büchslin"; these were the portable kits containing ointments and tools used by traveling barbers</note>—should be corrected is difficult to explain thoroughly. For they involve themselves with countless "merciful" arts and are so unskilled in practice. Because they have grown up and hardened themselves in this way from their youth, it is hard to even call it a method. They look like seafarers or vagabonds, and while they recognize each other's ignorance, they often despise their own arts. Even if one instructs them and gives them good tools, the medicine does not come from them; they always remain in their imposture. For they have wasted the time for learning skill by combing hair and scratching, learning from minor masters who could not maintain their own mastery except through habit.

However, if a proper correction is to occur, the first step is that the imposture they carry out with their brass boxes must be cast away: for no good medicine will allow itself to be carried in such a manner. Just as a painter who wishes to portray someone diligently uses many colors, they focus on the "colors" <note>metaphor for superficial appearances or fake remedies</note> up and down the streets; but this signifies nothing other than poor art. The salves contained therein cannot powerfully withstand any disease and are as useful to the sick as a cold Requiem <note>a funeral mass</note> is to the souls of the dead.

If they truly wish to be physicians and know the internal medicine <note>original: "Leibarsney"</note> for all the diseases they compare to wounds, they must know what they are dealing with. If they then ask "Doctor Hans" <note>a derogatory name for an unlearned or generic practitioner</note> for advice—alas, he knows nothing of the wounds, and you know nothing of the origin; thus both of you know nothing, and the patient is not helped. Therefore, look to your own business: for shaving beards makes no one healthy; you must know more. And even if you can cup and scratch well, you have not yet begun to learn medicine; and even if you can boil an "Apostolicum" <note>a specific type of cleansing ointment</note> or distinguish the Ram from the Fish <note>astrological signs used in medieval medicine</note>, you have still not begun. Therefore, the highest correction is to learn more and further, so that what you treat, you complete with experienced art and knowledge of the origin.

It also profits you nothing that you can heal wounds or broken bones: in the healing of the French Disease, you must follow other school-rules <note>original: "Schulrecht"</note>; these old ways are worth nothing. You must fill a different box, not smear with little knives or carry around "butter-boxes" <note>original: "Burresbüchslin"; likely a derogatory term for cheap salve containers</note> and many instruments with no art behind them—only measuring and not knowing why, cooling without benefit, and similar bungling <note>original: "grotteln"</note>. Align yourself with the fundamental truth; if you know that, you will yourself spit upon such clumsy work <note>original: "Bosselarbeit"</note>. Furthermore, no correction can help you unless you cast off your imposture and learn how the French Disease should be healed according to the contents of the previous and other writings.

---

### CHAPTER XV.
#### On the Correction of the Jews.

One should also correct the Jews, for they have never had any foundation of medicine among them, but have directed all their affairs toward knavery <note>original: "Büberey"</note>. Whatever they occasionally possess that makes them seem superior comes from others and not from themselves, or perhaps from accidental observation. As for their language, as much medicine as has been found in it, there is not enough theory or philosophy therein to discover the origin of the smallest scab <note>original: "Rauden"</note>. Nor is there enough to certainly learn how to drive away the smallest scale <note>original: "Schiepen"</note>. But because Hebrew is rare, they rely more strongly upon it in their corruption. Nothing is believed of them except what is believed of vagabonds; and because they had the most noble Patriarchs, they imagine themselves to be the most noble in medicine as well. Their best shot and shield is that they gain money honestly or dishonestly <note>original: "per fas und nefas"</note>.

Know also that they have never learned anything secret from God regarding medicine above other nations. For God has always distributed medicine equally, sharing it with the Heathens just as early as with others, and never held any reservation of medicine. Nor did He promise it to any nation specifically above the others, but regarded the German language just as well as the Hebrew, the Polish as the Chaldean. Whatever any nation boasts of having for itself while depriving another is based on arrogance. Also, there have been diseases and arts in other languages that were always unknown in this [Hebrew] language. No one should rely on this, for God has not preferred one language over the others, but has shared what is necessary everywhere, just as the sun shines on the whole earth.

<margin>Otherwise, because they kept it in memory and the other language never did, but instead arose as a pride of one language over the others. But it is a pride that bears no fruit; that is, even if the other language were full of this, and as rightful in speech as the others, they are still much better diseased and corrupted.</margin>

Although it is true that some languages have specifically described their daily experience, and thus kept it in memory while the other language never did, but instead forgave it in a "barbaric" way. From this, only a pride of one language over the others has arisen. But it is a pride that yields no fruit; that is, even if the other languages were full of this, and as linguistically valid as the others, they [the Jewish practitioners] still treat the French Disease with smears, washes, obsessed with urine, purging, and performing all sorts of monkey-business <note>original: "Affenspiel"</note>. They see...

# On the Correction of Impostures.

That the Christians are easily overthrown and wish to be deceived; they have more love for the Jews than for their own brothers, for which reason [the impostors] boldly venture it. They also see well that the Christians themselves know nothing, nor wish to learn anything; thus the Greeks <note>The author likely refers to those adhering to Greek medical authorities like Galen</note> push them aside; if they create a "taste" once a year, they have a hundred subjects and [the people] believe in it. Therefore, their correction is nothing other than that they themselves cast off their pretensions and teach the Foundation, as the Scriptures demonstrate, with right understanding.

### CHAPTER XVI.
On the Imposture of Greek Physicians.

<note>Large ornate initial 'S'</note> It was said above that no language is gifted a hair's breadth higher than another for the sake of medicine; so note that languages should be recognized by the physician in this way: one before the other. It happens that a disease may be in Persia and reign therein for a long time, and nowhere else in the world. This [disease] subsequently comes to the Greeks across the lands, then into Italy, into Germany, Gaul, Spain, etc. Thus, the language is only of so much use as one who knows the Persian language—not only the language, but also the other languages—can discover that same disease. In such a manner, the German language, the Gallic, the English, etc., might be necessary to the Persians. But from this it does not follow that the art belongs to the Persians alone—far from us!—or that the art stays only with them. Therefore, know regarding these things: where the diseases are, there are also the <margin>B</margin> <note>God</note> has not ordained it so [that one must travel], but rather where He provided man his dwelling, He also provided his food, drink, all necessities, and the medicine in his garden. But certain languages have broken forth—namely those most skilled at climbing—and testify [of themselves]; they have sought pride and described medicine according to their own understanding <unclear>...</unclear> the honey is oversalted, so that all other languages lick at it and <unclear>...</unclear> shared in their houses. But there must be something that is lacking <unclear>...</unclear> in these and all other things. It is useful, however, for a physician to know <gloss><term>Pathology</term> (the study of the nature of diseases)</gloss> what disease encountered the Greeks, what the Arabs, what the Saracens, the Italians, what comes from the earth, what from heaven, what from the elements, what is new, what is old, how this or that [came to be]. These all belong to a physician, not so that he wishes to keep only Greek, or commit himself only to Greek in the lands and places where Greek substances <unclear>...</unclear> no sick people are more misled than those led by <unclear>...</unclear> speech; he who knows nothing in German disputes in Greek, and he who knows nothing <unclear>...</unclear> in Alacutish <note>Likely a reference to a foreign or "barbaric" tongue</note>. Always coming with strange, wicked foreign things that people do not understand. Therefore, their correction lies solely in this: that they be physicians of their own fatherland, bearing good knowledge of the local ailments, understanding one thing from the other; and the main point should be [the land] of which he is a physician: not [treating] the people of the Rheingau out of Greek, or the Thuringians out of <unclear>...</unclear>. [God] did not set the Greeks as Jewish gods, or make them the Evangelists of medicine in Portugal, etc. But they have compared themselves to Rome, which has <margin>C</margin> <unclear>...</unclear> so the Greeks also [claim] medicine. And just as Latin protects Rome, [so they use Greek]. Regarding the Greek imposture: whichever language brings its trade into German will gain little praise from it.

### CHAPTER XVII.
On the Correction of the Wood.

<note>Large ornate initial 'S'</note> The correction of the Wood <note>Refers to Guaiacum or "Holy Wood," imported from the Americas to treat syphilis</note> is, fundamentally, that the Wood be found in its true nature, which is solely that of an <term>Incarnative</term> <note>A medicine that promotes the growth of new flesh/healing of wounds</note>; from this it is understood that only cleansed patients should be brought to it. If this imposture is put away, the greatest correction has already occurred.

Thereafter, know that because of the "unclean diseases" <note>Syphilis/The French Disease</note> which are not subject to the Wood, they have added "Abstinence" <note>Strict fasting diets</note> so that they might be healed by the Wood; for open sores and the "French flows" there has never been any [true] healing [by the wood alone]. But they have stitched one thing into the other so that they might establish something. So know herein that the correction sounds like nothing else than to ordain abstinence according to the person's condition, with the best food and drink, so that the inner nature is not more harshly corrupted by the "Abstinence Imposture."

Furthermore, know that its preparation with food and drink should be done in such a way that it happens in closed vessels, and with the drink like a wound-potion, in the manner I have described in a special booklet on the use of the Wood.

In every way, however, know that there are not as many virtues in it as people say, and much more is attributed to it and used for more than its virtues can reach. Thus, there is a distinction between what belongs to it and what does not; this is the greatest thing to know regarding the Wood, and to learn and experience this is the highest correction, as you will find in the [treatise on] the correction of the Wood.
