# Of the French Disease: The Second Book.

### CHAPTER XVIII.
->On the Correction of Diseases which they call the Penance of the Saints.<-

<note>The author refers to the common medieval belief that certain diseases, like St. Anthony's Fire or the "French Disease" (syphilis), were divine punishments or "penances" sent by specific saints.</note>

It is a harsh imposture <note>fraud or deception</note>, not only regarding medicine, but even more so on account of false, unfathomable superstition. For in the end, to claim that diseases come from a "Penance of the Saints" and to attribute illnesses to them cannot be found possible. It would imply that they [the Saints] are the cause of our pains, even though they are supposed to be for our benefit, since they regard us in love and not in malice. Although I can never oppose the idea of sorcerers or magicians—other than to say they are estimated to be capable of causing disease—the way in which that happens, that they create diseases, can be read in the book *On Superstitions* <note>original: "de Superstitionibus"</note>.

But at this point, so that the imposture may be corrected, know that natural diseases have been falsely attributed to the Saints by money-hungry, frivolous priests and their followers. They create an appearance as if the Saint does it, whereas it is actually superstition, or perhaps natural medicine that has been simply mixed in. Therefore, it is possible to do away with this imposture at this point, provided that this class of people, by whom it is thus falsified, is abolished. For they have so many priests and mockers, and have thereby so misled the common man, that he cannot escape the knavery; and even if he does get out, they lead him right back into it the next morning.

In these diseases, in which people imagine or believe themselves to be plagued by Saints, it is difficult to provide medicine. For their own judgment and conceived **imagination** <term>Imaginierung: the psychological state where a patient's belief in a curse physically worsens their condition</term> visibly poison the disease, and it changes to such an extent that no natural character or essence can be found in it anymore. Because of this, the flow, the location, the signs, and whatever should be naturally discovered therein are transformed. All of this is brought about by persuasion and great chatter, through which nature is entirely corrupted and poisoned. Therefore, so that such things do not happen, this whole profession must be laid aside, upon which not only disease, but also death (as often happens) and despair descend.

<margin>Imagination</margin> Finally, no one should expect that the Saints will be revealed in the way that the impostures of the [Papal] Legates claim. For the reason is this: such excellent imposture is not only among the Christians, but the Turks and all heathendom are quite full of it. They do not recognize our Saints, yet it happens through their idolatrous ways; likewise, an idolatrous faith is established by such impostors, through which these things occur. Now, their "medicine" is to satisfy the Saint's desire, and once that is done, the disease extinguishes itself, in that the patient then draws from another faith—believing he has honorably satisfied the Saint with courage and gifts. From this "easy faith," which takes hold of him a second time, health follows: and if he held no such belief, it would not happen to him. Thus, health follows according to how he binds and releases himself.

Regarding this, know that you should entirely uproot this imposture. No one is sick outside of nature who behaves toward Christ and his Apostles as they do toward these diseases—among whom there was no counting, brotherhoods, similar help, registration, annual interest, or other such softening with prayers, fasting, etc. Instead, they acted truly from the foundation. These [impostors] mislead people into a false model, acting according to what they ordain and boast of through their fantasy. If they would commit themselves to acting like the Apostles, they would correct themselves and not overburden the people with disease.

---

### CHAPTER XIX.
->On the Correction of the Apothecaries' Imposture.<-

It is no small imposture that grows in the apothecaries. For let everyone calculate for themselves that "shooters" and "wandering scholars" <note>original: "Schützen vnnd Bachanten," referring to uneducated, traveling vagabonds who took up trades</note> enter into it, and are raised therein like shooters and wandering scholars; they learn nothing else but how to splash and rumble about like a messy cook in his kitchen. When something comes into the mind of such an untimely beast, no one can talk him out of it: for they push forward like a Hungarian ox.

Now they seek to provide us with much "art," but little understanding. They believe themselves to be understanding enough. It follows that they already pass judgment, as if their persuasion were the whole of the art. Know then, that so much lies in the knowledge of diseases that truly all their art cannot make them physicians; all their collection of **prescriptions** <term>Recepten</term> is not even the beginning. Therefore, it is an excellent imposture that they undertake to manage the whole of medicine because of their art found in "cooking" [mixing drugs]; but anyone can see that pride and greed are what drive them.

Although over a long time they learn to recognize the **preparations of Berthold** <term>species Bertholdi</term>, and have been schoolmasters, **convent-leaders**, **procurators**, and have thus sat upon the nests of widows, they have thereby inherited the books, the names, and the jars. And because they know **"which case is long"** <note>original: "Cuius Casus Lognus" - a play on Latin grammar</note>, they also presume to know **"what gender is Aloe-wood"** <note>original: "Cuius generis Lignum Aloes"</note>, etc. Note all of you what a great imposture that is! Although they learn to know the preparations over a long time and travel to Venice—believing that is their new beginning—they consider themselves sufficient; and when they later fail, they must become physicians, though they are as full of art as a cow is of hay.

One must admit they know something, but it is with great terror and lack of understanding in medicine.

# On the Correction of Impostures

Medicine; for though the fish knows the water, he is not therefore a fisherman; the man who can drink wine and can harvest the grapes is not therefore a winemaker. So it is with other things as well, wherein each man is found, and he should not break out further than that in which he was raised.

CHAPTER XX.

->On the Correction of Lead Plasters.<-

<margin>B</margin>
<insert>A</insert>s to how the <term>imposture</term> <note>deception or fraudulent practice</note> of lead arose, know that the entire basis and intention was to seek a nature similar to that of quicksilver. Although it is, in the first part, a delight found by <term>mineral philosophers</term> <note>alchemists</note>: nevertheless, in medicine it is an imposture that may result in no small harm, and is good for nothing. The correction is needed in the error that they do not recognize the disease, and before other blockages and the like in such ways more. Now all this is not to be considered, but alone the nature of <term>Mercury</term> <note>quicksilver</note> is to be considered. That this <term>Mercury of Lead</term> is not to be regarded in the same way as <term>Common Mercury</term> <note>original: "Mercurius Vulgi"</note>, for Common Mercury is that which has its essence unbroken when it is transformed into metals; that same <term>Mercury</term> is capable of that. From this it follows that the diseases are of the nature of the metals. Not with lead bandages alone, but also silver, tin, copper, iron, and above them all; and therefore it is an <term>imposture</term> that they use lead bandages without understanding, not knowing how far it reaches or what it hits.
But a correction is to be undertaken therein in such a way: if the lead bandage is to proceed, it should be amalgamated with a twentieth part of <term>Common Mercury</term>. Subsequently, it should be given to the sickness, except for iron. Although it is true that more benefit is created by the broken <gloss>metal</gloss> than the whole. For what is white lead, what is minium <note>red lead</note>, other than lead? <margin>Plaster-20. *appears previously I. 662*</margin> From this it follows now, that the <term>Plaster of Minium</term> <note>original: "Emplastrum de Minio"</note> heals excellently, for it is the <term>Mercury of Saturn</term> <note>alchemical term for lead</note>. So also is the <term>Froth of Mercury</term> <note>original: "Spuma Mercurii"</note>; therefore, the use of lead bandages in this way is not poorly conceived, but devised by great philosophers. But it is poorly "impostured" <note>deceptively applied</note> that no further knowledge accompanies it. One should deal with such bandages who alone possesses the whole understanding of the <term>Nature of Mercury</term>. From this distinction follows how you should conduct yourself herein, which is excellent for every physician to know, as all recipes from <term>minerals are impostured</term>, and were also described as impostured by the ancients.

CHAPTER XXI.

->On the Correction of Wasting, etc.<-

<margin>Correction of the Chapters</margin>
<insert>I</insert>n the wasting of the limbs, know that every <term>imposture</term>, as with the roller bandages, should also be understood here. Except only in this reservation: that no breakout follows, but in the body in such measure as has been said of other blockages and displacements. Moreover, it causes curvature and paralysis of the limbs, likewise shrinking, swelling, hard glands <note>original: "Heerdrußen," likely referring to swollen lymph nodes or tumors</note>, <margin>Follows at Chapter 169.</margin> kidneys and bladder, and the like. Therefore the correction in this place is to take internally into the body what may stand from the "fluxes" <note>bodily fluids or discharges</note>, according to the appearance of the same, through that which alone has the power to turn this, and no other besides.
But if several of the aforementioned diseases should occur, such as <term>hernia</term>, <term>bubo</term> <note>swollen lymph node</note>, or other such <term>ulcerations</term>, know that they must be opened, and are in no way permanently driven away otherwise. And in the same way as that same open wound was healed, or should have been, in that same healing also treat these occurring diseases. For it is one origin, one matter, and one essence. It is the highest correction in this, that you prevent such things, first before the wasting of the limbs begins, as was indicated regarding blockages.

CHAPTER XXII.

->On the Correction of my Servants.<-

<insert>I</insert> have encountered many kinds of diseases in my days, and many things have happened with them: therefore, truly, I acted excellently according to the teaching of the ancient writers, and could obtain little from it. Subsequently, I was forced to adopt and measure and weigh various things here and there, according to how they lay before me. In such matters, I encountered many things of experience and experiments, so that I initially stood in error myself; which experiment the praise belongs to. Those who maintain themselves in medicine here and there have secretly snatched up things that I regarded as nothing, but they regarded as great: I recognized that it was nothing, but they did not. They subsequently used great <term>imposture</term> with inexperienced arts, and pointed at me, saying that everything with me was rejected.

They have often seen me heal excellent and difficult things, and because I have healed them, they have presumed it could happen in all things, which is a great and excellent <term>imposture</term> <note>A deception or fraudulent practice</note>. When they had seen three or four excellent trials, and the recipes, etc., had passed through their hands—diligently copied by them—they were then sent away by me. Although they are most highly learned and diligent in loud heavy-work, boasting, and in every way nothing but contempt.

Every element—as it pertains to nature—must have its <term>concordance</term> <note>A state of harmony or balance between the four elements within the body</note>. ->CHAPTER XIX.<-

B now note further the division of the book, in what way the practice and order shall be conducted. For it is openly apparent that they act with diligence toward status <note>original: "Anfleiß"</note> and not with true diligence <note>original: "Fleiß"</note>.

->CHAPTER XX.<-

H ere in this following practice you should also know that I mention certain diseases for which specific special remedies <note>original: "specialia Remedia"</note> are assigned, and some in general. This is caused by the fact that the style <note>original: "stillus"</note> dictates it so, and the diseases themselves demand it. For they produce processes and erratic symptoms <note>original: "Zufäll"</note>. At one time it is treated according to the nature of Mercury, at another according to constriction <note>original: "Contrictionis"</note>—that is, concerning those diseases that come from these—sometimes in general, as any mineral may give, whatever the cause may be most excellently. This will be described in *The Origin of New Diseases* <note>original: "Origine Morborum Novorum"</note>, which I have set down and ordered especially for the sake of these diseases, for those who compose and describe prescriptions anew. This is so that in the following time another may come and turn toward following new symptoms, or whatever may be left out and unknown, all of which must be undertaken solely from this theory. Therefore, I have specifically put them together to fulfill this deficiency in that same place.

->CHAPTER XXI.<-

### On the New Hectic Fever <note>original: "Ethica"</note>

C Hectic fever is a consumption of the body, with a decrease in the substance of the flesh and the like, accompanied by certain chills and heats. It takes its origin from the fact that nature, through the disease, has remained unhealed for too long a time; therefore, it follows for the body that it can never again put on weight, for the power to add substance has departed from it. Such long delays happen through the ignorance of physicians who undertake to heal and cannot complete it. Thus, time stretches out so that the strength decreases, and subsequently can never increase again.

### On the New Spitting Sickness.

I n every chilling of the body that occurs from the coldness of Mercury, or from the coldness of the <insert>decay of</insert> blood, so that in all its substance it becomes a discharge <note>original: "Roß"</note> that constantly presses to be cast out; and for that reason the body wastes away and also goes into consumption. For from the blood, the flesh is caused to flay; from great heat the limbs are numbed, so that just as from the cold, a discharged blood is born. Therefore, frost and sleeping heat, caused by the poison of the medicine, change the body from its natural course.

### On the New Dropsy.

S o as Mercury coagulates the substance of the body, much or little, so it also dissolves the same again in its departure, or through its nature. Then that which was coagulated flows downward in a watery flux and fills those places so that they swell, and they puff up with winds, all of which come from such corrupted medicine, be it mercury in smoke, water, or ointments, etc. There is also such a nature in wood that specifically promotes dropsy.

<summary>Paracelsus distinguishes between natural diseases and "new" diseases caused by toxic mineral treatments like mercury, criticizing ancient authorities and ignorant physicians for failing to recognize these chemical corruptions of the body. He defines new forms of consumption (Ethica) and dropsy (Wasserfucht) as direct results of the body's strength being depleted or its substances being unnaturally coagulated and dissolved by metallic poisons.</summary>

<header>Of the French Disease: The Third Book</header>

# Of the New Internal Ulcers.

<sig>A</sig>
The <term>New Ulcers</term> <note>original: "Newen Geschwer"</note> take their origin when the fluids—which by their nature should fall into the external limbs—are displaced and blocked; then they retreat inward, and what they should have produced in the outer limbs, they produce inside the body. From this it follows that the internal body cannot endure the effect as the external limbs can; for this reason, it leads to death, in the same manner and form as <term>Pleurisy</term> <note>an inflammation of the lungs</note> or an <term>Ulcer</term>.

## Of the Consumption of the Lungs.

As the nature of <term>Mercury</term> <note>original: "Mercurij"</note> is such that it expels through the mouth, it likewise searches through the regions of the lungs. And if it settles therein, just as it does in the mouth, it brings to the lungs all that it was meant to expel. And just as it causes <term>mouth-rot</term> <note>original: "Mundtseule"; likely mercurial stomatitis</note>, so it also causes <term>lung-rot</term>. Now, when the lung is overloaded with such rot and fluids, it cannot be helped as easily as the mouth. From this follows coughing, spitting, stinking breath, and the like; whatever pains the lung suffers, they all open up together.

## Of the New Hip-Sickness.

<sig>B</sig>
It also happens through too much loss of natural heat that the <term>Kidneys</term> fall into a <term>Sickness</term>, by the nature of <term>Mercury</term>, which is driven into the body beyond measure and without understanding. When this mercury seizes the <term>Anatomy</term> <note>here meaning the physical structure or essence</note> of the kidneys or the back, it causes eternal <term>loins-ache</term> around the belt, in the hips, and in the thickness of the flesh, with many accompanying ailments, especially if <term>Gravel</term> or <term>Stone</term> are present, or <term>constipation</term>, and the like.

## Of the New Stomach-Sickness.

It also happens that from such improper <term>Quicksilver</term> <note>mercury</note>, the stomach—once its <term>Anatomy</term> has received it—suffers from what is called the <term>Sobbing</term> <note>original: "Herschen"</note>, or <term>Singultus</term> <note>Latin: hiccups or convulsive sobbing</note>. For just as <term>Quicksilver</term> makes the hands tremble, so the <term>Sobbing</term> is the trembling of the stomach. Also, just as it is inclined toward <term>Vomiting</term>, so the <term>Mercury</term> binds and unites itself in the stomach and rules the stomach according to its own nature, so that it is not strong enough to digest food or drink, but must continually <term>Belch</term> <note>original: "Rosen"</note>, as is the nature of <term>Mercury</term>. Also, from taking too many <term>Purgatives</term>, the stomach takes on that same quality and remains as if it were purging every day.

## Of the New Dysentery or Flux.

<sig>C</sig>
So also is the <term>Medicine</term> seen in itself; from <term>Quicksilver</term> or other <term>Medicines</term>, if they have affected the <term>Anatomy</term> of the <term>Bowel Movement</term>, they melt down the whole body and drive it out through the stool, not by the power of natural expulsion, but by the <term>Malice</term> <note>original: "Boßheiten"; the toxic properties</note> that is in the <term>Medicine</term>. And if such a malicious poison turns acidic, it becomes a <term>Flux</term> without end.

## Of the New Stitches in the Side.

The poisonous <term>Medicines</term> used in the <term>French Sicknesses</term>, by their nature, if they are given without weight or measure and against their proper order, they immediately press toward the <term>Sobbing</term>, from which <term>Stitches in the Side</term> follow, and tightness around the <term>Chest</term>, depending on how much of that poison there is. And if it sticks and settles in the <term>Blood</term>, it passes along until it causes an internal <term>Ulceration</term> <note>original: "Viceration"</note>, just as it does externally in the limbs, which is death, and a <term>Sickness</term> unlike all old <term>Sicknesses</term>.

## Of the New Frenzy.

Such harsh poisons rise through the <term>Anatomy</term> of the <term>Brain</term> into the region of the <term>Brain</term>, and when they enter there, they bring their effect as in other places. And as the poison took hold elsewhere, so it does there. And since such a region has no specific opening for pain, when the <term>Aches</term> appear here in the <term>Brain</term> according to the nature of the <term>Brain</term>—be they many or few, <term>Raging</term>, <term>Dull</term>, or with many other such pains—depending on whether the poison turns acidic herein, the <term>Sickness</term> is permanent or not.
